readme: The "batteries included" extended library for Lean 4. This is a collection of data structures and tactics intended for use by both computer-science applications and mathematics applications of Lean 4.

items.statement:
theorem lexOrd_def [Ord α] [Ord β] :
    (lexOrd : Ord (α × β)).compare = compareLex (compareOn (·.1)) (compareOn (·.2))

items.name: Std.LawfulLTCmp
items.doc: `LawfulLTCmp cmp` asserts that `cmp x y = .lt` and `x < y` coincide.
items.statement:
class LawfulLTCmp [LT α] (cmp : α → α → Ordering) : Prop extends OrientedCmp cmp where
  /-- `cmp x y = .lt` holds iff `x < y` is true. -/
  eq_lt_iff_lt : cmp x y = .lt ↔ x < y

    cmp x y = .gt ↔ y < x

items.name: Std.LawfulLECmp
items.doc: `LawfulLECmp cmp` asserts that `(cmp x y).isLE` and `x ≤ y` coincide.
items.statement:
class LawfulLECmp [LE α] (cmp : α → α → Ordering) : Prop extends OrientedCmp cmp where
  /-- `cmp x y ≠ .gt` holds iff `x ≤ y` is true. -/
  isLE_iff_le : (cmp x y).isLE ↔ x ≤ y

items.name: Std.LawfulBCmp
items.doc:
`LawfulBCmp cmp` asserts that the `LE`, `LT`, `BEq` are all coherent with each other
and with `cmp`, describing a strict weak order (a linear order except for antisymmetry).
items.statement:
class LawfulBCmp [LE α] [LT α] [BEq α] (cmp : α → α → Ordering) : Prop extends
  TransCmp cmp, LawfulBEqCmp cmp, LawfulLTCmp cmp, LawfulLECmp cmp

items.name: Std.LawfulCmp
items.doc:

and with `cmp`, describing a linear order.
items.statement:
class LawfulCmp [LE α] [LT α] (cmp : α → α → Ordering) : Prop extends
  TransCmp cmp, LawfulEqCmp cmp, LawfulLTCmp cmp, LawfulLECmp cmp

modules.doc:
This is an opt-in mechanism for making machine-applicable `@[deprecated]` definitions. When enabled
(by setting the `machineApplicableDeprecated` tag attribute), a code action will be triggered
whenever the deprecation lint also fires, allowing the user to replace the usage of the deprecated
constant.

items.name: Batteries.CodeAction.matchExpand
items.doc:
Invoking tactic code action `Generate a list of alternatives for this match.` in the
following:
```lean
def myfun2 (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  match n
```
produces:
```lean
def myfun2 (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  match n with
  | 0 => _
  | n + 1 => _
```
Also has support for multiple discriminants, e.g.
```
def myfun3 (o : Option Bool) (m : Nat) : Nat :=
  match o, m with
```
can be expanded into
```
def myfun3 (o : Option Bool) (m : Nat) : Nat :=
  match o, m with
  | none, 0 => _
  | none, n_2 + 1 => _
  | some val_1, 0 => _
  | some val_1, n_2 + 1 => _
```
If it makes sense to use at least one of the constructors with `@` (i.e. iff it has an
implicit non-parameter argument) then we also show a codeaction that expands every such constructor
with implicit arguments filled in with the syntax `implicitArg := implicitArg`.
E.g. invoking `Generate a list of equations with implicit arguments for this match.` in
the following
```lean
inductive TermWithImplicit (F : Nat → Type u) (α : Type w)
  | var (x : α) : TermWithImplicit F α
  | func {l : Nat} (f : F l) (ts : Fin l → TermWithImplicit F α) : TermWithImplicit F α

def myfun4 (t : TermWithImplicit F α) : Nat := by
  match t with
```
produces
```lean
def myfun4 (t : TermWithImplicit F α) : Nat := by
  match t with
  | .var x => _
  | .func (l := l) f ts => _
```
where the implicit argument `{l : Nat}` is now usable.
Note that the arguments `F` and `α` are not filled since they are `parameters`
(a parameter is an argument to an inductive type that is fixed over constructors), i.e.
they are already determined by the match discriminant `t`. This means they don't provide any
new information for you.
items.statement: def matchExpand : CommandCodeAction

items.doc:
Hole code action used to fill in a structure's field when specifying an instance.

In the following:
```lean
instance : Monad Id := _
```

invoking the hole code action "Generate a (minimal) skeleton for the structure under construction."
produces:
```lean
instance : Monad Id where
  pure := _
  bind := _
```

and invoking "Generate a (maximal) skeleton for the structure under construction." produces:
```lean
instance : Monad Id where
  map := _
  mapConst := _
  pure := _
  seq := _
  seqLeft := _
  seqRight := _
  bind := _
```

following:

```lean

  | .bvar deBruijnIndex => _
  | .fvar fvarId => _

  | .lam binderName binderType body binderInfo => _
  | .forallE binderName binderType body binderInfo => _
  | .letE declName type value body nonDep => _
  | .lit _ => _
  | .mdata data expr => _
```

items.doc:
Invoking tactic code action "Generate an explicit pattern match for 'induction'" in the
following:
```lean
example (x : Nat) : x = x := by
  induction x
```
produces:
```lean
example (x : Nat) : x = x := by
  induction x with
  | zero => sorry
  | succ n ih => sorry
```

It also works for `cases`.


```
example : True ∧ True := by
  constructor
  · done
  · done
```

modules.title: Laws for Monads with Failure
modules.doc:
Definitions for monads that also have an `Alternative` instance while sharing the underlying
`Applicative` instance, and a class `LawfulAlternative` for types where the `failure` and `orElse`
operations behave in a natural way. More specifically they satisfy:

* `f <$> failure = failure`
* `failure <*> x = failure`
* `x <|> failure = x`
* `failure <|> y = y`
* `x <|> y <|> z = (x <|> y) <|> z`
* `f <$> (x <|> y) = (f <$> x <|> f <$> y)`

`Option`/`OptionT` are the most basic examples, but transformers like `StateT` also preserve
the lawfulness of this on the underlying monad.

The law `x *> failure = failure` is true for monads like `Option` and `List` that don't
have any "side effects" to execution, but not for something like `OptionT` on some monads,
so we don't include this condition.

We also define a class `LawfulAlternativeLift` similar to `LawfulMonadLift` that states that
a lifting between monads preserves `failure` and `orElse`.

## Tags

monad, alternative, failure

items.name: AlternativeMonad
items.doc:
`AlternativeMonad m` means that `m` has both a `Monad` and `Alternative` instance,
which both share the same underlying `Applicative` instance.
The main example is `Option`, but many monad transformers also preserve or add this structure.
items.statement: class AlternativeMonad (m : Type _ → Type _) extends Alternative m, Monad m

items.name: LawfulAlternative
items.doc:
`LawfulAlternative m` means that the `failure` operation on `m` behaves naturally
with respect to `map`, `seq`, and `orElse` operators.
items.statement:
class LawfulAlternative (m : Type _ → Type _) [Alternative m] : Prop
    extends LawfulApplicative m where
  /-- Mapping the result of a failure is still a failure -/
  map_failure (f : α → β) : f <$> (failure : m α) = failure
  /-- Sequencing a `failure` call results in failure -/
  failure_seq (x : m α) : (failure : m (α → β)) <*> x = failure
  /-- `failure` is a right identity for `orElse`. -/
  orElse_failure (x : m α) : (x <|> failure) = x
  /-- `failure` is a left identity for `orElse`. -/
  failure_orElse (y : m α) : (failure <|> y) = y
  /-- `orElse` is associative. -/
  orElse_assoc (x y z : m α) : (x <|> y <|> z) = ((x <|> y) <|> z)
  /-- `map` commutes with `orElse`. The stronger statement with `bind` generally isn't true -/
  map_orElse (x y : m α) (f : α → β) : f <$> (x <|> y) = (f <$> x <|> f <$> y)

items.name: mapConst_failure
items.statement:
theorem mapConst_failure [Alternative m] [LawfulAlternative m] (y : β) :
    Functor.mapConst y (failure : m α) = failure

items.name: mapConst_orElse
items.statement:
theorem mapConst_orElse [Alternative m] [LawfulAlternative m] (x x' : m α) (y : β) :
    Functor.mapConst y (x <|> x') = (Functor.mapConst y x <|> Functor.mapConst y x')

items.name: failure_seqLeft
items.statement:
theorem failure_seqLeft [Alternative m] [LawfulAlternative m] (x : m α) :
    (failure : m β) <* x = failure

items.name: failure_seqRight
items.statement:
theorem failure_seqRight [Alternative m] [LawfulAlternative m] (x : m α) :
    (failure : m β) *> x = failure

items.name: failure_bind
items.statement:
theorem failure_bind [AlternativeMonad m] [LawfulAlternative m] [LawfulMonad m]
    (x : α → m β) : failure >>= x = failure

items.name: seq_failure
items.statement:
theorem seq_failure [AlternativeMonad m] [LawfulAlternative m] [LawfulMonad m]
    (x : m (α → β)) : x <*> failure = x *> failure

items.name: LawfulAlternativeLift
items.doc: Type-class for monad lifts that preserve the `Alternative` operations.
items.statement:
class LawfulAlternativeLift (m : semiOutParam (Type u → Type v)) (n : Type u → Type w)
    [Alternative m] [Alternative n] [MonadLift m n] : Prop where
  /-- Lifting preserves `failure`. -/
  monadLift_failure : monadLift (failure : m α) = (failure : n α)
  /-- Lifting preserves `orElse`. -/
  monadLift_orElse (x y : m α) : monadLift (x <|> y) = (monadLift x <|> monadLift y : n α)

items.name: ForInStep.bind
items.doc:
This is similar to a monadic `bind` operator, except that the two type parameters have to be
the same, which prevents putting a monad instance on `ForInStepT m α := m (ForInStep α)`.
items.statement:
protected def ForInStep.bind [Monad m]
    (a : ForInStep α) (f : α → m (ForInStep α)) : m (ForInStep α)

items.name: ForInStep.bindM
items.statement:
protected abbrev ForInStep.bindM [Monad m]
    (a : m (ForInStep α)) (f : α → m (ForInStep α)) : m (ForInStep α)

items.name: ForInStep.run
items.doc:
Get the value out of a `ForInStep`.
This is usually done at the end of a `forIn` loop to scope the early exit to the loop body.
items.statement: def ForInStep.run : ForInStep α → α

items.name: ForInStep.bindList
items.doc: Applies function `f` to each element of a list to accumulate a `ForInStep` value.
items.statement:
def ForInStep.bindList [Monad m]
      (f : α → β → m (ForInStep β)) : List α → ForInStep β → m (ForInStep β)

items.name: ForInStep.bind_done
items.statement:
theorem ForInStep.bind_done [Monad m] (a : α) (f : α → m (ForInStep α)) :
    (ForInStep.done a).bind (m := m) f = pure (.done a)

items.name: ForInStep.bind_yield
items.statement:
theorem ForInStep.bind_yield [Monad m] (a : α) (f : α → m (ForInStep α)) :
    (ForInStep.yield a).bind (m := m) f = f a

items.name: ForInStep.run_done
items.statement: theorem ForInStep.run_done : (ForInStep.done a).run = a

items.name: ForInStep.run_yield
items.statement: theorem ForInStep.run_yield : (ForInStep.yield a).run = a

items.name: ForInStep.bindList_nil
items.statement:
theorem ForInStep.bindList_nil [Monad m] (f : α → β → m (ForInStep β))
    (s : ForInStep β) : s.bindList f [] = pure s

items.name: ForInStep.bindList_cons
items.statement:
theorem ForInStep.bindList_cons [Monad m]
    (f : α → β → m (ForInStep β)) (s : ForInStep β) (a l) :
    s.bindList f (a::l) = s.bind fun b => f a b >>= (·.bindList f l)

items.name: ForInStep.done_bindList
items.statement:
theorem ForInStep.done_bindList [Monad m]
    (f : α → β → m (ForInStep β)) (a l) :
    (ForInStep.done a).bindList f l = pure (.done a)

items.name: ForInStep.bind_yield_bindList
items.statement:
theorem ForInStep.bind_yield_bindList [Monad m]
    (f : α → β → m (ForInStep β)) (s : ForInStep β) (l) :
    (s.bind fun a => (yield a).bindList f l) = s.bindList f l

items.name: ForInStep.bind_bindList_assoc
items.statement:
theorem ForInStep.bind_bindList_assoc [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
    (f : β → m (ForInStep β)) (g : α → β → m (ForInStep β)) (s : ForInStep β) (l) :
    s.bind f >>= (·.bindList g l) = s.bind fun b => f b >>= (·.bindList g l)

items.name: ForInStep.bindList_cons'
items.statement:
theorem ForInStep.bindList_cons' [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
    (f : α → β → m (ForInStep β)) (s : ForInStep β) (a l) :
    s.bindList f (a::l) = s.bind (f a) >>= (·.bindList f l)

items.name: ForInStep.bindList_append
items.statement:
theorem ForInStep.bindList_append [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
    (f : α → β → m (ForInStep β)) (s : ForInStep β) (l₁ l₂) :
    s.bindList f (l₁ ++ l₂) = s.bindList f l₁ >>= (·.bindList f l₂)

modules.title: Laws for Monads with State
modules.doc:
This file defines a typeclass for `MonadStateOf` with compatible `get` and `set` operations.

Note that we use `MonadStateOf` over `MonadState` as the first induces the second,
but we phrase things using `MonadStateOf.set` and `MonadState.get` as those are the
versions that are available at the top level namespace.

items.name: monadStateOf_get_eq_get
items.doc: The namespaced `MonadStateOf.get` is equal to the `MonadState` provided `get`.
items.statement:
theorem monadStateOf_get_eq_get [MonadStateOf σ m] :
    (MonadStateOf.get : m σ) = get

items.name: monadStateOf_modifyGet_eq_modifyGet
items.doc: The namespaced `MonadStateOf.modifyGet` is equal to the `MonadState` provided `modifyGet`.
items.statement:
theorem monadStateOf_modifyGet_eq_modifyGet [MonadStateOf σ m]
    (f : σ → α × σ) : (MonadStateOf.modifyGet f : m α) = modifyGet f

items.name: liftM_get
items.statement:
theorem liftM_get {m n}  [MonadStateOf σ m] [MonadLift m n] :
    (liftM (get (m := m)) : n _) = get

items.name: liftM_set
items.statement:
theorem liftM_set {m n} [MonadStateOf σ m] [MonadLift m n]
    (s : σ) : (liftM (set (m := m) s) : n _) = set s

items.name: liftM_modify
items.statement:
theorem liftM_modify {m n} [MonadStateOf σ m] [MonadLift m n]
    (f : σ → σ) : (liftM (modify (m := m) f) : n _) = modify f

items.name: liftM_modifyGet
items.statement:
theorem liftM_modifyGet {m n} [MonadStateOf σ m] [MonadLift m n]
    (f : σ → α × σ) : (liftM (modifyGet (m := m) f) : n _) = modifyGet f

items.name: liftM_getModify
items.statement:
theorem liftM_getModify {m n} [MonadStateOf σ m] [MonadLift m n]
    (f : σ → σ) : (liftM (getModify (m := m) f) : n _) = getModify f

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf
items.doc:
Class for well behaved state monads, extending the base `MonadState` type.
Requires that `modifyGet` is equal to the same definition with only `get` and `set`,
that `get` is idempotent if the result isn't used, and that `get` after `set` returns
exactly the value that was previously `set`.
items.statement:
class LawfulMonadStateOf (σ : semiOutParam (Type _)) (m : Type _ → Type _)
    [Monad m] [MonadStateOf σ m] extends LawfulMonad m where
  /-- `modifyGet f` is equal to getting the state, modifying it, and returning a result. -/
  modifyGet_eq {α} (f : σ → α × σ) :
    modifyGet (m := m) f = do let z ← f <$> get; set z.2; return z.1
  /-- Discarding the result of `get` is the same as never getting the state. -/
  get_bind_const {α} (mx : m α) : (do let _ ← get; mx) = mx
  /-- Calling `get` twice is the same as just using the first retreived state value. -/
  get_bind_get_bind {α} (mx : σ → σ → m α) :
    (do let s ← get; let s' ← get; mx s s') = (do let s ← get; mx s s)
  /-- Setting the monad state to its current value has no effect. -/
  get_bind_set_bind {α} (mx : σ → PUnit → m α) :
    (do let s ← get; let u ← set s; mx s u) = (do let s ← get; mx s PUnit.unit)
  /-- Setting and then returning the monad state is the same as returning the set value. -/
  set_bind_get (s : σ) : (do set (m := m) s; get) = (do set s; return s)
  /-- Setting the monad twice is the same as just setting to the final state. -/
  set_bind_set (s s' : σ) : (do set (m := m) s; set s') = set s'

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.get_seqRight
items.statement: theorem get_seqRight (mx : m α) : get *> mx = mx

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.seqLeft_get
items.statement: theorem seqLeft_get (mx : m α) : mx <* get = mx

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.get_map_const
items.statement:
theorem get_map_const (x : α) :
    (fun _ => x) <$> get (m := m) = pure x

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.get_bind_get
items.statement: theorem get_bind_get : (do let _ ← get (m := m); get) = get

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.get_bind_set
items.statement:
theorem get_bind_set :
    (do let s ← get (m := m); set s) = return PUnit.unit

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.get_bind_map_set
items.statement:
theorem get_bind_map_set (f : σ → PUnit → α) :
    (do let s ← get (m := m); f s <$> set s) = (do return f (← get) PUnit.unit)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.set_bind_get_bind
items.statement:
theorem set_bind_get_bind (s : σ) (f : σ → m α) :
    (do set s; let s' ← get; f s') = (do set s; f s)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.set_bind_map_get
items.statement:
theorem set_bind_map_get (f : σ → α) (s : σ) :
    (do set (m := m) s; f <$> get) = (do set (m := m) s; pure (f s))

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.set_bind_set_bind
items.statement:
theorem set_bind_set_bind (s s' : σ) (mx : m α) :
    (do set s; set s'; mx) = (do set s'; mx)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.set_bind_map_set
items.statement:
theorem set_bind_map_set (s s' : σ) (f : PUnit → α) :
    (do set (m := m) s; f <$> set s') = (do f <$> set s')

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.modifyGetThe_eq
items.statement:
theorem modifyGetThe_eq (f : σ → α × σ) :
    modifyGetThe σ (m := m) f = do let z ← f <$> get; set z.2; return z.1 := modifyGet_eq f

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.modify_eq
items.statement:
theorem modify_eq (f : σ → σ) :
    modify (m := m) f = (do set (f (← get)))

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.modifyThe_eq
items.statement:
theorem modifyThe_eq (f : σ → σ) :
    modifyThe σ (m := m) f = (do set (f (← get)))

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.getModify_eq
items.statement:
theorem getModify_eq (f : σ → σ) :
    getModify (m := m) f = do let s ← get; set (f s); return s := by
  rw [getModify, modifyGet_eq, bind_map_left]

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.modifyGet_eq'
items.doc: Version of `modifyGet_eq` that preserves an call to `modify`.
items.statement:
theorem modifyGet_eq' (f : σ → α × σ) :
    modifyGet (m := m) f = do let s ← get; modify (Prod.snd ∘ f); return (f s).fst := by
  simp [modify_eq, modifyGet_eq]

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.modify_id
items.statement: theorem modify_id : modify (m := m) id = pure PUnit.unit

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.getModify_id
items.statement: theorem getModify_id : getModify (m := m) id = get

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.set_bind_modify
items.statement:
theorem set_bind_modify (s : σ) (f : σ → σ) :
    (do set (m := m) s; modify f) = set (f s)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.set_bind_modify_bind
items.statement:
theorem set_bind_modify_bind (s : σ) (f : σ → σ) (mx : PUnit → m α) :
    (do set s; let u ← modify f; mx u) = (do set (f s); mx PUnit.unit)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.set_bind_modifyGet
items.statement:
theorem set_bind_modifyGet (s : σ) (f : σ → α × σ) :
    (do set (m := m) s; modifyGet f) = (do set (f s).2; return (f s).1)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.set_bind_modifyGet_bind
items.statement:
theorem set_bind_modifyGet_bind (s : σ) (f : σ → α × σ) (mx : α → m β) :
    (do set s; let x ← modifyGet f; mx x) = (do set (f s).2; mx (f s).1)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.set_bind_getModify
items.statement:
theorem set_bind_getModify (s : σ) (f : σ → σ) :
    (do set (m := m) s; getModify f) = (do set (f s); return s)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.set_bind_getModify_bind
items.statement:
theorem set_bind_getModify_bind (s : σ) (f : σ → σ) (mx : σ → m α) :
    (do set s; let x ← getModify f; mx x) = (do set (f s); mx s)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.modify_bind_modify
items.statement:
theorem modify_bind_modify (f g : σ → σ) :
    (do modify (m := m) f; modify g) = modify (g ∘ f)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.modify_bind_modifyGet
items.statement:
theorem modify_bind_modifyGet (f : σ → σ) (g : σ → α × σ) :
    (do modify (m := m) f; modifyGet g) = modifyGet (g ∘ f)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.getModify_bind_modify
items.statement:
theorem getModify_bind_modify (f : σ → σ) (g : σ → σ → σ) :
    (do let s ← getModify (m := m) f; modify (g s)) =
      (do let s ← get; modify (g s ∘ f))

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.modify_comm_of_comp_comm
items.statement:
theorem modify_comm_of_comp_comm {f g : σ → σ} (h : f ∘ g = g ∘ f) :
    (do modify (m := m) f; modify g) = (do modify (m := m) g; modify f)

items.name: LawfulMonadStateOf.modify_bind_get
items.statement:
theorem modify_bind_get (f : σ → σ) :
    (do modify (m := m) f; get) = (do let s ← get; modify f; return (f s))

items.name: ReaderT.run_failure
items.statement:
theorem run_failure [Monad m] [Alternative m] (ctx : ρ) :
    (failure : ReaderT ρ m α).run ctx = failure

items.name: ReaderT.run_orElse
items.statement:
theorem run_orElse [Monad m] [Alternative m] (x y : ReaderT ρ m α) (ctx : ρ) :
    (x <|> y).run ctx = (x.run ctx <|> y.run ctx)

items.name: ReaderT.run_throw
items.statement:
theorem run_throw [MonadExceptOf ε m] (e : ε) (ctx : ρ) :
    (throw e : ReaderT ρ m α).run ctx = throw e

items.name: ReaderT.run_throwThe
items.statement:
theorem run_throwThe [MonadExceptOf ε m] (e : ε) (ctx : ρ) :
    (throwThe ε e : ReaderT ρ m α).run ctx = throwThe ε e

items.name: ReaderT.run_tryCatch
items.statement:
theorem run_tryCatch [MonadExceptOf ε m]
    (body : ReaderT ρ m α) (handler : ε → ReaderT ρ m α) (ctx : ρ) :
    (tryCatch body handler).run ctx = tryCatch (body.run ctx) (handler · |>.run ctx)

items.name: ReaderT.run_tryCatchThe
items.statement:
theorem run_tryCatchThe [MonadExceptOf ε m]
    (body : ReaderT ρ m α) (handler : ε → ReaderT ρ m α) (ctx : ρ) :
    (tryCatchThe ε body handler).run ctx = tryCatchThe ε (body.run ctx) (handler · |>.run ctx)

items.name: StateT.run_failure
items.statement:
theorem run_failure {α σ} [Monad m] [Alternative m] (s : σ) :
    (failure : StateT σ m α).run s = failure

items.name: StateT.run_orElse
items.statement:
theorem run_orElse {α σ} [Monad m] [Alternative m] (x y : StateT σ m α) (s : σ) :
    (x <|> y).run s = (x.run s <|> y.run s)

items.name: StateT.run_throw
items.statement:
theorem run_throw [Monad m] [MonadExceptOf ε m] (e : ε) (s : σ) :
    (throw e : StateT σ m α).run s = (do let a ← throw e; pure (a, s))

items.name: StateT.run_throwThe
items.statement:
theorem run_throwThe [Monad m] [MonadExceptOf ε m] (e : ε) (s : σ) :
    (throwThe ε e : StateT σ m α).run s = (do let a ← throwThe ε e; pure (a, s))

items.name: StateT.run_tryCatch
items.statement:
theorem run_tryCatch [Monad m] [MonadExceptOf ε m]
    (body : StateT σ m α) (handler : ε → StateT σ m α) (s : σ) :
    (tryCatch body handler).run s = tryCatch (body.run s) (handler · |>.run s)

items.name: StateT.run_tryCatchThe
items.statement:
theorem run_tryCatchThe [Monad m] [MonadExceptOf ε m]
    (body : StateT σ m α) (handler : ε → StateT σ m α) (s : σ) :
    (tryCatchThe ε body handler).run s = tryCatchThe ε (body.run s) (handler · |>.run s)

modules.title: A nondeterminism monad.
modules.doc:
We represent nondeterministic values in a type `α` as a single field structure containing an
`MLList m (σ × α)`, i.e. as a monadic lazy list of possible values,
each equipped with the backtrackable state
required to run further computations in the ambient monad.

We provide an `Alternative` `Monad` instance, as well as functions `bind`, `mapM`, and `filterMapM`,
and functions `singletonM`, `ofListM`, `ofOptionM`, and `firstM`
for entering and leaving the nondeterministic world.

Operations on the nondeterministic value via `bind`, `mapM`, and `filterMapM`
run with the appropriate backtrackable state, and are responsible for updating the state themselves
(typically this doesn't need to be done explicitly,
but just happens as a side effect in the monad `m`).

items.name: Nondet
items.doc:
`Nondet m α` is variation on `MLList m α` suitable for use with backtrackable monads `m`.

We think of `Nondet m α` as a nondeterministic value in `α`,
with the possible alternatives stored in a monadic lazy list.

Along with each `a : α` we store the backtrackable state, and ensure that monadic operations
on alternatives run with the appropriate state.

Operations on the nondeterministic value via `bind`, `mapM`, and `filterMapM`
run with the appropriate backtrackable state, and are responsible for updating the state themselves
(typically this doesn't need to be done explicitly,
but just happens as a side effect in the monad `m`).
items.statement:
structure Nondet (m : Type → Type) [MonadBacktrack σ m] (α : Type) : Type where
  /--
  Convert a non-deterministic value into a lazy list, keeping the backtrackable state.
  Be careful that monadic operations on the `MLList` will not respect this state!
  -/
  toMLList : MLList m (α × σ)

items.name: Nondet.nil
items.doc: The empty nondeterministic value.
items.statement: def nil : Nondet m α

items.name: Nondet.squash
items.doc: Squash a monadic nondeterministic value to a nondeterministic value.
items.statement: def squash (L : Unit → m (Nondet m α)) : Nondet m α

items.name: Nondet.bind
items.doc:
Bind a nondeterministic function over a nondeterministic value,
ensuring the function is run with the relevant backtrackable state at each value.
items.statement: partial def bind (L : Nondet m α) (f : α → Nondet m β) : Nondet m β

items.name: Nondet.singletonM
items.doc: Convert any value in the monad to the singleton nondeterministic value.
items.statement: def singletonM (x : m α) : Nondet m α

items.name: Nondet.singleton
items.doc: Convert a value to the singleton nondeterministic value.
items.statement: def singleton (x : α) : Nondet m α

items.name: Nondet.ofListM
items.doc:
Lift a list of monadic values to a nondeterministic value.
We ensure that each monadic value is evaluated with the same backtrackable state.
items.statement: def ofListM (L : List (m α)) : Nondet m α

items.name: Nondet.ofList
items.doc:
Lift a list of values to a nondeterministic value.
(The backtrackable state in each will be identical:
whatever the state was when we first read from the result.)
items.statement: def ofList (L : List α) : Nondet m α

items.name: Nondet.mapM
items.doc: Apply a function which returns values in the monad to every alternative of a `Nondet m α`.
items.statement: def mapM (f : α → m β) (L : Nondet m α) : Nondet m β

items.name: Nondet.map
items.doc: Apply a function to each alternative in a `Nondet m α` .
items.statement: def map (f : α → β) (L : Nondet m α) : Nondet m β

items.name: Nondet.ofOptionM
items.doc: Convert a monadic optional value to a nondeterministic value.
items.statement: def ofOptionM (x : m (Option α)) : Nondet m α

items.name: Nondet.ofOption
items.doc: Convert an optional value to a nondeterministic value.
items.statement: def ofOption (x : Option α) : Nondet m α

items.name: Nondet.filterMapM
items.doc: Filter and map a nondeterministic value using a monadic function which may return `none`.
items.statement: def filterMapM (f : α → m (Option β)) (L : Nondet m α) : Nondet m β

items.name: Nondet.filterMap
items.doc: Filter and map a nondeterministic value.
items.statement: def filterMap (f : α → Option β) (L : Nondet m α) : Nondet m β

items.name: Nondet.filterM
items.doc: Filter a nondeterministic value using a monadic predicate.
items.statement: def filterM (p : α → m (ULift Bool)) (L : Nondet m α) : Nondet m α

items.name: Nondet.filter
items.doc: Filter a nondeterministic value.
items.statement: def filter (p : α → Bool) (L : Nondet m α) : Nondet m α

items.name: Nondet.iterate
items.doc:
All iterations of a non-deterministic function on an initial value.

(That is, depth first search.)
items.statement: partial def iterate (f : α → Nondet m α) (a : α) : Nondet m α

theorem run_monadLift [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] [MonadLiftT n m] (x : n α) :

items.name: Array.scanlM
items.doc:
Folds a monadic function over an array from the left, accumulating the partial results starting with
`init`. The accumulated value is combined with the each element of the list in order, using `f`.

The optional parameters `start` and `stop` control the region of the array to be folded. Folding
proceeds from `start` (inclusive) to `stop` (exclusive), so no folding occurs unless `start < stop`.
By default, the entire array is folded.

Examples:
```lean example
example [Monad m] (f : α → β → m α) :
    Array.scanlM f x₀ #[a, b, c] = (do
      let x₁ ← f x₀ a
      let x₂ ← f x₁ b
      let x₃ ← f x₂ c
      pure #[x₀, x₁, x₂, x₃])
    := by simp [scanlM, scanlM.loop]
```

```lean example
example [Monad m] (f : α → β → m α) :
    Array.scanlM f x₀ #[a, b, c] (start := 1) (stop := 3) = (do
      let x₁ ← f x₀ b
      let x₂ ← f x₁ c
      pure #[x₀, x₁, x₂])
    := by simp [scanlM, scanlM.loop]
```
items.statement:
def scanlM [Monad m] (f : β → α → m β) (init : β) (as : Array α) (start := 0)
    (stop := as.size) : m (Array β)

items.name: Array.scanrM
items.doc:
Folds a monadic function over an array from the right, accumulating the partial results starting
with `init`. The accumulated value is combined with the each element of the list in order using `f`.

The optional parameters `start` and `stop` control the region of the array to be folded. Folding
proceeds from `start` (exclusive) to `stop` (inclusive), so no folding occurs unless `start > stop`.
By default, the entire array is folded.

Examples:
```lean example
example [Monad m] (f : α → β → m β) :
    Array.scanrM f x₀ #[a, b, c] = (do
      let x₁ ← f c x₀
      let x₂ ← f b x₁
      let x₃ ← f a x₂
      pure #[x₃, x₂, x₁, x₀])
    := by simp [scanrM, scanrM.loop]
```

```lean example
example [Monad m] (f : α → β → m β) :
    Array.scanrM f x₀ #[a, b, c] (start := 3) (stop := 1) = (do
      let x₁ ← f c x₀
      let x₂ ← f b x₁
      pure #[x₂, x₁, x₀])
    := by simp [scanrM, scanrM.loop]
```
items.statement:
def scanrM [Monad m]
    (f : α → β → m β) (init : β) (as : Array α) (start := as.size) (stop := 0) : m (Array β)

items.doc:

items.name: Array.merge
items.doc:
`O(|xs| + |ys|)`. Merge arrays `xs` and `ys`. If the arrays are sorted according to `lt`, then the
result is sorted as well. If two (or more) elements are equal according to `lt`, they are preserved.
items.statement: def merge (lt : α → α → Bool) (xs ys : Array α) : Array α

items.name: Array.mergeDedupWith
items.doc:
`O(|xs| + |ys|)`. Merge arrays `xs` and `ys`, which must be sorted according to `compare` and must
not contain duplicates. Equal elements are merged using `merge`. If `merge` respects the order
(i.e. for all `x`, `y`, `y'`, `z`, if `x < y < z` and `x < y' < z` then `x < merge y y' < z`)
then the resulting array is again sorted.
items.statement: def mergeDedupWith [ord : Ord α] (xs ys : Array α) (merge : α → α → α) : Array α

items.name: Array.mergeDedup
items.doc:
`O(|xs| + |ys|)`. Merge arrays `xs` and `ys`, which must be sorted according to `compare` and must
not contain duplicates. If an element appears in both `xs` and `ys`, only one copy is kept.
items.statement: def mergeDedup [ord : Ord α] (xs ys : Array α) : Array α

items.name: Array.mergeUnsortedDedup
items.doc:
`O(|xs| * |ys|)`. Merge `xs` and `ys`, which do not need to be sorted. Elements which occur in
both `xs` and `ys` are only added once. If `xs` and `ys` do not contain duplicates, then neither
does the result.
items.statement: def mergeUnsortedDedup [eq : BEq α] (xs ys : Array α) : Array α

items.name: Array.mergeAdjacentDups
items.doc:
`O(|xs|)`. Replace each run `[x₁, ⋯, xₙ]` of equal elements in `xs` with
`f ⋯ (f (f x₁ x₂) x₃) ⋯ xₙ`.
items.statement: def mergeAdjacentDups [eq : BEq α] (f : α → α → α) (xs : Array α) : Array α

items.name: Array.dedupSorted
items.doc:
`O(|xs|)`. Deduplicate a sorted array. The array must be sorted with to an order which agrees with
`==`, i.e. whenever `x == y` then `compare x y == .eq`.
items.statement: def dedupSorted [eq : BEq α] (xs : Array α) : Array α

items.name: Array.sortDedup
items.doc: `O(|xs| log |xs|)`. Sort and deduplicate an array.
items.statement: def sortDedup [ord : Ord α] (xs : Array α) : Array α

items.name: Array.Pairwise
items.doc:
`Pairwise R as` means that all the elements of the array `as` are `R`-related to all elements with
larger indices.

`Pairwise R #[1, 2, 3] ↔ R 1 2 ∧ R 1 3 ∧ R 2 3`

For example `as.Pairwise (· ≠ ·)` asserts that `as` has no duplicates, `as.Pairwise (· < ·)` asserts
that `as` is strictly sorted and `as.Pairwise (· ≤ ·)` asserts that `as` is weakly sorted.
items.statement: def Pairwise (R : α → α → Prop) (as : Array α) : Prop

items.name: Array.pairwise_iff_getElem
items.statement:
theorem pairwise_iff_getElem {as : Array α} : as.Pairwise R ↔
    ∀ (i j : Nat) (_ : i < as.size) (_ : j < as.size), i < j → R as[i] as[j]

items.name: Array.pairwise_empty
items.statement: theorem pairwise_empty : #[].Pairwise R

items.name: Array.pairwise_singleton
items.statement: theorem pairwise_singleton (R : α → α → Prop) (a) : #[a].Pairwise R

items.name: Array.pairwise_pair
items.statement: theorem pairwise_pair : #[a, b].Pairwise R ↔ R a b

items.name: Array.pairwise_append
items.statement:
theorem pairwise_append {as bs : Array α} :
    (as ++ bs).Pairwise R ↔ as.Pairwise R ∧ bs.Pairwise R ∧ (∀ x ∈ as, ∀ y ∈ bs, R x y)

items.name: Array.pairwise_push
items.statement:
theorem pairwise_push {as : Array α} :
    (as.push a).Pairwise R ↔ as.Pairwise R ∧ (∀ x ∈ as, R x a)

items.name: Array.pairwise_extract
items.statement:
theorem pairwise_extract {as : Array α} (h : as.Pairwise R) (start stop) :
    (as.extract start stop).Pairwise R

modules.title: Array
modules.doc: Prove basic results about `Array.scanl`, `Array.scanr`, `Array.scanlM` and `Array.scanrM`.

items.name: Array.scanlM.loop_toList
items.statement:
theorem scanlM.loop_toList [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
    {f : β → α → m β} {stop : Nat} (h : stop ≤ as.size) :
    Array.toList <$> scanlM.loop f init as start stop h acc =
      return acc.toList
               ++ (← as.toList.drop start
                  |>.take (stop - start)
                  |>.scanlM f init)

items.name: Array.scanlM_eq_scanlM_toList
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_eq_scanlM_toList [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → m β} {as : Array α} :
    as.scanlM f init = List.toArray <$> as.toList.scanlM f init

items.name: Array.toList_scanlM
items.statement:
theorem toList_scanlM [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → m β} {as : Array α} :
    toList <$> as.scanlM f init = as.toList.scanlM f init

items.name: Array.scanrM.loop_toList
items.statement:
theorem scanrM.loop_toList [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α → β → m β}
    {start : Nat} {h : start ≤ as.size} :
    Array.toList <$> scanrM.loop f init as start stop h acc =
      return (← as.toList.drop stop
                  |>.take (start - stop)
                  |>.scanrM f init)
                ++ acc.toList.reverse

items.name: Array.scanrM_eq_scanrM_toList
items.statement:
theorem scanrM_eq_scanrM_toList [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α → β → m β} {as : Array α} :
    as.scanrM f init = List.toArray <$> as.toList.scanrM f init

items.name: Array.toList_scanrM
items.statement:
theorem toList_scanrM [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α → β → m β} {as : Array α} :
    toList <$> as.scanrM f init = as.toList.scanrM f init

items.name: Array.scanlM_extract
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_extract [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → m β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.extract start stop).scanlM f init = as.scanlM f init start stop

items.name: Array.scanrM_extract
items.statement:
theorem scanrM_extract [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α → β → m β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.extract stop start).scanrM f init = as.scanrM f init start stop

items.name: Array.scanlM_empty
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_empty [Monad m] {f : β → α → m β} {start stop : Nat} :
    #[].scanlM f init start stop = pure #[init]

items.name: Array.scanrM_empty
items.statement:
theorem scanrM_empty [Monad m] {f : α → β → m β} {start stop : Nat} :
    #[].scanrM f init start stop = pure #[init]

items.name: Array.scanlM_reverse
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_reverse [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → m β} {as : Array α} :
    as.reverse.scanlM f init = Array.reverse <$> (as.scanrM (flip f) init)

items.name: Array.scanlM_pure
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_pure [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → β} {as : Array α} :
    as.scanlM (m := m) (pure <| f · ·) init = pure (as.scanl f init)

items.name: Array.scanrM_pure
items.statement:
theorem scanrM_pure [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α → β → β} {as : Array α} :
    as.scanrM (m := m) (pure <| f · ·) init = pure (as.scanr f init)

items.name: Array.idRun_scanlM
items.statement:
theorem idRun_scanlM {f : β → α → Id β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.scanlM f init).run = as.scanl (f · · |>.run) init

items.name: Array.idRun_scanrM
items.statement:
theorem idRun_scanrM {f : α → β → Id β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.scanrM f init).run = as.scanr (f · · |>.run) init

items.name: Array.scanlM_map
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_map [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α₁ → α₂ } {g: β → α₂ → m β} {as : Array α₁} :
    (as.map f).scanlM g init = as.scanlM (g · <| f ·) init

items.name: Array.scanrM_map
items.statement:
theorem scanrM_map [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α₁ → α₂ } {g: α₂ → β → m β} {as : Array α₁} :
    (as.map f).scanrM g init = as.scanrM (fun a b => g (f a) b) init

items.name: Array.scanl_eq_scanlM
items.doc: ### Array.scanl
items.statement:
theorem scanl_eq_scanlM {f : β → α → β} {as: Array α} :
    as.scanl f init = (as.scanlM (m := Id) (pure <| f · ·) init).run

items.name: Array.scanl_eq_scanl_toList
items.statement:
theorem scanl_eq_scanl_toList {f: β → α → β} {as : Array α} :
    as.scanl f init = (as.toList.scanl f init).toArray

items.name: Array.toList_scanl
items.statement:
theorem toList_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as: Array α} :
    (as.scanl f init).toList = as.toList.scanl f init

items.name: Array.size_scanl
items.statement:
theorem size_scanl {f : β → α → β} (init : β) (as : Array α) :
    size (scanl f init as) = as.size + 1

items.name: Array.scanl_empty
items.statement:
theorem scanl_empty {f : β → α → β} (init : β) :
    scanl f init #[] = #[init]

items.name: Array.scanl_singleton
items.statement:
theorem scanl_singleton {f : β → α → β} :
    scanl f init #[a] = #[init, f init a]

items.name: Array.scanl_ne_empty
items.statement: theorem scanl_ne_empty {f : β → α → β} : scanl f init as ≠ #[]

items.name: Array.scanl_eq_singleton_iff
items.statement:
theorem scanl_eq_singleton_iff {f : β → α → β} (c : β) :
    scanl f init as = #[c] ↔ c = init ∧ as = #[]

items.name: Array.getElem_scanl
items.statement:
theorem getElem_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as: Array α} (h : i < (as.scanl f init).size) :
    (as.scanl f init)[i]'h = foldl f init (as.take i)

items.name: Array.getElem?_scanl
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_scanl {f : β → α → β} :
    (scanl f a l)[i]? = if i ≤ l.size then some (foldl f a (l.take i)) else none

items.name: Array.take_scanl
items.statement:
theorem take_scanl {f : β → α → β} (init : β) (as : Array α) :
    (scanl f init as).take (i + 1) = scanl f init (as.take i)

items.name: Array.getElem?_scanl_zero
items.statement: theorem getElem?_scanl_zero {f : β → α → β} : (scanl f init as)[0]? = some init

items.name: Array.getElem_scanl_zero
items.statement: theorem getElem_scanl_zero {f : β → α → β} : (scanl f init as)[0] = init

items.name: Array.getElem?_succ_scanl
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_succ_scanl {f : β → α → β} :
    (scanl f init as)[i + 1]? = (scanl f init as)[i]?.bind fun x => as[i]?.map fun y => f x y

items.name: Array.getElem_succ_scanl
items.statement:
theorem getElem_succ_scanl {f : β → α → β} (h : i + 1 < (scanl f b as).size) :
    (as.scanl f b)[i + 1] = f (as.scanl f b)[i] (as[i]'(by grind))

items.name: Array.scanl_push
items.statement:
theorem scanl_push {f : β → α → β} {init: β} {a : α} {as : Array α} :
    (as.push a).scanl f init = (as.scanl f init).push (f (as.foldl f init) a)

items.name: Array.scanl_map
items.statement:
theorem scanl_map {f : γ → β → γ} {g : α → β} (init : γ) (as : Array α) :
    scanl f init (as.map g) = scanl (f · <| g ·) init as

items.name: Array.back_scanl
items.statement:
theorem back_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.scanl f init).back = as.foldl f init

items.name: Array.back?_scanl
items.statement:
theorem back?_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.scanl f init).back? = some (as.foldl f init)

items.name: Array.back_scanl?
items.statement: alias back_scanl?

items.name: Array.scanr_eq_scanrM
items.statement:
theorem scanr_eq_scanrM {f : α → β → β} {as : Array α} :
    as.scanr f init = (as.scanrM (m := Id) (pure <| f · ·) init).run

items.name: Array.scanr_eq_scanr_toList
items.statement:
theorem scanr_eq_scanr_toList {f : α → β → β} {as : Array α} :
    as.scanr f init = (as.toList.scanr f init).toArray

items.name: Array.toList_scanr
items.statement:
theorem toList_scanr {f : α → β → β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.scanr f init).toList = as.toList.scanr f init

items.name: Array.size_scanr
items.statement:
theorem size_scanr {f : α → β → β} (init : β) (as : Array α) :
    size (as.scanr f init) = as.size + 1

items.name: Array.scanr_empty
items.statement:
theorem scanr_empty {f : α → β → β} {init: β} :
    #[].scanr f init = #[init]

items.name: Array.scanr_ne_empty
items.statement:
theorem scanr_ne_empty {f : α → β → β} {as : Array α} :
    as.scanr f init ≠ #[]

items.name: Array.scanr_push
items.statement:
theorem scanr_push {f : α → β → β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.push a).scanr f init = (as.scanr f (f a init)).push init

items.name: Array.back_scanr
items.statement: theorem back_scanr {f : α → β → β} {as : Array α} : (as.scanr f init).back = init

items.name: Array.back?_scanr
items.statement:
theorem back?_scanr {f : α → β → β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.scanr f init).back? = some init

items.name: Array.getElem_scanr
items.statement:
theorem getElem_scanr {f : α → β → β} (h : i < (scanr f b l).size) :
    (scanr f b l)[i] = foldr f b (l.drop i)

items.name: Array.getElem?_scanr
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_scanr {f : α → β → β} :
    (scanr f b as)[i]? = if i < as.size + 1 then some (foldr f b (as.drop i)) else none

items.name: Array.getElem_scanr_zero
items.statement:
theorem getElem_scanr_zero {f : α → β → β} :
    (scanr f init as)[0] = as.foldr f init

items.name: Array.getElem?_scanr_zero
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_scanr_zero {f : α → β → β} :
    (scanr f init as)[0]? = some (as.foldr f init )

items.name: Array.scanr_map
items.statement:
theorem scanr_map {f : β → γ → γ} {g : α → β} (init : γ) (as : Array α) :
    scanr f init (as.map g) = scanr (fun x acc => f (g x) acc) init as

items.name: Array.scanl_reverse
items.statement:
theorem scanl_reverse {f : β → α → β} {as : Array α} :
    scanl f init as.reverse = reverse (scanr (flip f) init as)

items.name: Array.scanr_reverse
items.statement:
theorem scanr_reverse {f : α → β → β} {as : Array α} :
    scanr f init as.reverse = reverse (scanl (flip f) init as)

items.name: Array.scanl_extract
items.statement:
theorem scanl_extract {f : β → α → β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.extract start stop).scanl f init = as.scanl f init start stop

items.name: Array.scanr_extract
items.statement:
theorem scanr_extract {f : α → β → β} {as : Array α} :
    (as.extract stop start).scanr f init = as.scanr f init start stop

items.name: List.toArray_scanlM
items.statement:
theorem toArray_scanlM [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → m β} {as : List α} :
    toArray <$> as.scanlM f init = as.toArray.scanlM f init

items.name: List.toArray_scanrM
items.statement:
theorem toArray_scanrM [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α → β → m β} {as : List α} :
    toArray <$> as.scanrM f init = as.toArray.scanrM f init

items.name: List.toArray_scanl
items.statement:
theorem toArray_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : List α} :
    (as.scanl f init).toArray = as.toArray.scanl f init

items.name: List.toArray_scanr
items.statement:
theorem toArray_scanr {f : α → β → β} {as : List α} :
    (as.scanr f init).toArray = as.toArray.scanr f init

items.name: Subarray.scanlM_eq_scanlM_extract
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_eq_scanlM_extract [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → m β} {as : Subarray α} :
    as.scanlM f init = (as.array.extract as.start as.stop).scanlM f init

items.name: Subarray.scanrM_eq_scanrM_extract
items.statement:
theorem scanrM_eq_scanrM_extract [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α → β → m β} {as : Subarray α} :
    as.scanrM f init = (as.array.extract as.start as.stop).scanrM f init

items.name: Subarray.scanl_eq_scanl_extract
items.statement:
theorem scanl_eq_scanl_extract {f : β → α → β} {as : Subarray α} :
    as.scanl f init = (as.array.extract as.start as.stop).scanl f init

items.name: Subarray.scanr_eq_scanr_extract
items.statement:
theorem scanr_eq_scanr_extract {f : α → β → β} {as : Subarray α} :
    as.scanr f init = (as.array.extract as.start as.stop).scanr f init

modules.title: Association lists
modules.doc:
`AssocList α β` is a `List (α × β)` with the pair structure flattened into the list constructor.
This file defines the type and its operations; the lemmas relating those operations to the
corresponding `List` operations along `AssocList.toList` are in `Batteries.Data.AssocList.Lemmas`.

items.name: Batteries.AssocList
items.doc:
`AssocList α β` is "the same as" `List (α × β)`, but flattening the structure
leads to one fewer pointer indirection (in the current code generator).
It is mainly intended as a component of `HashMap`, but it can also be used as a plain
key-value map.
items.statement:
inductive AssocList (α : Type u) (β : Type v) where
  /-- An empty list -/
  | nil
  /-- Add a `key, value` pair to the list -/
  | cons (key : α) (value : β) (tail : AssocList α β)
  deriving Inhabited

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList
items.doc:
`O(n)`. Convert an `AssocList α β` into the equivalent `List (α × β)`.
This is used to give specifications for all the `AssocList` functions
in terms of corresponding list functions.
items.statement: def toList : AssocList α β → List (α × β)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.isEmpty
items.doc: `O(1)`. Is the list empty?
items.statement: def isEmpty : AssocList α β → Bool

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.length
items.doc: The number of entries in an `AssocList`.
items.statement: def length (L : AssocList α β) : Nat

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.foldlM
items.doc: `O(n)`. Fold a monadic function over the list, from head to tail.
items.statement: def foldlM [Monad m] (f : δ → α → β → m δ) : (init : δ) → AssocList α β → m δ

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.foldl
items.doc: `O(n)`. Fold a function over the list, from head to tail.
items.statement: def foldl (f : δ → α → β → δ) (init : δ) (as : AssocList α β) : δ

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.foldlM_eq
items.statement:
theorem foldlM_eq [Monad m] (f : δ → α → β → m δ) (init l) :
    foldlM f init l = l.toList.foldlM (fun d (a, b) => f d a b) init

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.foldl_eq
items.statement:
theorem foldl_eq (f : δ → α → β → δ) (init l) :
    foldl f init l = l.toList.foldl (fun d (a, b) => f d a b) init

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toListTR
items.doc: Optimized version of `toList`.
items.statement: def toListTR (as : AssocList α β) : List (α × β)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList_eq_toListTR
items.statement: theorem toList_eq_toListTR : @toList = @toListTR

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.forM
items.doc: `O(n)`. Run monadic function `f` on all elements in the list, from head to tail.
items.statement: def forM [Monad m] (f : α → β → m PUnit) : AssocList α β → m PUnit

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.mapKey
items.doc: `O(n)`. Map a function `f` over the keys of the list.
items.statement: def mapKey (f : α → δ) : AssocList α β → AssocList δ β

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.mapVal
items.doc: `O(n)`. Map a function `f` over the values of the list.
items.statement: def mapVal (f : α → β → δ) : AssocList α β → AssocList α δ

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.filterMapVal
items.doc: `O(n)`. Map a function `f` over the values of the list, dropping `none`.
items.statement: def filterMapVal (f : α → β → Option δ) : AssocList α β → AssocList α δ

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.findEntryP?
items.doc: `O(n)`. Returns the first entry in the list whose entry satisfies `p`.
items.statement: def findEntryP? (p : α → β → Bool) : AssocList α β → Option (α × β)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.findEntry?
items.doc: `O(n)`. Returns the first entry in the list whose key is equal to `a`.
items.statement: def findEntry? [BEq α] (a : α) (l : AssocList α β) : Option (α × β)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.find?
items.doc: `O(n)`. Returns the first value in the list whose key is equal to `a`.
items.statement: def find? [BEq α] (a : α) : AssocList α β → Option β

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.any
items.doc: `O(n)`. Returns true if any entry in the list satisfies `p`.
items.statement: def any (p : α → β → Bool) : AssocList α β → Bool

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.all
items.doc: `O(n)`. Returns true if every entry in the list satisfies `p`.
items.statement: def all (p : α → β → Bool) : AssocList α β → Bool

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.All
items.doc: Returns true if every entry in the list satisfies `p`.
items.statement: def All (p : α → β → Prop) (l : AssocList α β) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.contains
items.doc: `O(n)`. Returns true if there is an element in the list whose key is equal to `a`.
items.statement: def contains [BEq α] (a : α) (l : AssocList α β) : Bool

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.replace
items.doc:
`O(n)`. Replace the first entry in the list
with key equal to `a` to have key `a` and value `b`.
items.statement: def replace [BEq α] (a : α) (b : β) : AssocList α β → AssocList α β

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.eraseP
items.doc: `O(n)`. Remove the first entry in the list with key equal to `a`.
items.statement: def eraseP (p : α → β → Bool) : AssocList α β → AssocList α β

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.erase
items.doc: `O(n)`. Remove the first entry in the list with key equal to `a`.
items.statement: def erase [BEq α] (a : α) (l : AssocList α β) : AssocList α β

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.modify
items.doc:
`O(n)`. Replace the first entry `a', b` in the list
with key equal to `a` to have key `a` and value `f a' b`.
items.statement: def modify [BEq α] (a : α) (f : α → β → β) : AssocList α β → AssocList α β

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.forIn
items.doc: The implementation of `ForIn`, which enables `for (k, v) in aList do ...` notation.
items.statement:
protected def forIn [Monad m]
    (as : AssocList α β) (init : δ) (f : (α × β) → δ → m (ForInStep δ)) : m δ

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.pop?
items.doc: Split the list into head and tail, if possible.
items.statement: def pop? : AssocList α β → Option ((α × β) × AssocList α β)

items.name: List.toAssocList
items.doc: Converts a list into an `AssocList`. This is the inverse function to `AssocList.toList`.
items.statement: def _root_.List.toAssocList : List (α × β) → AssocList α β

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.beq
items.doc: Implementation of `==` on `AssocList`.
items.statement: protected def beq [BEq α] [BEq β] : AssocList α β → AssocList α β → Bool

modules.authors: Leonardo de Moura, Mario Carneiro, Yann Herklotz
modules.title: Lemmas about association lists
modules.doc:
Each operation on `AssocList` is specified by a lemma relating it to the corresponding
operation on `List (α × β)`, transported along `AssocList.toList`.

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.empty_eq
items.statement: theorem empty_eq : (∅ : AssocList α β) = nil

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.isEmpty_eq
items.statement: theorem isEmpty_eq (l : AssocList α β) : isEmpty l = l.toList.isEmpty

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.length_nil
items.statement: theorem length_nil : length (nil : AssocList α β) = 0

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.length_cons
items.statement: theorem length_cons : length (cons a b t) = length t + 1

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.length_toList
items.statement: theorem length_toList (l : AssocList α β) : l.toList.length = l.length

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.forM_eq
items.statement:
theorem forM_eq [Monad m] (f : α → β → m PUnit) (l) :
    forM f l = l.toList.forM (fun (a, b) => f a b)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList_mapKey
items.statement:
theorem toList_mapKey (f : α → δ) (l : AssocList α β) :
    (mapKey f l).toList = l.toList.map (fun (a, b) => (f a, b))

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.length_mapKey
items.statement: theorem length_mapKey : (mapKey f l).length = l.length

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList_mapVal
items.statement:
theorem toList_mapVal (f : α → β → δ) (l : AssocList α β) :
    (mapVal f l).toList = l.toList.map (fun (a, b) => (a, f a b))

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.length_mapVal
items.statement: theorem length_mapVal : (mapVal f l).length = l.length

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.filterMapVal_nil
items.statement: theorem filterMapVal_nil : filterMapVal f nil = nil

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.filterMapVal_cons
items.statement:
theorem filterMapVal_cons (f : α → β → Option γ) (k) (v) (t) :
    filterMapVal f (.cons k v t) =
      match f k v with
      | none => filterMapVal f t
      | some d => .cons k d (filterMapVal f t)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList_filterMapVal
items.statement:
theorem toList_filterMapVal (f : α → β → Option δ) (l : AssocList α β) :
    (filterMapVal f l).toList =
      l.toList.filterMap (fun (a, b) => (f a b).map fun v => (a, v))

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.length_filterMapVal_le
items.statement: theorem length_filterMapVal_le : (filterMapVal f l).length ≤ l.length

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.findEntryP?_eq
items.statement:
theorem findEntryP?_eq (p : α → β → Bool) (l : AssocList α β) :
    findEntryP? p l = l.toList.find? fun (a, b) => p a b

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.findEntry?_eq
items.statement:
theorem findEntry?_eq [BEq α] (a : α) (l : AssocList α β) :
    findEntry? a l = l.toList.find? (·.1 == a)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.find?_eq_findEntry?
items.statement:
theorem find?_eq_findEntry? [BEq α] (a : α) (l : AssocList α β) :
    find? a l = (l.findEntry? a).map (·.2)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.find?_eq
items.statement:
theorem find?_eq [BEq α] (a : α) (l : AssocList α β) :
    find? a l = (l.toList.find? (·.1 == a)).map (·.2)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.find?_mapVal
items.statement:
theorem find?_mapVal [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] (f : α → β → γ)
    (a : α) (l : AssocList α β) :
    (l.mapVal f).find? a = (l.find? a).map (f a)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.any_eq
items.statement:
theorem any_eq (p : α → β → Bool) (l : AssocList α β) :
    any p l = l.toList.any fun (a, b) => p a b

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.all_eq
items.statement:
theorem all_eq (p : α → β → Bool) (l : AssocList α β) :
    all p l = l.toList.all fun (a, b) => p a b

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.contains_eq
items.statement:
theorem contains_eq [BEq α] (a : α) (l : AssocList α β) :
    contains a l = l.toList.any (·.1 == a)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList_replace
items.statement:
theorem toList_replace [BEq α] (a : α) (b : β) (l : AssocList α β) :
    (replace a b l).toList =
    l.toList.replaceF (bif ·.1 == a then some (a, b) else none)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.length_replace
items.statement: theorem length_replace [BEq α] {a : α} : (replace a b l).length = l.length

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList_eraseP
items.statement:
theorem toList_eraseP (p) (l : AssocList α β) :
    (eraseP p l).toList = l.toList.eraseP fun (a, b) => p a b

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList_erase
items.statement:
theorem toList_erase [BEq α] (a : α) (l : AssocList α β) :
    (erase a l).toList = l.toList.eraseP (·.1 == a)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList_modify
items.statement:
theorem toList_modify [BEq α] (a : α) (l : AssocList α β) :
    (modify a f l).toList =
    l.toList.replaceF fun (k, v) => bif k == a then some (a, f k v) else none

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.length_modify
items.statement: theorem length_modify [BEq α] {a : α} : (modify a f l).length = l.length

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.forIn_eq
items.statement:
theorem forIn_eq [Monad m] (l : AssocList α β) (init : δ)
    (f : (α × β) → δ → m (ForInStep δ)) : forIn l init f = forIn l.toList init f

items.name: List.toList_toAssocList
items.statement: theorem _root_.List.toList_toAssocList (l : List (α × β)) : l.toAssocList.toList = l

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList_toAssocList
items.statement: theorem toList_toAssocList (l : AssocList α β) : l.toList.toAssocList = l

items.name: List.length_toAssocList
items.statement:
theorem _root_.List.length_toAssocList (l : List (α × β)) :
    l.toAssocList.length = l.length

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.beq_nil₂
items.statement: theorem beq_nil₂ [BEq α] [BEq β] : ((.nil : AssocList α β) == .nil) = true

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.beq_nil_cons
items.statement: theorem beq_nil_cons [BEq α] [BEq β] : ((.nil : AssocList α β) == .cons a b t) = false

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.beq_cons_nil
items.statement: theorem beq_cons_nil [BEq α] [BEq β] : ((.cons a b t : AssocList α β) == .nil) = false

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.beq_cons₂
items.statement:
theorem beq_cons₂ [BEq α] [BEq β] :
    ((.cons a b t : AssocList α β) == .cons a' b' t') = (a == a' && b == b' && t == t')

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.beq_eq
items.statement:
protected theorem beq_eq [BEq α] [BEq β] {l m : AssocList α β} :
    (l == m) = (l.toList == m.toList)

modules.authors: Mario Carneiro, François G. Dorais, Chad Sharp

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap
items.doc: A max-heap data structure.
items.statement:
structure BinaryHeap (α : Type w) [Ord α] where
  /-- `O(1)`. Get data array for a `BinaryHeap`. -/
  arr : Array α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.maxChild
items.doc: Given a node, return the index of its larger child, if it exists
items.statement: def maxChild [Ord α] (a : Vector α sz) (i : Fin sz) : Option (Fin sz)

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.maxChild_gt
items.doc: maxChild returns an index greater than i.
items.statement:
theorem maxChild_gt [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} {i : Fin sz} {j : Fin sz}
    (h : maxChild a i = some j) : i < j

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown
items.doc:
Core operation for binary heaps, expressed directly on arrays.
Given an array which is a max-heap, push item `i` down to restore the max-heap property.
items.statement:
def heapifyDown [Ord α] (a : Vector α sz) (i : Fin sz) :
    Vector α sz

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.mkHeap
items.doc:
Core operation for binary heaps, expressed directly on arrays.
Construct a heap from an unsorted array, by heapifying all the elements.
items.statement: def mkHeap [Ord α] (a : Vector α sz) : Vector α sz

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyUp
items.doc:
Core operation for binary heaps, expressed directly on arrays.
Given an array which is a max-heap, push item `i` up to restore the max-heap property.
items.statement:
def heapifyUp [Ord α] (a : Vector α sz) (i : Fin sz) :
    Vector α sz

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.empty
items.doc: `O(1)`. Build a new empty heap.
items.statement: def empty [Ord α] : BinaryHeap α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.mem_def
items.statement: theorem mem_def [Ord α] {x : α} {h : BinaryHeap α} : x ∈ h ↔ x ∈ h.arr

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.singleton
items.doc: `O(1)`. Build a one-element heap.
items.statement: def singleton [Ord α] (x : α) : BinaryHeap α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.size
items.doc: `O(1)`. Get the number of elements in a `BinaryHeap`.
items.statement: def size [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) : Nat

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.vector
items.doc: `O(1)`. Get data vector of a `BinaryHeap`.
items.statement: def vector [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) : Vector α heap.size

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.toArray_vector
items.statement: theorem toArray_vector [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) : heap.vector.toArray = heap.arr

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.mem_vector
items.statement: theorem mem_vector [Ord α] {heap : BinaryHeap α} : x ∈ heap.vector ↔ x ∈ heap.arr

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.get
items.doc: `O(1)`. Get an element in the heap by index.
items.statement: def get [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) (i : Fin heap.size) : α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.insert
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Insert an element into a `BinaryHeap`, preserving the max-heap property.
items.statement: def insert [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) (x : α) : BinaryHeap α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.size_insert
items.statement:
theorem size_insert [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) (x : α) :
    (heap.insert x).size = heap.size + 1

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.max
items.doc: `O(1)`. Get the maximum element in a `BinaryHeap`.
items.statement: def max [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) : Option α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.popMax
items.doc:
`O(log n)`. Remove the maximum element from a `BinaryHeap`.
Call `max` first to actually retrieve the maximum element.
items.statement: def popMax [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) : BinaryHeap α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.size_popMax
items.statement:
theorem size_popMax [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) :
    heap.popMax.size = heap.size - 1

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.extractMax
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Return and remove the maximum element from a `BinaryHeap`.
items.statement: def extractMax [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) : Option α × BinaryHeap α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.max_eq_none_iff
items.statement:
theorem max_eq_none_iff [Ord α] {heap : BinaryHeap α} :
    heap.max = none ↔ heap.size = 0

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.size_pos_of_max
items.statement:
theorem size_pos_of_max [Ord α] {heap : BinaryHeap α} (h : heap.max = some x) :
    0 < heap.size

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.insertExtractMax
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Equivalent to `extractMax (heap.insert x)`, except that extraction cannot fail.
items.statement: def insertExtractMax [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) (x : α) : α × BinaryHeap α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.replaceMax
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Equivalent to `(heap.max, heap.popMax.insert x)`.
items.statement: def replaceMax [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) (x : α) : Option α × BinaryHeap α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.decreaseKey
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Replace the value at index `i` by `x`. Assumes that `x ≤ heap.get i`.
items.statement: def decreaseKey [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) (i : Fin heap.size) (x : α) : BinaryHeap α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.increaseKey
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Replace the value at index `i` by `x`. Assumes that `heap.get i ≤ x`.
items.statement: def increaseKey [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) (i : Fin heap.size) (x : α) : BinaryHeap α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.toSortedArray
items.doc: `O(n log n)`. Return the contents of `heap` as an array sorted in descending order.
items.statement: def toSortedArray [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) : Array α

items.name: Vector.toBinaryHeap
items.doc: `O(n)`. Convert an unsorted vector to a `BinaryHeap`.
items.statement: def Vector.toBinaryHeap [Ord α] (v : Vector α n) : Batteries.BinaryHeap α

items.name: Array.toBinaryHeap
items.doc: `O(n)`. Convert an unsorted array to a `BinaryHeap`.
items.statement: def Array.toBinaryHeap [Ord α] (a : Array α) : Batteries.BinaryHeap α

items.name: Array.heapSort
items.doc: `O(n log n)`. Sort an array using a `BinaryHeap`.
items.statement: def Array.heapSort [instOrd : Ord α] (a : Array α) : Array α

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.maxChild_none_iff
items.doc: If maxChild returns none, there are no children in bounds.
items.statement:
theorem maxChild_none_iff [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} :
    maxChild a i = none ↔ sz ≤ 2 * i.val + 1

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.maxChild_some_iff
items.doc: maxChild returns some iff there is at least one child.
items.statement:
theorem maxChild_some_iff [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} :
    (maxChild a i).isSome ↔ 2 * i.val + 1 < sz

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.maxChild_isChild
items.doc: If maxChild returns some j, then j is a child of i.
items.statement:
theorem maxChild_isChild [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} (h : maxChild a i = some j) :
    j.val = 2 * i.val + 1 ∨ j.val = 2 * i.val + 2

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.maxChild_ge_left
items.statement:
theorem maxChild_ge_left [Ord α] [Std.OrientedOrd α] (a : Vector α sz) (i j : Fin sz)
    (hmc : maxChild a i = some j) (hleft : 2 * i.val + 1 < sz) :
    compare a[j] a[2 * i.val + 1] |>.isGE

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.maxChild_ge_right
items.statement:
theorem maxChild_ge_right [Ord α] [Std.OrientedOrd α] (a : Vector α sz)
    (i j : Fin sz) (hmc : maxChild a i = some j) (hright : 2 * i.val + 2 < sz) :
    compare a[↑j] a[2 * ↑i + 2] |>.isGE

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Children.of_swap_maxChild
items.doc: After swapping with maxChild, `a[j]` (now at position `i`) dominates both children.

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Children.of_ge_maxChild
items.doc: If parent >= maxChild, then WF.Children holds at that position.

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_eq_of_maxChild_none
items.doc: When maxChild returns none, heapifyDown is the identity.
items.statement:
theorem heapifyDown_eq_of_maxChild_none [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} (h : maxChild a i = none) :
    heapifyDown a i = a

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_eq_of_lt_child
items.doc:
When maxChild returns some and the parent is less than the child,
heapifyDown swaps and recurses.

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_eq_of_not_lt_child
items.doc: When maxChild returns some but parent is not less than child, heapifyDown is the identity.

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_getElem_of_not_inSubtree
items.doc: `heapifyDown` does not modify elements outside the subtree rooted at `i`.

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_getElem_of_not_inSubtree'
items.doc:
Variant of `heapifyDown_getElem_of_not_inSubtree` that takes a `Nat` index instead of `Fin`
Mostly for automation, simp/grind have a hard time doing this on their own

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_get_of_not_child
items.doc:
`heapifyDown` preserves WF.Children at positions before the heapified index that are not its
children.
items.statement:
theorem heapifyDown_get_of_not_child [Ord α] {v : Vector α sz}
    (hki : k < i) (hwf : WF.Children v k)
    (hleft_ne : i.val ≠ 2 * k.val + 1) (hright_ne : i.val ≠ 2 * k.val + 2) :
    WF.Children (heapifyDown v i) k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_swap_children_of_lt
items.doc: heapifyDown at j preserves WF.Children k when i < k < j and j is a child of i
items.statement:
theorem heapifyDown_swap_children_of_lt [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} {i j k : Fin sz}
    (hchild : j.val = 2 * i.val + 1 ∨ j.val = 2 * i.val + 2)
    (hik : i < k) (hkj : k < j) (hwf : WF.Children a k) :
    WF.Children (heapifyDown (a.swap i j i.isLt j.isLt) j) k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_preserves_ge_root_of_subtree
items.doc: If v dominates all values in the subtree, v dominates the result at root
items.statement:
theorem heapifyDown_preserves_ge_root_of_subtree [Ord α]
    {a : Vector α sz} (hge : ∀ k : Fin sz, InSubtree j.val k.val → (compare v a[k]).isGE) :
    (compare v (heapifyDown a j)[j]).isGE

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_children_of_ge_subtree
items.doc:
heapifyDown at j preserves WF.Children at k when j is a child of k,
k dominates everything in j's subtree, and WF.Children already holds at k
items.statement:
theorem heapifyDown_children_of_ge_subtree [Ord α]
    {b : Vector α sz} {j k : Fin sz}
    (hj_child : j.val = 2 * k.val + 1 ∨ j.val = 2 * k.val + 2)
    (hge_subtree : ∀ m : Fin sz, InSubtree j.val m.val → (compare b[k] b[m]).isGE)
    (hwf_k : WF.Children b k) :
    WF.Children (heapifyDown b j) k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_set_of_le_preserves_children
items.doc: heapifyDown at i preserves WF.Children at parent of i when value decreased

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_children_swap
Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_wf
items.doc:
`heapifyDown` restores the heap property at node `i` and below, given that all nodes
below `i` already satisfy `WF.Children`.

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyUp_bottomUp
items.doc:
heapifyUp fixes the heap when the only violation is at i
and i's children are already ≤ i's parent

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyUp_topDown
items.doc:
`heapifyUp` restores the full heap property, given that all nodes except `i` satisfy
the parent property and `i`'s children are ≤ `i`'s parent.
items.statement:
theorem heapifyUp_topDown [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α]
    {a : Vector α sz} (hexcept : WF.ExceptAt a i) (hchildren : WF.ParentGeChildren a i) :
    WF.TopDown (heapifyUp a i)

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyDown_perm
items.doc: `heapifyDown` is a permutation
items.statement: theorem heapifyDown_perm [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} : (heapifyDown a i).Perm a

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.heapifyUp_perm
items.doc: `heapifyUp` is a permutation
items.statement: theorem heapifyUp_perm [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} {i : Fin sz} : (heapifyUp a i).Perm a

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.popMax_perm
items.doc: popMax returns a permutation: the original is a perm of max :: popMax
items.statement:

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.max_eq_arr_zero
items.doc: When max returns some, the value equals arr[0].
items.statement:
theorem max_eq_arr_zero [Ord α] {heap : BinaryHeap α} (h : heap.max = some x) :

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.toSortedArray.loop_perm
items.doc: The inner loop of toSortedArray produces a permutation of heap ++ out

theorem toSortedArray.loop_perm [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) (out : Array α) :
    (toSortedArray.loop heap out).toList.Perm (heap.arr.toList ++ out.toList)

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.toSortedArray_perm
items.doc: `toSortedArray` produces a permutation of the heap.
items.statement:
public theorem toSortedArray_perm [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) :
    heap.toSortedArray.Perm heap.arr

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.mkHeap.loop_perm
items.statement:
theorem mkHeap.loop_perm [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} {h : n ≤ sz} :
    (mkHeap.loop n a h).Perm a

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.mkHeap.loop_wf
items.doc:
The inner loop of `mkHeap` establishes `WF.Children` for all nodes, given that
nodes at index ≥ n already satisfy the invariant.
items.statement:
theorem mkHeap.loop_wf [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α]
    {a : Vector α sz} {h : n ≤ sz} (hinv : ∀ k : Fin sz, n ≤ k.val → WF.Children a k) :

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.insertExtractMax_fst_of_lt
