items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Children
items.doc:
The primary local correctness property for the heap. A node should be >= both its children
(if it has them).
items.statement: def WF.Children [Ord α] (a : Vector α sz) (i : Fin sz) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown
items.doc: The vector underlying a `BinaryHeap` is well-formed iff every node is ≥ any children it has
items.statement: def WF.TopDown [Ord α] (v : Vector α sz) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF
items.doc: The well-formedness property of a binary heap
items.statement: def WF [Ord α] (heap : BinaryHeap α) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Children.congr
items.doc:
`WF.Children` depends only on the values at position `k` and its two children.
If those values agree between two vectors, `WF.Children` transfers.
items.statement:
theorem WF.Children.congr [Ord α] {a b : Vector α sz} {k : Fin sz}
    (hwf : WF.Children a k)
    (hk : b[k] = a[k])
    (hl : ∀ _ : 2 * k.val + 1 < sz, b[2 * k.val + 1] = a[2 * k.val + 1])
    (hr : ∀ _ : 2 * k.val + 2 < sz, b[2 * k.val + 2] = a[2 * k.val + 2]) :
    WF.Children b k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.InSubtree
items.doc: Index `k` lies in the subtree rooted at index `root` in the implicit binary heap tree.
items.statement:
inductive InSubtree (root : Nat) : Nat → Prop
  | refl : InSubtree root root
  | left : InSubtree root k → InSubtree root (2 * k + 1)
  | right : InSubtree root k → InSubtree root (2 * k + 2)

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.InSubtree.le
items.statement: theorem le (ins : InSubtree j k) : j ≤ k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.InSubtree.not_of_lt
items.statement: theorem not_of_lt (hlt : k < j) : ¬InSubtree j k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.InSubtree.lt_of_ne
items.statement: theorem lt_of_ne (hsub : InSubtree j k) (hne : j ≠ k) : j < k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.InSubtree.trans
items.statement: theorem trans (hij : InSubtree i j) (hjk : InSubtree j k) : InSubtree i k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.InSubtree.ne_of_lt
items.statement: theorem ne_of_lt (h: i < j) (hins : InSubtree j k) : k ≠ i

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.InSubtree.mem_of_zero
items.doc: Every index is a member of the subtree rooted at 0.
items.statement: theorem mem_of_zero (a : Nat) : InSubtree 0 a

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.InSubtree.of_child
items.doc: A child index is in the subtree of its parent.
items.statement: theorem of_child (h : j = 2 * i + 1 ∨ j = 2 * i + 2) : InSubtree i j

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Below
items.doc:
All nodes at indices greater than `i` are well-formed (according to `WF.Children`)
Used when verifying `heapifyDown`
items.statement: def Below [Ord α] (a : Vector α sz) (i : Nat) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Below.of_le
items.doc: WF.Below is monotone: larger threshold means weaker condition.
items.statement:
theorem Below.of_le {a : Vector α sz} [Ord α]
    (hij : i ≤ j) (hbelow : WF.Below a i) : WF.Below a j

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Below.swap
items.doc:
if i < j, and the heap is well formed below i, then a[i] and a[j] can be swapped
and the heap will still be well-formed below j -
items.statement:
theorem Below.swap [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} {i j : Fin sz} (hbelow : WF.Below a i)
    (hij : i < j) : WF.Below (a.swap i j i.isLt j.isLt) j

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Children.set_of_ne
items.doc: For k ≠ i where neither child of k equals i, set at i preserves `WF.Children` at k
items.statement:
theorem Children.set_of_ne [Ord α] {v : Vector α sz} {i k : Fin sz}
    (hwf : WF.Children v k) (hki : i.val ≠ k.val)
    (hleft_ne : i.val ≠ 2 * k.val + 1) (hright_ne : i.val ≠ 2 * k.val + 2) :
    WF.Children (v.set i x i.isLt) k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Children.set_of_ge_child
items.doc: Setting a child to a smaller value preserves WF.Children at the parent
items.statement:
theorem Children.set_of_ge_child [Ord α] {v : Vector α sz} {k i : Fin sz}
    (hwf : WF.Children v k) (h_child : i.val = 2 * k.val + 1 ∨ i.val = 2 * k.val + 2)
    (h_ge : compare v[k] x |>.isGE) :
    WF.Children (v.set i x i.isLt) k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown.below_of_set
items.doc: Setting a smaller value preserves WF.Below
items.statement:
theorem TopDown.below_of_set [Ord α] {v : Vector α sz} {i : Fin sz} (htd : WF.TopDown v) :
    WF.Below (v.set i x i.isLt) i

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown.empty
items.doc: An empty vector is trivially well-formed (no nodes to violate the heap property).
items.statement: theorem TopDown.empty [Ord α] : WF.TopDown (#v[] : Vector α 0)

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown.singleton
items.doc: A single-element vector is trivially well-formed (no children to compare with).
items.statement: theorem TopDown.singleton [Ord α] {x : α} : WF.TopDown #v[x]

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown.of_root_and_below
items.doc: `WF.TopDown` follows from `WF.Children` at 0 and `WF.Below` at 0
items.statement:
theorem TopDown.of_root_and_below [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} {h0 : 0 < sz} :
   WF.Children a ⟨0, h0⟩ ∧  WF.Below a 0 → WF.TopDown a

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown.children_and_below
items.statement:
theorem TopDown.children_and_below [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} (htd : WF.TopDown a) (i : Fin sz) :
    WF.Children a i ∧ WF.Below a i

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.parent_ge_subtree
items.doc: A node dominates all descendants in its subtree in a well-formed heap.
items.statement:
theorem parent_ge_subtree [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α]
    {a : Vector α sz} {hk : k < sz} {hj : j < sz} (hwf_at : WF.Children a ⟨j, hj⟩)
    (hwf_below : WF.Below a j) (hsub : InSubtree j k) :
    (compare a[j] a[k]).isGE

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.ge_subtree_of_modify
items.doc:
If v dominates the new value at j, v dominated the original value at j,
the original array was well-formed at and below j, and b agrees with a outside position j,
then v dominates everything in b's subtree at j.
items.statement:
theorem ge_subtree_of_modify [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α] {a b : Vector α sz} {j : Fin sz}
    (hge : compare v a[j] |>.isGE) (hwf_at : WF.Children a j)
    (hwf_below : WF.Below a j) (hge_new : compare v b[j] |>.isGE)
    (hunchanged : ∀ k : Fin sz, InSubtree j.val k.val → j.val ≠ k.val → b[k] = a[k]) :
    ∀ m : Fin sz, InSubtree j.val m.val → (compare v b[m]).isGE

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown.parent_ge_subtree_of_set
items.doc: Parent dominates all descendants after setting a smaller value
items.statement:
theorem TopDown.parent_ge_subtree_of_set [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α] {v : Vector α sz} {i : Fin sz}
    (htd : WF.TopDown v) (h_le : compare v[i] x |>.isGE) (hi : 0 < i.val)
    (m : Fin sz) (hsub : InSubtree i.val m.val) :
    (compare v[(i.val - 1) / 2] (v.set i x i.isLt)[m]).isGE

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.swap_preserves_ge_subtree
items.doc: a[j] dominates everything in (a.swap i j)'s subtree at j when i < j and a[i] < a[j]
items.statement:
theorem swap_preserves_ge_subtree [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α]
    {a : Vector α sz} {i j k : Fin sz} (h_ij : i < j) (h_ge : (compare a[j] a[i]).isGE)
    (hbelow : WF.Below a i) (hsub : InSubtree j k) :
    (compare a[j] (a.swap i j i.isLt j.isLt)[k]).isGE

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown.root_ge_all
items.doc: The root element is greater than or equal to all heap elements.
items.statement:
theorem TopDown.root_ge_all [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α]
    {a : Vector α sz} (hwf : WF.TopDown a) (hne : 0 < sz) (k : Fin sz) :
    (compare a[0] a[k]).isGE

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Parent
items.doc:
"Dual" correctness property to `WF.Children`. A parent should be >= current node.
Used when verifying heapifyUp
items.statement: def Parent [Ord α] (a : Vector α sz) (i : Fin sz) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.ParentGeChildren
items.doc:
The parent of node `i` is >= node `i`'s children
Part of the invariant required/maintained by heapifyUp
items.statement: def ParentGeChildren [Ord α] (a: Vector α sz) (i : Fin sz) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.ExceptAt
items.doc:
Every other node (except possibly i) is <= its parent (if it has one)
Part of the invariant required/maintained by heapifyUp
items.statement: def ExceptAt [Ord α] (a : Vector α sz) (i : Fin sz) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.ExceptAt.swap_parent
items.doc: If `ExceptAt` i and `ParentGeChildren` i, swap preserves `ExceptAt` at parent
items.statement:
theorem ExceptAt.swap_parent [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α]
    {a : Vector α sz} {i : Fin sz} (h_ge : compare a[i] a[(i.val - 1) / 2] |>.isGE)
    (hexcept : ExceptAt a i) (hchildren : ParentGeChildren a i) :
    ExceptAt (a.swap i ((i.val - 1) / 2) i.isLt (by omega)) ⟨(i.val - 1) / 2, by omega⟩

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.ParentGeChildren.swap_parent
items.doc: If `ExceptAt` a i, swap preserves `ParentGeChildren` at parent
items.statement:
theorem ParentGeChildren.swap_parent [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α] {a : Vector α sz}
    {i : Fin sz} (h_ge : compare a[i] a[(i.val - 1)/2] |>.isGE) (hexcept : ExceptAt a i) :
    ParentGeChildren
      (a.swap i ((i.val - 1) / 2) i.isLt (by omega)) ⟨(i.val - 1) / 2, by omega⟩

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.BottomUp
items.doc:
Dual global correctness property to `WF`. The vector underlying a BinaryHeap is well-formed
iff all nodes are ≤ their parent.
Used when verifying heapifyUp.
items.statement: def BottomUp [Ord α] (v : Vector α sz) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown.iff_bottomUp
items.doc: `WF.TopDown` and `WF.BottomUp` are equivalent.
items.statement:
theorem TopDown.iff_bottomUp [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} :
    WF.TopDown a ↔ WF.BottomUp a

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.BottomUp.of_exceptAt_root
items.doc: If exception is at 0, then `BottomUp` holds
items.statement:
theorem BottomUp.of_exceptAt_root [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} (h : 0 < sz)
    (hexcept : ExceptAt a ⟨0, h⟩) :
    WF.BottomUp a

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.BottomUp.of_parent_and_exceptAt
items.doc: If both the parent property and `ExceptAt` property hold at i, then the heap is `BottomUp`.

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.of_topDown
items.doc:
A well-formed vector transfers its well-formedness to a BinaryHeap created from its array
representation.
items.statement: theorem of_topDown {v : Vector α sz} [Ord α] (h_td : WF.TopDown v) : WF ⟨v.toArray⟩

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.ExceptAt.set_of_ge
items.doc: Setting a larger value preserves `ExceptAt`
items.statement:
theorem ExceptAt.set_of_ge [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α]
    {v : Vector α sz} {i : Fin sz} (hbu : WF.BottomUp v) (h_ge : compare x v[i] |>.isGE) :
    ExceptAt (v.set i x i.isLt) i

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.ParentGeChildren.set_of_ge
items.doc: Setting a larger value preserves `ParentGeChildren` when original heap is well-formed
items.statement:
theorem ParentGeChildren.set_of_ge [Ord α] [Std.TransOrd α]
    {v : Vector α sz} {i : Fin sz} (hbu : WF.BottomUp v) (h_ge : compare x v[i] |>.isGE) :
    ParentGeChildren (v.set i x i.isLt) i

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown.below_of_swap_pop
items.doc:
Swapping the root with the last element and then popping maintains the Below invariant at the
root for heapifyDown.
items.statement:
theorem TopDown.below_of_swap_pop [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} (hwf : WF.TopDown a) (h0 : 0 < sz) :
    WF.Below (a.swap 0 (sz - 1) h0 (by omega) |>.pop) 0

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.children_split
items.doc:
Prove WF.Children for all k ≥ lo by splitting at pivot i:
k > i from hbelow, k = i from hchildren, k ∈ [lo, i) from hrange
items.statement:
theorem children_split [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} {lo : Nat} {i : Fin sz}
    (hchildren_i : WF.Children a i)
    (hbelow_i : WF.Below a i)
    (hrange : ∀ k : Fin sz, lo ≤ k.val → k.val < i.val → WF.Children a k) :
    ∀ {k : Fin sz}, lo ≤ k.val → WF.Children a k

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.TopDown.of_children_below_and_above
items.doc: Build WF.TopDown from WF.Children at i, WF.Below at i, and a proof for positions < i
items.statement:
theorem TopDown.of_children_below_and_above [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} {i : Fin sz}
    (hchildren_i : WF.Children a i)
    (hbelow_i : WF.Below a i)
    (habove : ∀ k : Fin sz, k.val < i.val → WF.Children a k) :
    WF.TopDown a

items.name: Batteries.BinaryHeap.WF.Below.of_children_below_and_between
items.doc: Build WF.Below at i from WF.Children at j, WF.Below at j, and a proof for positions between
items.statement:
theorem Below.of_children_below_and_between [Ord α] {a : Vector α sz} {i j : Fin sz}
    (hchildren_j : WF.Children a j)
    (hbelow_j : WF.Below a j)
    (hbetween : ∀ k : Fin sz, i.val < k.val → k.val < j.val → WF.Children a k) :
    WF.Below a i

modules.authors: Leonardo de Moura, Jannis Limperg, Mario Carneiro

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode
items.doc:
A `HeapNode` is one of the internal nodes of the binomial heap.
It is always a perfect binary tree, with the depth of the tree stored in the `Heap`.
However the interpretation of the two pointers is different: we view the `child`
as going to the first child of this node, and `sibling` goes to the next sibling
of this tree. So it actually encodes a forest where each node has children
`node.child`, `node.child.sibling`, `node.child.sibling.sibling`, etc.

Each edge in this forest denotes a `le a b` relation that has been checked, so
the root is smaller than everything else under it.
items.statement:
inductive HeapNode (α : Type u) where
  /-- An empty forest, which has depth `0`. -/
  | nil : HeapNode α
  /-- A forest of rank `r + 1` consists of a root `a`,
  a forest `child` of rank `r` elements greater than `a`,
  and another forest `sibling` of rank `r`. -/
  | node (a : α) (child sibling : HeapNode α) : HeapNode α
  deriving Repr

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.realSize
items.doc:
The "real size" of the node, counting up how many values of type `α` are stored.
This is `O(n)` and is intended mainly for specification purposes.
For a well formed `HeapNode` the size is always `2^n - 1` where `n` is the depth.
items.statement: def HeapNode.realSize : HeapNode α → Nat

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.singleton
items.doc: A node containing a single element `a`.
items.statement: def HeapNode.singleton (a : α) : HeapNode α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.rank
items.doc:
`O(log n)`. The rank, or the number of trees in the forest.
It is also the depth of the forest.
items.statement: def HeapNode.rank : HeapNode α → Nat

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.rankTR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `HeapNode.rank`.
items.statement: def HeapNode.rankTR (s : HeapNode α) : Nat

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.rankTR_eq
items.statement: theorem HeapNode.rankTR_eq : @rankTR = @rank

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap
items.doc:
A `Heap` is the top level structure in a binomial heap.
It consists of a forest of `HeapNode`s with strictly increasing ranks.
items.statement:
inductive Heap (α : Type u) where
  /-- An empty heap. -/
  | nil : Heap α
  /-- A cons node contains a tree of root `val`, children `node` and rank `rank`,
  and then `next` which is the rest of the forest. -/
  | cons (rank : Nat) (val : α) (node : HeapNode α) (next : Heap α) : Heap α
  deriving Repr

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.realSize
items.doc:
`O(n)`. The "real size" of the heap, counting up how many values of type `α` are stored.
This is intended mainly for specification purposes.
Prefer `Heap.size`, which is the same for well formed heaps.
items.statement: def Heap.realSize : Heap α → Nat

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.size
items.doc: `O(log n)`. The number of elements in the heap.
items.statement: def Heap.size : Heap α → Nat

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.isEmpty
items.doc: `O(1)`. Is the heap empty?
items.statement: def Heap.isEmpty : Heap α → Bool

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.singleton
items.doc: `O(1)`. The heap containing a single value `a`.
items.statement: def Heap.singleton (a : α) : Heap α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.rankGT
items.doc: `O(1)`. Auxiliary for `Heap.merge`: Is the minimum rank in `Heap` strictly larger than `n`?
items.statement: def Heap.rankGT : Heap α → Nat → Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.length
items.doc: `O(log n)`. The number of trees in the forest.
items.statement: def Heap.length : Heap α → Nat

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.combine
items.doc:
`O(1)`. Auxiliary for `Heap.merge`: combines two heap nodes of the same rank
into one with the next larger rank.
items.statement: def combine (le : α → α → Bool) (a₁ a₂ : α) (n₁ n₂ : HeapNode α) : α × HeapNode α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.merge
items.doc:
Merge two forests of binomial trees. The forests are assumed to be ordered
by rank and `merge` maintains this invariant.
items.statement: def Heap.merge (le : α → α → Bool) : Heap α → Heap α → Heap α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.toHeap
items.doc:
`O(log n)`. Convert a `HeapNode` to a `Heap` by reversing the order of the nodes
along the `sibling` spine.
items.statement: def HeapNode.toHeap (s : HeapNode α) : Heap α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.headD
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Get the smallest element in the heap, including the passed in value `a`.
items.statement: def Heap.headD (le : α → α → Bool) (a : α) : Heap α → α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.head?
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Get the smallest element in the heap, if it has an element.
items.statement: def Heap.head? (le : α → α → Bool) : Heap α → Option α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.FindMin
items.doc:
The return type of `FindMin`, which encodes various quantities needed to
reconstruct the tree in `deleteMin`.
items.statement:
structure FindMin (α) where
  /-- The list of elements prior to the minimum element, encoded as a "difference list". -/
  before : Heap α → Heap α := id
  /-- The minimum element. -/
  val : α
  /-- The children of the minimum element. -/
  node : HeapNode α
  /-- The forest after the minimum element. -/
  next : Heap α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.findMin
items.doc:
`O(log n)`. Find the minimum element, and return a data structure `FindMin` with information
needed to reconstruct the rest of the binomial heap.
items.statement:
def Heap.findMin (le : α → α → Bool) (k : Heap α → Heap α) :
    Heap α → FindMin α → FindMin α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.deleteMin
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Find and remove the the minimum element from the binomial heap.
items.statement: def Heap.deleteMin (le : α → α → Bool) : Heap α → Option (α × Heap α)

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.tail?
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Get the tail of the binomial heap after removing the minimum element.
items.statement: def Heap.tail? (le : α → α → Bool) (h : Heap α) : Option (Heap α)

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.tail
items.doc: `O(log n)`. Remove the minimum element of the heap.
items.statement: def Heap.tail (le : α → α → Bool) (h : Heap α) : Heap α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.realSize_merge
items.statement:
theorem Heap.realSize_merge (le) (s₁ s₂ : Heap α) :
    (s₁.merge le s₂).realSize = s₁.realSize + s₂.realSize

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.realSize_toHeap
items.statement: theorem HeapNode.realSize_toHeap (s : HeapNode α) : s.toHeap.realSize = s.realSize

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.realSize_deleteMin
items.statement:
theorem Heap.realSize_deleteMin {s : Heap α} (eq : s.deleteMin le = some (a, s')) :
    s.realSize = s'.realSize + 1

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.realSize_tail?
items.statement:
theorem Heap.realSize_tail? {s : Heap α} : s.tail? le = some s' →
    s.realSize = s'.realSize + 1

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.realSize_tail
items.statement: theorem Heap.realSize_tail (le) (s : Heap α) : (s.tail le).realSize = s.realSize - 1

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.foldM
items.doc:
`O(n log n)`. Monadic fold over the elements of a heap in increasing order,
by repeatedly pulling the minimum element out of the heap.
items.statement:
def Heap.foldM [Monad m] (le : α → α → Bool) (s : Heap α)
    (init : β) (f : β → α → m β) : m β

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.fold
items.doc:
`O(n log n)`. Fold over the elements of a heap in increasing order,
by repeatedly pulling the minimum element out of the heap.
items.statement: def Heap.fold (le : α → α → Bool) (s : Heap α) (init : β) (f : β → α → β) : β

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.toArray
items.doc: `O(n log n)`. Convert the heap to an array in increasing order.
items.statement: def Heap.toArray (le : α → α → Bool) (s : Heap α) : Array α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.toList
items.doc: `O(n log n)`. Convert the heap to a list in increasing order.
items.statement: def Heap.toList (le : α → α → Bool) (s : Heap α) : List α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.foldTreeM
items.doc: `O(n)`. Fold a monadic function over the tree structure to accumulate a value.
items.statement: def HeapNode.foldTreeM : HeapNode α → m β

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.foldTreeM
items.doc: `O(n)`. Fold a monadic function over the tree structure to accumulate a value.
items.statement: def Heap.foldTreeM : Heap α → m β

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.foldTree
items.doc: `O(n)`. Fold a function over the tree structure to accumulate a value.
items.statement: def Heap.foldTree (nil : β) (join : α → β → β → β) (s : Heap α) : β

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.toListUnordered
items.doc: `O(n)`. Convert the heap to a list in arbitrary order.
items.statement: def Heap.toListUnordered (s : Heap α) : List α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.toArrayUnordered
items.doc: `O(n)`. Convert the heap to an array in arbitrary order.
items.statement: def Heap.toArrayUnordered (s : Heap α) : Array α

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.WF
items.doc:
The well formedness predicate for a heap node.
It asserts that:
* If `a` is added at the top to make the forest into a tree, the resulting tree
  is a `le`-min-heap (if `le` is well-behaved)
* When interpreting `child` and `sibling` as left and right children of a binary tree,
  it is a perfect binary tree with depth `r`
items.statement: def HeapNode.WF (le : α → α → Bool) (a : α) : HeapNode α → Nat → Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.WF
items.doc:
The well formedness predicate for a binomial heap.
It asserts that:
* It consists of a list of well formed trees with the specified ranks
* The ranks are in strictly increasing order, and all are at least `n`
items.statement: def Heap.WF (le : α → α → Bool) (n : Nat) : Heap α → Prop

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.WF.nil
items.statement: theorem Heap.WF.nil : Heap.nil.WF le n

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.WF.singleton
items.statement: theorem Heap.WF.singleton : (Heap.singleton a).WF le 0

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.WF.of_rankGT
items.statement: theorem Heap.WF.of_rankGT (hlt : s.rankGT n) (h : Heap.WF le n' s) : s.WF le (n+1)

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.WF.of_le
items.statement: theorem Heap.WF.of_le (hle : n ≤ n') (h : Heap.WF le n' s) : s.WF le n

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.rankGT.of_le
items.statement: theorem Heap.rankGT.of_le (h : Heap.rankGT s n) (h' : n' ≤ n) : s.rankGT n'

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.WF.rankGT
items.statement: theorem Heap.WF.rankGT (h : Heap.WF lt (n+1) s) : s.rankGT n

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.WF.merge'
items.statement:
theorem Heap.WF.merge' (h₁ : s₁.WF le n) (h₂ : s₂.WF le n) :
    (merge le s₁ s₂).WF le n ∧ ((s₁.rankGT n ↔ s₂.rankGT n) → (merge le s₁ s₂).rankGT n)

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.Heap.WF.merge
items.statement: theorem Heap.WF.merge (h₁ : s₁.WF le n) (h₂ : s₂.WF le n) : (merge le s₁ s₂).WF le n

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.WF.rank_eq
items.statement: theorem HeapNode.WF.rank_eq : ∀ {n} {s : HeapNode α}, s.WF le a n → s.rank = n

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.HeapNode.WF.toHeap
items.statement: theorem HeapNode.WF.toHeap {s : HeapNode α} (h : s.WF le a n) : s.toHeap.WF le 0

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap.Imp.FindMin.WF
items.doc:
The well formedness predicate for a `FindMin` value.
This is not actually a predicate, as it contains an additional data value
`rank` corresponding to the rank of the returned node, which is omitted from `findMin`.
items.statement:
structure FindMin.WF (le : α → α → Bool) (res : FindMin α) where
  /-- The rank of the minimum element -/
  rank : Nat
  /-- `before` is a difference list which can be appended to a binomial heap
  with ranks at least `rank` to produce another well formed heap. -/
  before : ∀ {s}, s.WF le rank → (res.before s).WF le 0
  /-- `node` is a well formed forest of rank `rank` with `val` at the root. -/
  node : res.node.WF le res.val rank
  /-- `next` is a binomial heap with ranks above `rank + 1`. -/
  next : res.next.WF le (rank + 1)

items.name: Batteries.BinomialHeap
items.doc:
A [binomial heap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_heap) is a data structure which supports
the following primary operations:

* `insert : α → BinomialHeap α → BinomialHeap α`: add an element to the heap
* `deleteMin : BinomialHeap α → Option (α × BinomialHeap α)`:
  remove the minimum element from the heap
* `merge : BinomialHeap α → BinomialHeap α → BinomialHeap α`: combine two heaps

The first two operations are known as a "priority queue", so this could be called
a "mergeable priority queue". The standard choice for a priority queue is a binary heap,
which supports `insert` and `deleteMin` in `O(log n)`, but `merge` is `O(n)`.
With a `BinomialHeap`, all three operations are `O(log n)`.

items.name: Char.caseFoldAsciiOnly
items.doc:
Case folding for ASCII characters only.

Alphabetic ASCII characters are mapped to their lowercase form, all other characters are left
unchanged. This agrees with the Unicode case folding algorithm for ASCII characters.

```
#eval caseFoldAsciiOnly 'A' == 'a'
#eval caseFoldAsciiOnly 'a' == 'a'
#eval caseFoldAsciiOnly 'À' == 'À'
#eval caseFoldAsciiOnly 'à' == 'à'
#eval caseFoldAsciiOnly '$' == '$'
```
items.statement: abbrev caseFoldAsciiOnly

```
#eval beqCaseInsensitiveAsciiOnly 'a' 'A' -- true
#eval beqCaseInsensitiveAsciiOnly 'a' 'a' -- true
#eval beqCaseInsensitiveAsciiOnly '$' '$' -- true
#eval beqCaseInsensitiveAsciiOnly 'a' 'b' -- false
#eval beqCaseInsensitiveAsciiOnly 'γ' 'Γ' -- false
#eval beqCaseInsensitiveAsciiOnly 'ä' 'Ä' -- false
```

ASCII-case insensitive implementation comparison returning an `Ordering`. Useful for sorting.

```
#eval cmpCaseInsensitiveAsciiOnly 'a' 'A' -- eq
```

items.name: Batteries.DList
items.doc:
A difference List is a Function that, given a List, returns the original
contents of the difference List prepended to the given List.
This structure supports `O(1)` `append` and `push` operations on lists, making it
useful for append-heavy uses such as logging and pretty printing.
items.statement:
structure DList (α : Type u) where
  /-- "Run" a `DList` by appending it on the right by a `List α` to get another `List α`. -/
  apply     : List α → List α
  /-- The `apply` function of a `DList` is completely determined by the list `apply []`. -/
  invariant : ∀ l, apply l = apply [] ++ l

modules.title: Difference list
modules.doc:
This file provides a few results about `DList`.

A difference list is a function that, given a list, returns the original content of the
difference list prepended to the given list. It is useful to represent elements of a given type
as `a₁ + ... + aₙ` where `+ : α → α → α` is any operation, without actually computing.

This structure supports `O(1)` `append` and `push` operations on lists, making it
useful for append-heavy uses such as logging and pretty printing.

items.name: Fin.dfoldrM
items.doc:
Heterogeneous monadic fold over `Fin n` from right to left:
```
Fin.foldrM n f xₙ = do
  let xₙ₋₁ : α (n-1) ← f (n-1) xₙ
  let xₙ₋₂ : α (n-2) ← f (n-2) xₙ₋₁
  ...
  let x₀ : α 0 ← f 0 x₁
  pure x₀
```
This is the dependent version of `Fin.foldrM`.
items.statement:
def dfoldrM [Monad m] (n : Nat) (α : Fin (n + 1) → Type _)
    (f : ∀ (i : Fin n), α i.succ → m (α i.castSucc)) (init : α (last n)) : m (α 0)

items.name: Fin.dfoldr
items.doc:
Heterogeneous fold over `Fin n` from the right: `foldr 3 f x = f 0 (f 1 (f 2 x))`, where
`f 2 : α 3 → α 2`, `f 1 : α 2 → α 1`, etc.

This is the dependent version of `Fin.foldr`.
items.statement:
def dfoldr (n : Nat) (α : Fin (n + 1) → Type _)
    (f : ∀ (i : Fin n), α i.succ → α i.castSucc) (init : α (last n)) : α 0

items.name: Fin.dfoldlM
items.doc:
Heterogeneous monadic fold over `Fin n` from left to right:
```
Fin.foldlM n f x₀ = do
  let x₁ : α 1 ← f 0 x₀
  let x₂ : α 2 ← f 1 x₁
  ...
  let xₙ : α n ← f (n-1) xₙ₋₁
  pure xₙ
```
This is the dependent version of `Fin.foldlM`.
items.statement:
def dfoldlM [Monad m] (n : Nat) (α : Fin (n + 1) → Type _)
    (f : ∀ (i : Fin n), α i.castSucc → m (α i.succ)) (init : α 0) : m (α (last n))

items.name: Fin.dfoldl
items.doc:
Heterogeneous fold over `Fin n` from the left: `foldl 3 f x = f 0 (f 1 (f 2 x))`, where
`f 0 : α 0 → α 1`, `f 1 : α 1 → α 2`, etc.

This is the dependent version of `Fin.foldl`.
items.statement:
def dfoldl (n : Nat) (α : Fin (n + 1) → Type _)
    (f : ∀ (i : Fin n), α i.castSucc → α i.succ) (init : α 0) : α (last n)

modules.title: Low-level coding recipes for `Fin` types
modules.doc:
This module collects encoding/decoding bijections to represent basic type constructors of `Fin`
types as `Fin` types. These functions implement the isomorphism `Option (Fin n) ≃ Fin (n+1)`,
`Fin m ⊕ Fin n ≃ Fin (m + n)`, `Fin m × Fin n ≃ Fin (m * n)`, ..., including, dependent sums,
dependent products, decidable subtypes and decidable quotients.

Only a minimal API is provided. These utility functions are intended for use in other constructions.
Such constructions should avoid exposing these functions as they are not meant for public use.

items.doc: Encode `{ i : Fin n // P i }` into `Fin (Fin.countP P)` where `P` is a decidable predicate.
items.statement:
def encodeSubtype (P : Fin n → Prop) [inst : DecidablePred P] (i : { i // P i }) :
    Fin (Fin.countP (P ·))

items.name: Fin.decodeSubtype
items.doc: Decode `{ i : Fin n // P i }` from `Fin (Fin.countP P)` where `P` is a decidable predicate.
items.statement:
def decodeSubtype (P : Fin n → Prop) [inst : DecidablePred P] (k : Fin (Fin.countP (P ·))) :
    { i // P i }

items.name: Fin.encodeSubtype_zero_pos
items.statement:
theorem encodeSubtype_zero_pos {P : Fin (n+1) → Prop} [DecidablePred P] (h₀ : P 0) :
    encodeSubtype P ⟨0, h₀⟩ = ⟨0, by grind [countP_succ]⟩

items.name: Fin.encodeSubtype_succ_pos
Fin.encodeSubtype_succ_neg
items.statement:
theorem encodeSubtype_succ_neg {P : Fin (n+1) → Prop} [DecidablePred P] (h₀ : ¬ P 0) {i : Fin n}
    (h : P i.succ) : encodeSubtype P ⟨i.succ, h⟩ =
      (encodeSubtype (fun i => P i.succ) ⟨i, h⟩).cast
        (by simp [-countP_eq_countP_map_finRange, countP_succ, *])

items.name: Fin.encodeSubtype_decodeSubtype
items.statement:
theorem encodeSubtype_decodeSubtype (P : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred P]
    (x : Fin (Fin.countP (P ·))) : encodeSubtype P (decodeSubtype P x) = x

theorem decodeSubtype_encodeSubtype (P : Fin n → Prop) [DecidablePred P] (x : { x // P x}) :

items.statement: abbrev getRepr (s : Setoid (Fin n)) [DecidableRel s.r] (x : Fin n) : Fin n

items.name: Fin.encodeQuotient
items.doc: Encode `Quotient s` into `Fin m` where `s` is a decidable setoid on `Fin n`.
items.statement:
def encodeQuotient (s : Setoid (Fin n)) [DecidableRel s.r] (x : Quotient s) :

items.name: Fin.decodeQuotient

items.name: Fin.dfoldrM_loop_zero
items.statement:
theorem dfoldrM_loop_zero [Monad m] (f : (i : Fin n) → α i.succ → m (α i.castSucc)) (x) :
    dfoldrM.loop n α f 0 h x = pure x

items.name: Fin.dfoldrM_loop_succ
items.statement:
theorem dfoldrM_loop_succ [Monad m] (f : (i : Fin n) → α i.succ → m (α i.castSucc)) (x) :
    dfoldrM.loop n α f (i+1) h x = f ⟨i, by omega⟩ x >>= dfoldrM.loop n α f i (by omega)

items.name: Fin.dfoldrM_loop
items.statement:
theorem dfoldrM_loop [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] (f : (i : Fin (n+1)) → α i.succ → m (α i.castSucc))
    (x) : dfoldrM.loop (n+1) α f (i+1) h x =
      dfoldrM.loop n (α ∘ succ) (f ·.succ) i (by omega) x >>= f 0

items.name: Fin.dfoldrM_zero
items.statement:
theorem dfoldrM_zero [Monad m] (f : (i : Fin 0) → α i.succ → m (α i.castSucc)) (x) :
    dfoldrM 0 α f x = pure x

items.name: Fin.dfoldrM_succ
items.statement:
theorem dfoldrM_succ [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] (f : (i : Fin (n+1)) → α i.succ → m (α i.castSucc))
    (x) : dfoldrM (n+1) α f x = dfoldrM n (α ∘ succ) (f ·.succ) x >>= f 0

items.name: Fin.dfoldrM_eq_foldrM
items.statement:
theorem dfoldrM_eq_foldrM [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] (f : (i : Fin n) → α → m α) (x) :
    dfoldrM n (fun _ => α) f x = foldrM n f x

items.name: Fin.dfoldr_eq_dfoldrM
items.statement:
theorem dfoldr_eq_dfoldrM (f : (i : Fin n) → α i.succ → α i.castSucc) (x) :
    dfoldr n α f x = dfoldrM (m:=Id) n α f x

items.name: Fin.dfoldr_zero
items.statement:
theorem dfoldr_zero (f : (i : Fin 0) → α i.succ → α i.castSucc) (x) :
    dfoldr 0 α f x = x

items.name: Fin.dfoldr_succ
items.statement:
theorem dfoldr_succ (f : (i : Fin (n+1)) → α i.succ → α i.castSucc) (x) :
    dfoldr (n+1) α f x = f 0 (dfoldr n (α ∘ succ) (f ·.succ) x)

items.name: Fin.dfoldr_succ_last
Fin.dfoldr_eq_foldr
items.statement:
theorem dfoldr_eq_foldr (f : (i : Fin n) → α → α) (x) :
    dfoldr n (fun _ => α) f x = foldr n f x

items.name: Fin.dfoldlM_loop_lt
items.statement:
theorem dfoldlM_loop_lt [Monad m] (f : ∀ (i : Fin n), α i.castSucc → m (α i.succ)) (h : i < n) (x) :
    dfoldlM.loop n α f i (Nat.lt_add_right 1 h) x =
      (f ⟨i, h⟩ x) >>= (dfoldlM.loop n α f (i+1) (Nat.add_lt_add_right h 1))

items.name: Fin.dfoldlM_loop_eq
items.statement:
theorem dfoldlM_loop_eq [Monad m] (f : ∀ (i : Fin n), α i.castSucc → m (α i.succ)) (x) :
    dfoldlM.loop n α f n (Nat.le_refl _) x = pure x

items.name: Fin.dfoldlM_zero
items.statement:
theorem dfoldlM_zero [Monad m] (f : (i : Fin 0) → α i.castSucc → m (α i.succ)) (x) :
    dfoldlM 0 α f x = pure x

items.name: Fin.dfoldlM_loop
items.statement:
theorem dfoldlM_loop [Monad m] (f : (i : Fin (n+1)) → α i.castSucc → m (α i.succ)) (h : i < n+1)
    (x) : dfoldlM.loop (n+1) α f i (Nat.lt_add_right 1 h) x =
      f ⟨i, h⟩ x >>= (dfoldlM.loop n (α ∘ succ) (f ·.succ ·) i h .)

items.name: Fin.dfoldlM_succ
items.statement:
theorem dfoldlM_succ [Monad m] (f : (i : Fin (n+1)) → α i.castSucc → m (α i.succ)) (x) :
    dfoldlM (n+1) α f x = f 0 x >>= (dfoldlM n (α ∘ succ) (f ·.succ ·) .)

items.name: Fin.dfoldlM_eq_foldlM
items.statement:
theorem dfoldlM_eq_foldlM [Monad m] (f : (i : Fin n) → α → m α) (x : α) :
    dfoldlM n (fun _ => α) f x = foldlM n (fun x i => f i x) x

items.name: Fin.dfoldl_zero
items.statement:
theorem dfoldl_zero (f : (i : Fin 0) → α i.castSucc → α i.succ) (x) :
    dfoldl 0 α f x = x

items.name: Fin.dfoldl_succ
items.statement:
theorem dfoldl_succ (f : (i : Fin (n+1)) → α i.castSucc → α i.succ) (x) :
    dfoldl (n+1) α f x = dfoldl n (α ∘ succ) (f ·.succ ·) (f 0 x)

items.name: Fin.dfoldl_succ_last
items.statement:
theorem dfoldl_succ_last (f : (i : Fin (n+1)) → α i.castSucc → α i.succ) (x) :
    dfoldl (n+1) α f x = f (last n) (dfoldl n (α ∘ castSucc) (f ·.castSucc ·) x)

items.name: Fin.dfoldl_eq_dfoldlM
items.statement:
theorem dfoldl_eq_dfoldlM (f : (i : Fin n) → α i.castSucc → α i.succ) (x) :
    dfoldl n α f x = dfoldlM (m := Id) n α f x

items.name: Fin.dfoldl_eq_foldl
items.statement:
theorem dfoldl_eq_foldl (f : Fin n → α → α) (x : α) :
    dfoldl n (fun _ => α) f x = foldl n (fun x i => f i x) x

theorem foldl_assoc {op : α → α → α} [ha : Std.Associative op] {f : Fin n → α} {a₁ a₂} :

      (a = b ∨ (a = .zero .positive ∧ b = .zero .negative) ∨
        (a = .zero .negative ∧ b = .zero .positive))

    (hb : spec.Valid b) (hb' : spec.Valid b') :
    (unpack spec b).beq (unpack spec b') ↔ b ≠ packedNaN spec ∧ b' ≠ packedNaN spec ∧
        (b = b' ∨ (b = packedZero spec .positive ∧ b' = packedZero spec .negative) ∨
          (b = packedZero spec .negative ∧ b' = packedZero spec .positive))

Note that the returned key may not be identical to the input, if `==` ignores some part
of the value.

```
hashMap.findEntry? "one" = some ("one", 1)
```

items.name: Batteries.HashMap
items.doc:
`HashMap α β` is a key-value map which stores elements in an array using a hash function
to find the values. This allows it to have very good performance for lookups
(average `O(1)` for a perfectly random hash function), but it is not a persistent data structure,
meaning that one should take care to use the map linearly when performing updates.
Copies are `O(n)`.

structure _root_.Batteries.HashMap (α : Type u) (β : Type v) [BEq α] [Hashable α] where
  /-- The inner `Std.HashMap` powering the `Batteries.HashMap`. -/
  inner : Std.HashMap α β

```
def hashMap := ofList [("one", 1), ("two", 2)]
hashMap.insert "three" 3 = {"one" => 1, "two" => 2, "three" => 3}
hashMap.insert "two" 0 = {"one" => 1, "two" => 0}
```

```
hashMap.contains "three" = false
```
items.statement: def contains (self : HashMap α β) (a : α) : Bool

items.name: Batteries.HashMap.foldM
items.doc:
Folds a monadic function over the elements in the map (in arbitrary order).
```
def sumEven (sum: Nat) (k : String) (v : Nat) : Except String Nat :=
  if v % 2 == 0 then pure (sum + v) else throw s!"value {v} at key {k} is not even"

foldM sumEven 0 (ofList [("one", 1), ("three", 3)]) =
  Except.error "value 3 at key three is not even"
foldM sumEven 0 (ofList [("two", 2), ("four", 4)]) = Except.ok 6
```
items.statement: def foldM [Monad m] (f : δ → α → β → m δ) (init : δ) (self : HashMap α β) : m δ

items.name: Batteries.HashMap.fold
items.doc:
Folds a function over the elements in the map (in arbitrary order).
```
fold (fun sum _ v => sum + v) 0 (ofList [("one", 1), ("two", 2)]) = 3
```
items.statement: def fold (f : δ → α → β → δ) (init : δ) (self : HashMap α β) : δ

items.name: Batteries.HashMap.mergeWithM
items.doc:
Combines two hashmaps using a monadic function `f` to combine two values at a key.
```
def map1 := ofList [("one", 1), ("two", 2)]
def map2 := ofList [("two", 2), ("three", 3)]
def map3 := ofList [("two", 3), ("three", 3)]
def mergeIfNoConflict? (_ : String) (v₁ v₂ : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  if v₁ != v₂ then none else some v₁


mergeWithM mergeIfNoConflict? map1 map2 = some {"one" => 1, "two" => 2, "three" => 3}
mergeWithM mergeIfNoConflict? map1 map3 = none
```
items.statement:
def mergeWithM [Monad m] (f : α → β → β → m β)
    (self other : HashMap α β) : m (HashMap α β)

items.name: Batteries.HashMap.mergeWith
items.doc:
Combines two hashmaps using function `f` to combine two values at a key.
```
mergeWith (fun _ v₁ v₂ => v₁ + v₂ )
  (ofList [("one", 1), ("two", 2)]) (ofList [("two", 2), ("three", 3)]) =
    {"one" => 1, "two" => 4, "three" => 3}
```
items.statement: def mergeWith (f : α → β → β → β) (self other : HashMap α β) : HashMap α β

items.name: Batteries.HashMap.forM
items.doc:
Runs a monadic function over the elements in the map (in arbitrary order).
```
def checkEven (k : String) (v : Nat) : Except String Unit :=
  if v % 2 == 0 then pure () else throw s!"value {v} at key {k} is not even"

forM checkEven (ofList [("one", 1), ("three", 3)]) = Except.error "value 3 at key three is not even"
forM checkEven (ofList [("two", 2), ("four", 4)]) = Except.ok ()
```
items.statement: def forM [Monad m] (f : α → β → m PUnit) (self : HashMap α β) : m PUnit

items.name: Batteries.HashMap.toList
items.doc:
Converts the map into a list of key-value pairs.
```
open List
(ofList [("one", 1), ("two", 2)]).toList ~ [("one", 1), ("two", 2)]
```
items.statement: def toList (self : HashMap α β) : List (α × β)

items.name: Batteries.HashMap.toArray
items.doc:
Converts the map into an array of key-value pairs.
```
open List
(ofList [("one", 1), ("two", 2)]).toArray.data ~ #[("one", 1), ("two", 2)].data
```
items.statement: def toArray (self : HashMap α β) : Array (α × β)

items.name: Batteries.HashMap.numBuckets
items.doc: The number of buckets in the hash map.
items.statement: def numBuckets (self : HashMap α β) : Nat

items.name: Batteries.HashMap.ofList
items.doc:
Builds a `HashMap` from a list of key-value pairs.
Values of duplicated keys are replaced by their respective last occurrences.
```
ofList [("one", 1), ("one", 2)] = {"one" => 2}
```
items.statement: def ofList [BEq α] [Hashable α] (l : List (α × β)) : HashMap α β

items.name: Batteries.HashMap.ofListWith
items.doc:
Variant of `ofList` which accepts a function that combines values of duplicated keys.
```
ofListWith [("one", 1), ("one", 2)] (fun v₁ v₂ => v₁ + v₂) = {"one" => 3}
```
items.statement: def ofListWith [BEq α] [Hashable α] (l : List (α × β)) (f : β → β → β) : HashMap α β

items.name: Int.testBit
items.doc:
`testBit m n` returns whether the `(n+1)` least significant bit is `1` or `0`, using the two's
complement convention for negative `m`.
items.statement: def testBit : Int → Nat → Bool

items.name: Int.ofBits
items.doc:
Construct an integer from a sequence of bits using little endian convention.

The sign is determined using the two's complement convention: the result is negative if and only if
`n > 0` and `f (n-1) = true`.
items.statement: def ofBits (f : Fin n → Bool)

items.name: Int.ofBits_zero
items.statement: theorem ofBits_zero (f : Fin 0 → Bool) : ofBits f = 0

items.name: Int.testBit_ofBits_lt
items.statement:
theorem testBit_ofBits_lt {f : Fin n → Bool} (h : i < n) :
    (ofBits f).testBit i = f ⟨i, h⟩

items.name: Int.testBit_ofBits_ge
items.statement:
theorem testBit_ofBits_ge {f : Fin n → Bool} (h : i ≥ n) :
    (ofBits f).testBit i = decide (ofBits f < 0)

items.name: Int.testBit_ofBits
items.statement:
theorem testBit_ofBits (f : Fin n → Bool) :
    (ofBits f).testBit i = if h : i < n then f ⟨i, h⟩ else decide (ofBits f < 0)

items.name: List.toArrayMap
items.doc:
This function is provided as a more efficient runtime alternative to `(l.map f).toArray`.
(It avoids the intermediate memory allocation of creating an intermediate list first.)
For verification purposes, we immediately simplify it to that form.
items.statement: def toArrayMap (l : List α) (f : α → β) : Array β

items.name: List.toArrayMap_toList
items.statement: theorem toArrayMap_toList (l : List α) (f : α → β ) : (l.toArrayMap f).toList = l.map f

items.name: List.toArrayMap_eq_toArray_map
items.statement: theorem toArrayMap_eq_toArray_map (l : List α) (f : α → β) : l.toArrayMap f = (l.map f).toArray

modules.doc: ## New definitions

items.name: List.max!
items.doc:
Get the maximum element of a list.
If the given list is empty, returns `(default : α)` and produces a panic error message.
items.statement: def max! {α} [Inhabited α] [Max α] (xs : List α) : α

items.name: List.min!
items.doc:
Get the minimum element of a list.
If the given list is empty, returns `(default : α)` and produces a panic error message.
items.statement: def min! {α} [Inhabited α] [Min α] (xs : List α) : α

items.name: List.bagInter
items.doc:
Computes the "bag intersection" of `l₁` and `l₂`, that is,
the collection of elements of `l₁` which are also in `l₂`. As each element
is identified, it is removed from `l₂`, so elements are counted with multiplicity.
items.statement: protected def bagInter {α} [BEq α] : List α → List α → List α

items.name: List.diff
items.doc: Computes the difference of `l₁` and `l₂`, by removing each element in `l₂` from `l₁`.
items.statement: protected def diff {α} [BEq α] : List α → List α → List α

items.name: List.next?
items.doc: Get the head and tail of a list, if it is nonempty.
items.statement: def next? : List α → Option (α × List α)

items.name: List.after
items.doc:
`after p xs` is the suffix of `xs` after the first element that satisfies
`p`, not including that element.
```lean
after      (· == 1) [0, 1, 2, 3] = [2, 3]
drop_while (· != 1) [0, 1, 2, 3] = [1, 2, 3]
```
items.statement: def after (p : α → Bool) : List α → List α

items.name: List.replaceF
items.doc: Replaces the first element of the list for which `f` returns `some` with the returned value.
items.statement: def replaceF (f : α → Option α) : List α → List α

items.name: List.replaceFTR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `replaceF`.
items.statement: def replaceFTR (f : α → Option α) (l : List α) : List α

items.name: List.replaceF_eq_replaceFTR
items.statement: theorem replaceF_eq_replaceFTR : @replaceF = @replaceFTR

items.name: List.union
items.doc:
Constructs the union of two lists, by inserting the elements of `l₁` in reverse order to `l₂`.
As a result, `l₂` will always be a suffix, but only the last occurrence of each element in `l₁`
will be retained (but order will otherwise be preserved).
items.statement: protected def union [BEq α] (l₁ l₂ : List α) : List α

items.name: List.inter
items.doc:
Constructs the intersection of two lists, by filtering the elements of `l₁` that are in `l₂`.
Unlike `bagInter` this does not preserve multiplicity: `[1, 1].inter [1]` is `[1, 1]`.
items.statement: protected def inter [BEq α] (l₁ l₂ : List α) : List α

items.name: List.splitAtD
items.doc:
Split a list at an index. Ensures the left list always has the specified length
by right padding with the provided default element.
```
splitAtD 2 [a, b, c] x = ([a, b], [c])
splitAtD 4 [a, b, c] x = ([a, b, c, x], [])
```
items.statement: def splitAtD (n : Nat) (l : List α) (dflt : α) : List α × List α

items.name: List.modifyLast
items.doc: Apply `f` to the last element of `l`, if it exists.
items.statement: def modifyLast (f : α → α) (l : List α) : List α

items.name: List.headD_eq_head?
items.statement: theorem headD_eq_head? (l) (a : α) : headD l a = (head? l).getD a

items.name: List.takeD
items.doc:
Take `n` elements from a list `l`. If `l` has less than `n` elements, append `n - length l`
elements `x`.
items.statement: def takeD : Nat → List α → α → List α

items.name: List.takeD_zero
items.statement: theorem takeD_zero (l) (a : α) : takeD 0 l a = []

items.name: List.takeD_succ
items.statement:
theorem takeD_succ (l) (a : α) :
    takeD (n+1) l a = l.head?.getD a :: takeD n l.tail a

items.name: List.takeD_nil
items.statement: theorem takeD_nil (n) (a : α) : takeD n [] a = replicate n a

items.name: List.takeDTR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `takeD`.
items.statement: def takeDTR (n : Nat) (l : List α) (dflt : α) : List α

items.name: List.takeDTR_go_eq
items.statement: theorem takeDTR_go_eq : ∀ n l, takeDTR.go dflt n l acc = acc.toList ++ takeD n l dflt

items.name: List.takeD_eq_takeDTR
items.statement: theorem takeD_eq_takeDTR : @takeD = @takeDTR

items.name: List.scanAuxM
items.doc: Tail-recursive helper function for `scanlM` and `scanrM`
items.statement: def scanAuxM [Monad m] (f : β → α → m β) (init : β) (l : List α) : m (List β)

items.name: List.foldlIdx
items.doc:
Fold a list from left to right as with `foldl`, but the combining function
also receives each element's index added to an optional parameter `start`
(i.e. the numbers that `f` takes as its first argument will be greater than or equal to `start` and
less than `start + l.length`).
items.statement:
def foldlIdx (f : Nat → α → β → α) (init : α) :
    List β → (start : Nat := 0) → α

items.name: List.foldrIdx
items.doc:
Fold a list from right to left as with `foldr`, but the combining function
also receives each element's index added to an optional parameter `start`
(i.e. the numbers that `f` takes as its first argument will be greater than or equal to `start` and
less than `start + l.length`).
items.statement:
def foldrIdx {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : Nat → α → β → β) (init : β) :
    (l : List α) → (start : Nat := 0) → β

items.name: List.foldrIdxTR
items.doc: A tail-recursive version of `foldrIdx`.
items.statement: def foldrIdxTR (f : Nat → α → β → β) (init : β) (l : List α) (start : Nat := 0) : β

items.name: List.foldrIdx_eq_foldrIdxTR
items.statement: theorem foldrIdx_eq_foldrIdxTR : @foldrIdx = @foldrIdxTR

items.name: List.findIdxs
items.doc:
`findIdxs p l s` is the list of indexes of elements of `l` that satisfy `p`, added to an
optional parameter `s` (so that the members of `findIdxs p l s` will be greater than or
equal to `s` and less than `l.length + s`).
items.statement: def findIdxs (p : α → Bool) (l : List α) (start : Nat := 0) : List Nat

items.name: List.findIdxsValues
items.doc:
Returns the elements of `l` that satisfy `p` together with their indexes in
`l` added to an optional parameter `start`. The returned list is ordered by index.
We have `l.findIdxsValues p s = (l.findIdxs p s).zip (l.filter p)`.
items.statement: def findIdxsValues (p : α → Bool) (l : List α) (start : Nat := 0) : List (Nat × α)

items.name: List.findIdxNth
items.doc:
`findIdxNth p xs n` returns the index of the `n`th element for which `p` returns `true`.
For example:
```
findIdxNth (· < 3) [5, 1, 3, 2, 4, 0, 1, 4] 2 = 5
```
items.statement: def findIdxNth (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) (n : Nat) : Nat

items.name: List.idxsOf
items.doc:
`idxsOf a l s` is the list of all indexes of `a` in `l`,  added to an
optional parameter `s`. For example:
```
idxsOf b [a, b, a, a] = [1]
idxsOf a [a, b, a, a] 5 = [5, 7, 8]
```
items.statement: def idxsOf [BEq α] (a : α) (xs : List α) (start : Nat := 0) : List Nat

items.name: List.idxOfNth
items.doc:
`idxOfNth a xs n` returns the index of the `n`th instance of `a` in `xs`, counting from `0`.

For example:
```
idxOfNth 1 [5, 1, 3, 2, 4, 0, 1, 4] 1 = 6
```
items.statement: def idxOfNth [BEq α] (a : α) (xs : List α) (n : Nat) : Nat

items.name: List.countPBefore
items.doc:
`countPBefore p xs i hip` counts the number of `x` in `xs` before the `i`th index for
which `p x = true`.

For example:
```
countPBefore (· < 3) [5, 1, 3, 2, 4, 0, 1, 4] 5 = 2
```
items.statement: def countPBefore (p : α → Bool) (xs : List α) (i : Nat) : Nat

items.name: List.countBefore
items.doc:
`countBefore a xs n` counts the number of `x` in `xs` before the
`i`th index for which `x == a` is true.

For example:
```
countBefore 1 [5, 1, 3, 2, 4, 0, 1, 4] 6 = 1
```
items.statement: def countBefore [BEq α] (a : α) : List α → Nat → Nat

items.name: List.lookmap
items.doc:
`lookmap` is a combination of `lookup` and `filterMap`.
`lookmap f l` will apply `f : α → Option α` to each element of the list,
replacing `a → b` at the first value `a` in the list such that `f a = some b`.
items.statement: def lookmap (f : α → Option α) (l : List α) : List α

items.name: List.inits
items.doc:
`inits l` is the list of initial segments of `l`.
```
inits [1, 2, 3] = [[], [1], [1, 2], [1, 2, 3]]
```
items.statement: def inits : List α → List (List α)

items.name: List.initsTR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `inits`.
items.statement: def initsTR (l : List α) : List (List α)

items.name: List.inits_eq_initsTR
items.statement: theorem inits_eq_initsTR : @inits = @initsTR

items.name: List.tails
items.doc:
`tails l` is the list of terminal segments of `l`.
```
tails [1, 2, 3] = [[1, 2, 3], [2, 3], [3], []]
```
items.statement: def tails : List α → List (List α)

items.name: List.tailsTR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `tails`.
items.statement: def tailsTR (l : List α) : List (List α)

items.name: List.tails_eq_tailsTR
items.statement: theorem tails_eq_tailsTR : @tails = @tailsTR

items.name: List.sublists'
items.doc:
`sublists' l` is the list of all (non-contiguous) sublists of `l`.
It differs from `sublists` only in the order of appearance of the sublists;
`sublists'` uses the first element of the list as the MSB,
`sublists` uses the first element of the list as the LSB.
```
sublists' [1, 2, 3] = [[], [3], [2], [2, 3], [1], [1, 3], [1, 2], [1, 2, 3]]
```
items.statement: def sublists' (l : List α) : List (List α)

items.name: List.sublists
items.doc:
`sublists l` is the list of all (non-contiguous) sublists of `l`; cf. `sublists'`
for a different ordering.
```
sublists [1, 2, 3] = [[], [1], [2], [1, 2], [3], [1, 3], [2, 3], [1, 2, 3]]
```
items.statement: def sublists (l : List α) : List (List α)

items.name: List.sublistsFast
items.doc: A version of `List.sublists` that has faster runtime performance but worse kernel performance
items.statement: def sublistsFast (l : List α) : List (List α)

items.name: List.sublists_eq_sublistsFast
items.statement: theorem sublists_eq_sublistsFast : @sublists = @sublistsFast

items.name: List.Forall₂
items.doc:
`Forall₂ R l₁ l₂` means that `l₁` and `l₂` have the same length,
and whenever `a` is the nth element of `l₁`, and `b` is the nth element of `l₂`,
then `R a b` is satisfied.
items.statement:
inductive Forall₂ (R : α → β → Prop) : List α → List β → Prop
  /-- Two nil lists are `Forall₂`-related -/
  | nil : Forall₂ R [] []
  /-- Two cons lists are related by `Forall₂ R`
  if the heads are related by `R` and the tails are related by `Forall₂ R` -/
  | cons {a b l₁ l₂} : R a b → Forall₂ R l₁ l₂ → Forall₂ R (a :: l₁) (b :: l₂)

items.name: List.forall₂_cons
items.statement:
theorem forall₂_cons {R : α → β → Prop} {a b l₁ l₂} :
    Forall₂ R (a :: l₁) (b :: l₂) ↔ R a b ∧ Forall₂ R l₁ l₂

items.name: List.all₂
items.doc:
Check for all elements `a`, `b`, where `a` and `b` are the nth element of the first and second
List respectively, that `r a b = true`.
items.statement: def all₂ (r : α → β → Bool) : List α → List β → Bool

items.name: List.all₂_eq_true
items.statement:
theorem all₂_eq_true {r : α → β → Bool} :
    ∀ l₁ l₂, all₂ r l₁ l₂ ↔ Forall₂ (r · ·) l₁ l₂

items.name: List.transpose
items.doc:
Transpose of a list of lists, treated as a matrix.
```
transpose [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]] = [[1, 3, 5], [2, 4, 6]]
```
items.statement: def transpose (l : List (List α)) : List (List α)

items.name: List.sections
items.doc:
List of all sections through a list of lists. A section
of `[L₁, L₂, ..., Lₙ]` is a list whose first element comes from
`L₁`, whose second element comes from `L₂`, and so on.
items.statement: def sections : List (List α) → List (List α)

items.name: List.sectionsTR
items.doc: Optimized version of `sections`.
items.statement: def sectionsTR (L : List (List α)) : List (List α)

items.name: List.sections_eq_nil_of_isEmpty
items.statement: theorem sections_eq_nil_of_isEmpty : ∀ {L}, L.any isEmpty → @sections α L = []

items.name: List.sections_eq_sectionsTR
items.statement: theorem sections_eq_sectionsTR : @sections = @sectionsTR

items.name: List.extractP
items.doc:
`extractP p l` returns a pair of an element `a` of `l` satisfying the predicate
`p`, and `l`, with `a` removed. If there is no such element `a` it returns `(none, l)`.
items.statement: def extractP (p : α → Bool) (l : List α) : Option α × List α

items.name: List.revzip
items.doc:
`revzip l` returns a list of pairs of the elements of `l` paired
with the elements of `l` in reverse order.
```
revzip [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] = [(1, 5), (2, 4), (3, 3), (4, 2), (5, 1)]
```
items.statement: def revzip (l : List α) : List (α × α)

items.name: List.product
items.doc:
`product l₁ l₂` is the list of pairs `(a, b)` where `a ∈ l₁` and `b ∈ l₂`.
```
product [1, 2] [5, 6] = [(1, 5), (1, 6), (2, 5), (2, 6)]
```
items.statement: def product (l₁ : List α) (l₂ : List β) : List (α × β)

items.name: List.productTR
items.doc: Optimized version of `product`.
items.statement: def productTR (l₁ : List α) (l₂ : List β) : List (α × β)

items.name: List.product_eq_productTR
items.statement: theorem product_eq_productTR : @product = @productTR

items.name: List.sigma
items.doc:
`sigma l₁ l₂` is the list of dependent pairs `(a, b)` where `a ∈ l₁` and `b ∈ l₂ a`.
```
sigma [1, 2] (λ_, [(5 : Nat), 6]) = [(1, 5), (1, 6), (2, 5), (2, 6)]
```
items.statement: protected def sigma {σ : α → Type _} (l₁ : List α) (l₂ : ∀ a, List (σ a)) : List (Σ a, σ a)

items.name: List.sigmaTR
items.doc: Optimized version of `sigma`.
items.statement: def sigmaTR {σ : α → Type _} (l₁ : List α) (l₂ : ∀ a, List (σ a)) : List (Σ a, σ a)

items.name: List.sigma_eq_sigmaTR
items.statement: theorem sigma_eq_sigmaTR : @List.sigma = @sigmaTR

items.name: List.ofFnNthVal
items.doc: `ofFnNthVal f i` returns `some (f i)` if `i < n` and `none` otherwise.
items.statement: def ofFnNthVal {n} (f : Fin n → α) (i : Nat) : Option α

items.name: List.Disjoint
items.doc: `Disjoint l₁ l₂` means that `l₁` and `l₂` have no elements in common.
items.statement: def Disjoint (l₁ l₂ : List α) : Prop

items.name: List.takeWhile₂
items.doc:
Returns the longest initial prefix of two lists such that they are pairwise related by `R`.
```
takeWhile₂ (· < ·) [1, 2, 4, 5] [5, 4, 3, 6] = ([1, 2], [5, 4])
```
items.statement: def takeWhile₂ (R : α → β → Bool) : List α → List β → List α × List β

items.name: List.takeWhile₂TR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `takeWhile₂`.
items.statement: def takeWhile₂TR (R : α → β → Bool) (as : List α) (bs : List β) : List α × List β

items.name: List.takeWhile₂_eq_takeWhile₂TR
items.statement: theorem takeWhile₂_eq_takeWhile₂TR : @takeWhile₂ = @takeWhile₂TR

items.name: List.pwFilter
items.doc:
`pwFilter R l` is a maximal sublist of `l` which is `Pairwise R`.
`pwFilter (·≠·)` is the erase duplicates function (cf. `eraseDups`), and `pwFilter (·<·)` finds
a maximal increasing subsequence in `l`. For example,
```
pwFilter (·<·) [0, 1, 5, 2, 6, 3, 4] = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
```
items.statement: def pwFilter (R : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel R] (l : List α) : List α

items.name: List.IsChain
items.doc:
`IsChain R l` means that `R` holds between adjacent elements of `l`. Example:
```
IsChain R [a, b, c, d] ↔ R a b ∧ R b c ∧ R c d
```
items.statement:
inductive IsChain (R : α → α → Prop) : List α → Prop where
  /-- A list of length 0 is a chain. -/
  | nil : IsChain R []
  /-- A list of length 1 is a chain. -/
  | singleton (a : α) : IsChain R [a]
  /-- If `a` relates to `b` and `b::l` is a chain, then `a :: b :: l` is also a chain. -/
  | cons_cons (hr : R a b) (h : IsChain R (b :: l)) : IsChain R (a :: b :: l)

items.name: List.isChain_cons_cons
items.statement: theorem isChain_cons_cons : IsChain R (a :: b :: l) ↔ R a b ∧ IsChain R (b :: l)

items.name: List.eraseDup
items.doc: **Deprecated:** Use `reverse ∘ eraseDups ∘ reverse` or just `eraseDups` instead.
items.statement: abbrev eraseDup [BEq α] : List α → List α

items.name: List.rotate
items.doc:
`rotate l n` rotates the elements of `l` to the left by `n`
```
rotate [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] 2 = [2, 3, 4, 5, 0, 1]
```
items.statement: def rotate (l : List α) (n : Nat) : List α

items.name: List.rotate'
items.doc: `rotate'` is the same as `rotate`, but slower. Used for proofs about `rotate`
items.statement: def rotate' : List α → Nat → List α

items.name: List.mapDiagM
items.doc:
`mapDiagM f l` calls `f` on all elements in the upper triangular part of `l × l`.
That is, for each `e ∈ l`, it will run `f e e` and then `f e e'`
for each `e'` that appears after `e` in `l`.
```
mapDiagM f [1, 2, 3] =
  return [← f 1 1, ← f 1 2, ← f 1 3, ← f 2 2, ← f 2 3, ← f 3 3]
```
items.statement: def mapDiagM [Monad m] (f : α → α → m β) (l : List α) : m (List β)

items.name: List.forDiagM
items.doc:
`forDiagM f l` calls `f` on all elements in the upper triangular part of `l × l`.
That is, for each `e ∈ l`, it will run `f e e` and then `f e e'`
for each `e'` that appears after `e` in `l`.
```
forDiagM f [1, 2, 3] = do f 1 1; f 1 2; f 1 3; f 2 2; f 2 3; f 3 3
```
items.statement: def forDiagM [Monad m] (f : α → α → m PUnit) : List α → m PUnit

items.name: List.getRest
items.doc:
`getRest l l₁` returns `some l₂` if `l = l₁ ++ l₂`.
If `l₁` is not a prefix of `l`, returns `none`
items.statement: def getRest [DecidableEq α] : List α → List α → Option (List α)

items.name: List.dropSlice
items.doc: `List.dropSlice n m xs` removes a slice of length `m` at index `n` in list `xs`.
items.statement: def dropSlice : Nat → Nat → List α → List α

items.name: List.dropSliceTR
items.doc: Optimized version of `dropSlice`.
items.statement: def dropSliceTR (n m : Nat) (l : List α) : List α

items.name: List.dropSlice_zero₂
items.statement: theorem dropSlice_zero₂ : ∀ n l, @dropSlice α n 0 l = l

items.name: List.dropSlice_eq_dropSliceTR
items.statement: theorem dropSlice_eq_dropSliceTR : @dropSlice = @dropSliceTR

items.name: List.zipWithLeft'
items.doc:
Left-biased version of `List.zipWith`. `zipWithLeft' f as bs` applies `f` to each
pair of elements `aᵢ ∈ as` and `bᵢ ∈ bs`. If `bs` is shorter than `as`, `f` is
applied to `none` for the remaining `aᵢ`. Returns the results of the `f`
applications and the remaining `bs`.
```
zipWithLeft' prod.mk [1, 2] ['a'] = ([(1, some 'a'), (2, none)], [])
zipWithLeft' prod.mk [1] ['a', 'b'] = ([(1, some 'a')], ['b'])
```
items.statement: def zipWithLeft' (f : α → Option β → γ) : List α → List β → List γ × List β

items.name: List.zipWithLeft'TR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `zipWithLeft'`.
items.statement:
def zipWithLeft'TR (f : α → Option β → γ)
    (as : List α) (bs : List β) : List γ × List β

items.name: List.zipWithLeft'_eq_zipWithLeft'TR
items.statement: theorem zipWithLeft'_eq_zipWithLeft'TR : @zipWithLeft' = @zipWithLeft'TR

items.name: List.zipWithRight'
items.doc:
Right-biased version of `List.zipWith`. `zipWithRight' f as bs` applies `f` to each
pair of elements `aᵢ ∈ as` and `bᵢ ∈ bs`. If `as` is shorter than `bs`, `f` is
applied to `none` for the remaining `bᵢ`. Returns the results of the `f`
applications and the remaining `as`.
```
zipWithRight' prod.mk [1] ['a', 'b'] = ([(some 1, 'a'), (none, 'b')], [])
zipWithRight' prod.mk [1, 2] ['a'] = ([(some 1, 'a')], [2])
```
items.statement: def zipWithRight' (f : Option α → β → γ) (as : List α) (bs : List β) : List γ × List α

items.name: List.zipLeft'
items.doc:
Left-biased version of `List.zip`. `zipLeft' as bs` returns the list of
pairs `(aᵢ, bᵢ)` for `aᵢ ∈ as` and `bᵢ ∈ bs`. If `bs` is shorter than `as`, the
remaining `aᵢ` are paired with `none`. Also returns the remaining `bs`.
```
zipLeft' [1, 2] ['a'] = ([(1, some 'a'), (2, none)], [])
zipLeft' [1] ['a', 'b'] = ([(1, some 'a')], ['b'])
zipLeft' = zipWithLeft' prod.mk
```
items.statement: def zipLeft' : List α → List β → List (α × Option β) × List β

items.name: List.zipRight'
items.doc:
Right-biased version of `List.zip`. `zipRight' as bs` returns the list of
pairs `(aᵢ, bᵢ)` for `aᵢ ∈ as` and `bᵢ ∈ bs`. If `as` is shorter than `bs`, the
remaining `bᵢ` are paired with `none`. Also returns the remaining `as`.
```
zipRight' [1] ['a', 'b'] = ([(some 1, 'a'), (none, 'b')], [])
zipRight' [1, 2] ['a'] = ([(some 1, 'a')], [2])
zipRight' = zipWithRight' prod.mk
```
items.statement: def zipRight' : List α → List β → List (Option α × β) × List α

items.name: List.zipWithLeft
items.doc:
Left-biased version of `List.zipWith`. `zipWithLeft f as bs` applies `f` to each pair
`aᵢ ∈ as` and `bᵢ ‌∈ bs`. If `bs` is shorter than `as`, `f` is applied to `none`
for the remaining `aᵢ`.
```
zipWithLeft prod.mk [1, 2] ['a'] = [(1, some 'a'), (2, none)]
zipWithLeft prod.mk [1] ['a', 'b'] = [(1, some 'a')]
zipWithLeft f as bs = (zipWithLeft' f as bs).fst
```
items.statement: def zipWithLeft (f : α → Option β → γ) : List α → List β → List γ

items.name: List.zipWithLeftTR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `zipWithLeft`.
items.statement:
def zipWithLeftTR (f : α → Option β → γ)
    (as : List α) (bs : List β) : List γ

items.name: List.zipWithLeft_eq_zipWithLeftTR
items.statement: theorem zipWithLeft_eq_zipWithLeftTR : @zipWithLeft = @zipWithLeftTR

items.name: List.zipWithRight
items.doc:
Right-biased version of `List.zipWith`. `zipWithRight f as bs` applies `f` to each
pair `aᵢ ∈ as` and `bᵢ ‌∈ bs`. If `as` is shorter than `bs`, `f` is applied to
`none` for the remaining `bᵢ`.
```
zipWithRight prod.mk [1, 2] ['a'] = [(some 1, 'a')]
zipWithRight prod.mk [1] ['a', 'b'] = [(some 1, 'a'), (none, 'b')]
zipWithRight f as bs = (zipWithRight' f as bs).fst
```
items.statement: def zipWithRight (f : Option α → β → γ) (as : List α) (bs : List β) : List γ

items.name: List.zipLeft
items.doc:
Left-biased version of `List.zip`. `zipLeft as bs` returns the list of pairs
`(aᵢ, bᵢ)` for `aᵢ ∈ as` and `bᵢ ∈ bs`. If `bs` is shorter than `as`, the
remaining `aᵢ` are paired with `none`.
```
zipLeft [1, 2] ['a'] = [(1, some 'a'), (2, none)]
zipLeft [1] ['a', 'b'] = [(1, some 'a')]
zipLeft = zipWithLeft prod.mk
```
items.statement: def zipLeft : List α → List β → List (α × Option β)

items.name: List.zipRight
items.doc:
Right-biased version of `List.zip`. `zipRight as bs` returns the list of pairs
`(aᵢ, bᵢ)` for `aᵢ ∈ as` and `bᵢ ∈ bs`. If `as` is shorter than `bs`, the
remaining `bᵢ` are paired with `none`.
```
zipRight [1, 2] ['a'] = [(some 1, 'a')]
zipRight [1] ['a', 'b'] = [(some 1, 'a'), (none, 'b')]
zipRight = zipWithRight prod.mk
```
items.statement: def zipRight : List α → List β → List (Option α × β)

items.name: List.allSome
items.doc:
If all elements of `xs` are `some xᵢ`, `allSome xs` returns the `xᵢ`. Otherwise
it returns `none`.
```
allSome [some 1, some 2] = some [1, 2]
allSome [some 1, none  ] = none
```
items.statement: def allSome (l : List (Option α)) : Option (List α)

items.name: List.takeList
items.doc:
`takeList as ns` extracts successive sublists from `as`. For `ns = n₁ ... nₘ`,
it first takes the `n₁` initial elements from `as`, then the next `n₂` ones,
etc. It returns the sublists of `as` -- one for each `nᵢ` -- and the remaining
elements of `as`. If `as` does not have at least as many elements as the sum of
the `nᵢ`, the corresponding sublists will have less than `nᵢ` elements.
```
takeList ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e'] [2, 1, 1] = ([['a', 'b'], ['c'], ['d']], ['e'])
takeList ['a', 'b'] [3, 1] = ([['a', 'b'], []], [])
```
items.statement: def takeList {α} : List α → List Nat → List (List α) × List α

items.name: List.takeListTR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `takeList`.
items.statement:
def takeListTR
    (xs : List α) (ns : List Nat) : List (List α) × List α

items.name: List.takeList_eq_takeListTR
items.statement: theorem takeList_eq_takeListTR : @takeList = @takeListTR

items.name: List.toChunksAux
items.doc:
Auxliary definition used to define `toChunks`.
`toChunksAux n xs i` returns `(xs.take i, (xs.drop i).toChunks (n+1))`,
that is, the first `i` elements of `xs`, and the remaining elements chunked into
sublists of length `n+1`.
items.statement: def toChunksAux {α} (n : Nat) : List α → Nat → List α × List (List α)

items.name: List.toChunks
items.statement: def toChunks {α} : Nat → List α → List (List α)

items.note:
We add some n-ary versions of `List.zipWith` for functions with more than two arguments.
These can also be written in terms of `List.zip` or `List.zipWith`.
For example, `zipWith₃ f xs ys zs` could also be written as
`zipWith id (zipWith f xs ys) zs`
or as
`(zip xs <| zip ys zs).map fun ⟨x, y, z⟩ => f x y z`.

items.name: List.zipWith₃
items.doc: Ternary version of `List.zipWith`.
items.statement: def zipWith₃ (f : α → β → γ → δ) : List α → List β → List γ → List δ

items.name: List.zipWith₄
items.doc: Quaternary version of `List.zipWith`.
items.statement: def zipWith₄ (f : α → β → γ → δ → ε) : List α → List β → List γ → List δ → List ε

items.name: List.zipWith₅
items.doc: Quinary version of `List.zipWith`.
items.statement: def zipWith₅ (f : α → β → γ → δ → ε → ζ) : List α → List β → List γ → List δ → List ε → List ζ

items.name: List.mapWithPrefixSuffixAux
items.doc: An auxiliary function for `List.mapWithPrefixSuffix`.
items.statement: def mapWithPrefixSuffixAux {α β} (f : List α → α → List α → β) : List α → List α → List β

items.name: List.mapWithPrefixSuffix
items.doc:
`List.mapWithPrefixSuffix f l` maps `f` across a list `l`.
For each `a ∈ l` with `l = pref ++ [a] ++ suff`, `a` is mapped to `f pref a suff`.
Example: if `f : list Nat → Nat → list Nat → β`,
`List.mapWithPrefixSuffix f [1, 2, 3]` will produce the list
`[f [] 1 [2, 3], f [1] 2 [3], f [1, 2] 3 []]`.
items.statement: def mapWithPrefixSuffix {α β} (f : List α → α → List α → β) (l : List α) : List β

items.name: List.mapWithComplement
items.doc:
`List.mapWithComplement f l` is a variant of `List.mapWithPrefixSuffix`
that maps `f` across a list `l`.
For each `a ∈ l` with `l = pref ++ [a] ++ suff`, `a` is mapped to `f a (pref ++ suff)`,
i.e., the list input to `f` is `l` with `a` removed.
Example: if `f : Nat → list Nat → β`, `List.mapWithComplement f [1, 2, 3]` will produce the list
`[f 1 [2, 3], f 2 [1, 3], f 3 [1, 2]]`.
items.statement: def mapWithComplement {α β} (f : α → List α → β) : List α → List β

items.name: List.traverse
items.doc:
Map each element of a `List` to an action, evaluate these actions in order,
and collect the results.
items.statement: protected def traverse [Applicative F] (f : α → F β) : List α → F (List β)

items.name: List.Subperm
items.doc:
`Subperm l₁ l₂`, denoted `l₁ <+~ l₂`, means that `l₁` is a sublist of
a permutation of `l₂`. This is an analogue of `l₁ ⊆ l₂` which respects
multiplicities of elements, and is used for the `≤` relation on multisets.
items.statement: def Subperm (l₁ l₂ : List α) : Prop

items.name: List.isSubperm
items.doc:
`O(|l₁| * (|l₁| + |l₂|))`. Computes whether `l₁` is a sublist of a permutation of `l₂`.
See `isSubperm_iff` for a characterization in terms of `List.Subperm`.
items.statement: def isSubperm [BEq α] (l₁ l₂ : List α) : Bool

items.name: List.insertP
items.doc:
`O(|l|)`. Inserts `a` in `l` right before the first element such that `p` is true, or at the end of
the list if `p` always false on `l`.
items.statement: def insertP (p : α → Bool) (a : α) (l : List α) : List α

items.name: List.dropPrefix?
items.doc:
`dropPrefix? l p` returns
`some r` if `l = p' ++ r` for some `p'` which is paiwise `==` to `p`,
and `none` otherwise.
items.statement: def dropPrefix? [BEq α] : List α → List α → Option (List α)

items.name: List.dropSuffix?
items.doc:
`dropSuffix? l s` returns
`some r` if `l = r ++ s'` for some `s'` which is paiwise `==` to `s`,
and `none` otherwise.
items.statement: def dropSuffix? [BEq α] (l s : List α) : Option (List α)

items.name: List.dropInfix?
items.doc:
`dropInfix? l i` returns
`some (p, s)` if `l = p ++ i' ++ s` for some `i'` which is paiwise `==` to `i`,
and `none` otherwise.

Note that this is an inefficient implementation, and if computation time is a concern you should be
using the Knuth-Morris-Pratt algorithm as implemented in `Batteries.Data.List.Matcher`.
items.statement: def dropInfix? [BEq α] (l i : List α) : Option (List α × List α)

items.name: List.partialSums
items.doc:
Computes the partial sums of the elements of a list.

Examples:

`[a, b, c].partialSums = [0, 0 + a, (0 + a) + b, ((0 + a) + b) + c]`
`[1, 2, 3].partialSums = [0, 1, 3, 6]`
items.statement: def partialSums [Add α] [Zero α] (l : List α) : List α

items.name: List.partialProds
items.doc:
Computes the partial products of the elements of a list.

Examples:

`[a, b, c].partialProds = [1, 1 * a, (1 * a) * b, ((1 * a) * b) * c]`
`[2, 3, 5].partialProds = [1, 2, 6, 30]`
items.statement: def partialProds [Mul α] [One α] (l : List α) : List α

items.name: List.swapAt
items.doc:
`swapAt xs i v` sets position `i` of `xs` to `v` and returns the displaced
element, or `v` itself (with `xs` unchanged) if `i` is out of bounds.
items.statement: def swapAt (xs : List α) (i : Nat) (v : α) : α × List α

items.name: List.swapAtTR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `swapAt`.
items.statement: def swapAtTR (l : List α) (i : Nat) (v : α) : α × List α

items.name: List.swapAt_eq_swapAtTR
items.statement: theorem swapAt_eq_swapAtTR : @swapAt = @swapAtTR

items.name: List.swap
items.doc:
`l.swap i j` exchanges the elements at positions `i` and `j` of `l`.
If either index is out of bounds, `l` is returned unchanged.
items.statement: def swap : List α → Nat → Nat → List α

items.name: List.swapTR
items.doc: Tail-recursive version of `swap`.
items.statement: def swapTR (l : List α) (i j : Nat) : List α

items.name: List.swap_eq_swapTR
items.statement: theorem swap_eq_swapTR : @swap = @swapTR

modules.authors: Parikshit Khanna, Jeremy Avigad, Leonardo de Moura, Floris van Doorn, Mario Carneiro
modules.title: Counting in lists
modules.doc:
This file proves basic properties of `List.countP` and `List.count`, which count the number of
elements of a list satisfying a predicate and equal to a given element respectively. Their
definitions can be found in `Batteries.Data.List.Basic`.

items.name: List.count_singleton'
items.statement: theorem count_singleton' [DecidableEq α] (a b : α) : count a [b] = if b = a then 1 else 0

items.name: List.count_concat
items.statement:
theorem count_concat [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] (a : α) (l : List α) :
    count a (concat l a) = count a l + 1

items.name: List.idxToSigmaCount
items.doc:
`idxToSigmaCount` is essentially a `Fin`-to-`Fin` wrapper for `countBefore` that also
includes the corresponding element.

For example:
```
idxToSigmaCount [5, 1, 3, 2, 4, 0, 1, 4] 5 = ⟨0, 0⟩
```
items.statement:
def idxToSigmaCount [BEq α] [ReflBEq α] (xs : List α) (i : Fin xs.length) :
    (x : α) × Fin (xs.count x)

items.name: List.fst_idxToSigmaCount
items.statement:
theorem fst_idxToSigmaCount [BEq α] [ReflBEq α] {xs: List α} {i : Fin xs.length} :
    (xs.idxToSigmaCount i).1 = xs[i.1]

items.name: List.snd_idxToSigmaCount
items.statement:
theorem snd_idxToSigmaCount [BEq α] [ReflBEq α] {xs: List α} {i : Fin xs.length} :
    (xs.idxToSigmaCount i).2 = ⟨xs.countBefore xs[i.1] i, by grind⟩

items.name: List.coe_snd_idxToSigmaCount
items.statement:
theorem coe_snd_idxToSigmaCount [BEq α] [ReflBEq α] {xs: List α} {i : Fin xs.length} :
    ((xs.idxToSigmaCount i).2 : Nat) = xs.countBefore xs[i.1] i

items.name: List.sigmaCountToIdx
items.doc:
`sigmaCountToIdx` is a `_ × Fin`-to-`Fin` wrapper for `countBefore`.

For example:
```
sigmaCountToIdx [5, 1, 3, 2, 4, 0, 1, 4] ⟨0, 0⟩ = 5
```
items.statement:
def sigmaCountToIdx [BEq α] (xs : List α) (xc : (x : α) × Fin (xs.count x)) :
    Fin xs.length

items.name: List.coe_sigmaCountToIdx
items.statement:
theorem coe_sigmaCountToIdx [BEq α] {xs: List α} {xc : (x : α) × Fin (xs.count x)} :
    (xs.sigmaCountToIdx xc : Nat) = xs.idxOfNth xc.1 xc.2

items.name: List.sigmaCountToIdx_idxToSigmaCount
items.statement:
theorem sigmaCountToIdx_idxToSigmaCount [BEq α] [ReflBEq α] {xs : List α}
    {i : Fin xs.length} : xs.sigmaCountToIdx (xs.idxToSigmaCount i) = i

items.name: List.leftInverse_sigmaCountToIdx_idxToSigmaCount
items.statement:
theorem leftInverse_sigmaCountToIdx_idxToSigmaCount [BEq α] [ReflBEq α] {xs : List α} :
  xs.sigmaCountToIdx.LeftInverse xs.idxToSigmaCount

items.name: List.rightInverse_idxToSigmaCount_sigmaCountToIdx
items.statement:
theorem rightInverse_idxToSigmaCount_sigmaCountToIdx [BEq α] [ReflBEq α] {xs : List α} :
  xs.idxToSigmaCount.RightInverse xs.sigmaCountToIdx

items.name: List.injective_idxToSigmaCount
items.statement:
theorem injective_idxToSigmaCount [BEq α] [ReflBEq α] {xs : List α} :
    xs.idxToSigmaCount.Injective

items.name: List.surjective_sigmaCountToIdx
items.statement:
theorem surjective_sigmaCountToIdx [BEq α] [ReflBEq α] {xs : List α} :
    xs.sigmaCountToIdx.Surjective

items.name: List.idxToSigmaCount_sigmaCountToIdx
items.statement:
theorem idxToSigmaCount_sigmaCountToIdx [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] {xs : List α}
    {xc : (x : α) × Fin (xs.count x)} : xs.idxToSigmaCount (xs.sigmaCountToIdx xc) = xc

items.name: List.leftInverse_idxToSigmaCount_sigmaCountToIdx
items.statement:
theorem leftInverse_idxToSigmaCount_sigmaCountToIdx [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] {xs : List α} :
  xs.idxToSigmaCount.LeftInverse xs.sigmaCountToIdx

items.name: List.rightInverse_sigmaCountToIdx_idxToSigmaCount
items.statement:
theorem rightInverse_sigmaCountToIdx_idxToSigmaCount [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] {xs : List α} :
  xs.sigmaCountToIdx.RightInverse xs.idxToSigmaCount

items.name: List.injective_sigmaCountToIdx
items.statement:
theorem injective_sigmaCountToIdx [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] {xs : List α} :
    xs.sigmaCountToIdx.Injective

items.name: List.surjective_idxToSigmaCount
items.statement:
theorem surjective_idxToSigmaCount [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] {xs : List α} :
    xs.idxToSigmaCount.Surjective

While this file is currently empty, it is intended as a home for any lemmas which are required for
