modules.title: Interleaving lists
modules.doc: This file defines interleaving of lists as an operation.

items.name: List.interleave
items.doc:
Interleave two lists `l₁` and `l₂`, starting with an element of `l₁`.

This operation fully interleave the two lists when the length of `l₁` is either the length of `l₂`
or one more. If one of the lists runs out early, the remainder of the other list is kept without
further interleaving, so that `l₁.interleave l₂` is always a permutation of `l₁ ++ l₂`.
See `interleave_perm_append`.

```
#eval interleave [0, 2, 4] [1] -- [0, 1, 2, 4] -- The second list is too short
#eval interleave [0, 2, 4] [1, 3] -- [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
#eval interleave [0, 2] [1, 3] -- [0, 1, 2, 3]
#eval interleave [0] [1, 3] -- [0, 1, 3] -- The first list is too short
```
items.statement: def interleave : List α → List α → List α

items.name: List.nil_interleave
items.statement: theorem nil_interleave (l₂ : List α) : [].interleave l₂ = l₂

items.name: List.interleave_nil
items.statement: theorem interleave_nil (l₁ : List α) : l₁.interleave [] = l₁

items.name: List.cons_interleave
items.statement:
theorem cons_interleave (a : α) (l₁ : List α) (l₂ : List α) :
    (a :: l₁).interleave l₂ = a :: interleave l₂ l₁

items.name: List.interleave_perm_append
items.statement: theorem interleave_perm_append : ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α}, l₁.interleave l₂ ~ l₁ ++ l₂

items.name: List.interleave_eq_nil
items.statement: theorem interleave_eq_nil : l₁.interleave l₂ = [] ↔ l₁ = [] ∧ l₂ = []

items.name: List.Perm.interleave
items.statement:
protected theorem Perm.interleave (h₁₃ : l₁ ~ l₃) (h₂₄ : l₂ ~ l₄) :
    l₁.interleave l₂ ~ l₃.interleave l₄

items.name: List.length_interleave
items.statement:
theorem length_interleave (l₁ l₂ : List α) :
    (l₁.interleave l₂).length = l₁.length + l₂.length

items.name: List.countP_interleave
items.statement:
theorem countP_interleave (l₁ l₂ : List α) (p : α → Bool) :
    (l₁.interleave l₂).countP p = l₁.countP p + l₂.countP p

items.name: List.count_interleave
items.statement:
theorem count_interleave [BEq α] (l₁ l₂ : List α) (a : α) :
    (l₁.interleave l₂).count a = l₁.count a + l₂.count a

items.name: List.interleave_append_append_of_length_eq_length
items.statement:
theorem interleave_append_append_of_length_eq_length :
    ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α} (_h₁₂ : l₁.length = l₂.length) (l₃ l₄ : List α),
      (l₁ ++ l₃).interleave (l₂ ++ l₄) = l₁.interleave l₂ ++ l₃.interleave l₄

items.name: List.interleave_append_append_of_length_eq_length_add_one
items.statement:
theorem interleave_append_append_of_length_eq_length_add_one :
    ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α} (_h₁₂ : l₁.length = l₂.length + 1) (l₃ l₄ : List α),
      (l₁ ++ l₃).interleave (l₂ ++ l₄) = l₁.interleave l₂ ++ l₄.interleave l₃

items.name: List.interleave_append_left
items.statement:
theorem interleave_append_left :
    ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α} (_h₂₁ : l₂.length ≤ l₁.length) (l₃ : List α),
      (l₁ ++ l₃).interleave l₂ = l₁.interleave l₂ ++ l₃

items.name: List.interleave_append_right
items.statement:
theorem interleave_append_right :
    ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α} (_h₁₂ : l₁.length ≤ l₂.length + 1) (l₃ : List α),
    l₁.interleave (l₂ ++ l₃) = l₁.interleave l₂ ++ l₃

items.name: List.interleave_flatten_flatten_of_length_eq_length
items.statement:
theorem interleave_flatten_flatten_of_length_eq_length :
    ∀ {L₁ L₂ : List (List α)} (h₁₂ : L₁.length = L₂.length),
      (∀ i (hi : i + 1 < L₁.length), length L₁[i] = length L₂[i]) →
        L₁.flatten.interleave L₂.flatten = (zipWith interleave L₁ L₂).flatten

items.name: List.reverse_interleave_of_length_eq_length
items.statement:
theorem reverse_interleave_of_length_eq_length :
    ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α}, l₁.length = l₂.length →
      (l₁.interleave l₂).reverse = l₂.reverse.interleave l₁.reverse

items.name: List.reverse_interleave_of_length_eq_length_add_one
items.statement:
theorem reverse_interleave_of_length_eq_length_add_one :
    ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α}, l₁.length = l₂.length + 1 →
      (l₁.interleave l₂).reverse = l₁.reverse.interleave l₂.reverse

items.name: List.interleave_ofFn_ofFn_even
items.statement:
theorem interleave_ofFn_ofFn_even :
    ∀ {n : Nat} {f g : Fin n → α},
      interleave (ofFn f) (ofFn g) =
        ofFn (n := 2 * n) (fun i => if i.val % 2 = 0 then f ⟨i / 2, by lia⟩ else g ⟨i / 2, by lia⟩)

items.name: List.interleave_ofFn_ofFn_odd
items.statement:
theorem interleave_ofFn_ofFn_odd :
    ∀ {n : Nat} {f : Fin (n + 1) → α} {g : Fin n → α},
      interleave (ofFn f) (ofFn g) =
        ofFn (n := 2 * n + 1)
          (fun i => if hi : i.val % 2 = 0 then f ⟨i / 2, by lia⟩ else g ⟨i / 2, by lia⟩)

items.name: List.right_sublist_interleave
items.statement: theorem right_sublist_interleave : ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α}, l₂ <+ l₁.interleave l₂

items.name: List.left_sublist_interleave
items.statement: theorem left_sublist_interleave : l₁ <+ l₁.interleave l₂

items.name: List.IsPrefix.interleave
items.statement:
protected theorem IsPrefix.interleave  :
    l₁.length = l₂.length ∨ l₁.length = l₂.length + 1 →
    l₁ <+: l₃ → l₂ <+: l₄ → l₁.interleave l₂ <+: l₃.interleave l₄

items.name: List.isEmpty_append
items.statement:
theorem isEmpty_append {xs ys : List α} :
    (xs ++ ys).isEmpty = (xs.isEmpty && ys.isEmpty)

items.name: List.count_getElem_take_succ
items.statement:
theorem count_getElem_take_succ [BEq α] [EquivBEq α] {xs : List α}
    {i : Nat} {hi} : (xs.take (i + 1)).count xs[i] = (xs.take i).count xs[i] + 1

items.name: List.count_getElem_take_lt_count
items.statement:
theorem count_getElem_take_lt_count [BEq α] [EquivBEq α] {xs : List α}

items.name: List.any_congr_mem
items.statement:
theorem any_congr_mem {xs : List α} {p q : α → Bool} (h : ∀ a ∈ xs, p a = q a) :
    xs.any p = xs.any q

items.name: List.find?_zipIdx
items.statement:
theorem find?_zipIdx {xs : List α} {p : α → Bool} {k : Nat} :
    (xs.zipIdx k).find? (fun ⟨x, _⟩ => p x) =
      (xs.findIdx? p).bind fun i => xs[i]?.map (·, i + k)

items.name: List.next?_nil
items.statement: theorem next?_nil : @next? α [] = none

items.name: List.next?_cons
items.statement: theorem next?_cons (a l) : @next? α (a :: l) = some (a, l)

items.name: List.dropLast_eq_eraseIdx
items.statement:
theorem dropLast_eq_eraseIdx {xs : List α} {i : Nat} (last_idx : i + 1 = xs.length) :
    xs.dropLast = List.eraseIdx xs i

items.name: List.set_eq_modify
items.statement: theorem set_eq_modify (a : α) : ∀ n (l : List α), l.set n a = l.modify n (fun _ => a)

items.name: List.set_eq_take_cons_drop
items.statement:
theorem set_eq_take_cons_drop (a : α) {n l} (h : n < length l) :
    set l n a = take n l ++ a :: drop (n + 1) l

items.name: List.modify_eq_set_getElem?
items.statement:
theorem modify_eq_set_getElem? (f : α → α) :
    ∀ n (l : List α), l.modify n f = ((fun a => l.set n (f a)) <$> l[n]?).getD l

items.name: List.modify_eq_set_get
items.statement:
theorem modify_eq_set_get (f : α → α) {n} {l : List α} (h) :
    l.modify n f = l.set n (f (l.get ⟨n, h⟩))

items.name: List.getElem?_set_eq_of_lt
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_set_eq_of_lt (a : α) {n} {l : List α} (h : n < length l) :
    (set l n a)[n]? = some a

items.name: List.getElem?_set_of_lt
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_set_of_lt (a : α) {m n} (l : List α) (h : n < length l) :
    (set l m a)[n]? = if m = n then some a else l[n]?

items.name: List.getElem?_set_of_lt'
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_set_of_lt' (a : α) {m n} (l : List α) (h : m < length l) :
    (set l m a)[n]? = if m = n then some a else l[n]?

items.name: List.length_tail_add_one
items.statement:
theorem length_tail_add_one (l : List α) (h : 0 < length l) :
    (length (tail l)) + 1 = length l

items.name: List.extractP_eq_find?_eraseP
items.statement:
theorem extractP_eq_find?_eraseP
    (l : List α) : extractP p l = (find? p l, eraseP p l)

items.name: List.erase_eq_self_iff_forall_bne
items.statement:
theorem erase_eq_self_iff_forall_bne [BEq α] (a : α) (xs : List α) :
    xs.erase a = xs ↔ ∀ (x : α), x ∈ xs → ¬x == a

items.name: List.replaceF_nil
items.statement: theorem replaceF_nil : [].replaceF p = []

items.name: List.replaceF_cons
items.statement:
theorem replaceF_cons (a : α) (l : List α) :
    (a :: l).replaceF p = match p a with
      | none => a :: replaceF p l
      | some a' => a' :: l

items.name: List.replaceF_cons_of_some
items.statement:
theorem replaceF_cons_of_some {l : List α} (p) (h : p a = some a') :
    (a :: l).replaceF p = a' :: l

items.name: List.replaceF_cons_of_none
items.statement:
theorem replaceF_cons_of_none {l : List α} (p) (h : p a = none) :
    (a :: l).replaceF p = a :: l.replaceF p

items.name: List.replaceF_of_forall_none
items.statement: theorem replaceF_of_forall_none {l : List α} (h : ∀ a, a ∈ l → p a = none) : l.replaceF p = l

items.name: List.exists_of_replaceF
items.statement:
theorem exists_of_replaceF : ∀ {l : List α} {a a'} (_ : a ∈ l) (_ : p a = some a'),
    ∃ a a' l₁ l₂,
      (∀ b ∈ l₁, p b = none) ∧ p a = some a' ∧ l = l₁ ++ a :: l₂ ∧ l.replaceF p = l₁ ++ a' :: l₂

items.name: List.exists_or_eq_self_of_replaceF
items.statement:
theorem exists_or_eq_self_of_replaceF (p) (l : List α) :
    l.replaceF p = l ∨ ∃ a a' l₁ l₂,
      (∀ b ∈ l₁, p b = none) ∧ p a = some a' ∧ l = l₁ ++ a :: l₂ ∧ l.replaceF p = l₁ ++ a' :: l₂

items.name: List.length_replaceF
items.statement: theorem length_replaceF : length (replaceF f l) = length l

items.statement: theorem nil_union (l : List α) : nil ∪ l = l

items.name: List.cons_union
items.statement:
theorem cons_union (a : α) (l₁ l₂ : List α) :
    (a :: l₁) ∪ l₂ = (l₁ ∪ l₂).insert a

items.name: List.mem_union_iff
items.statement:
theorem mem_union_iff [LawfulBEq α] {x : α} {l₁ l₂ : List α} :
    x ∈ l₁ ∪ l₂ ↔ x ∈ l₁ ∨ x ∈ l₂

items.name: List.inter_def
items.statement: theorem inter_def [BEq α] (l₁ l₂ : List α)  : l₁ ∩ l₂ = filter (elem · l₂) l₁

items.name: List.mem_inter_iff
items.statement:
theorem mem_inter_iff [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] {x : α} {l₁ l₂ : List α} :
    x ∈ l₁ ∩ l₂ ↔ x ∈ l₁ ∧ x ∈ l₂

items.name: List.pair_mem_product
items.doc: List.prod satisfies a specification of cartesian product on lists.
items.statement:
theorem pair_mem_product {xs : List α} {ys : List β} {x : α} {y : β} :
    (x, y) ∈ product xs ys ↔ x ∈ xs ∧ y ∈ ys

items.name: List.forIn_eq_bindList
items.statement:
theorem forIn_eq_bindList [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
    (f : α → β → m (ForInStep β)) (l : List α) (init : β) :
    forIn l init f = ForInStep.run <$> (ForInStep.yield init).bindList f l

items.name: List.mapM_eq_ok_iff_forall₂
items.statement:
theorem mapM_eq_ok_iff_forall₂ {f : α → Except ε β} {l : List α} {bs : List β} :
    l.mapM f = .ok bs ↔ Forall₂ (fun a b => f a = .ok b) l bs

items.name: List.exists_mapM_eq_ok_iff
items.statement:
theorem exists_mapM_eq_ok_iff {f : α → Except ε β} {l : List α} :
    (∃ bs, l.mapM f = .ok bs) ↔ ∀ a ∈ l, ∃ b, f a = .ok b

items.name: List.mapM_eq_error_iff
items.doc:
`mapM f` fails with `e` iff some element `a` fails with `e` and every element before it
succeeds; `a` is the first failing element, since `mapM` stops at the first error.
items.statement:
theorem mapM_eq_error_iff {f : α → Except ε β} {l : List α} {e : ε} :
    l.mapM f = .error e ↔
      ∃ l₁ a l₂, l = l₁ ++ a :: l₂ ∧ (∀ x ∈ l₁, ∃ b, f x = .ok b) ∧ f a = .error e

items.name: List.mapM_eq_some_iff_forall₂
items.statement:
theorem mapM_eq_some_iff_forall₂ {f : α → Option β} {l : List α} {bs : List β} :
    l.mapM f = some bs ↔ Forall₂ (fun a b => f a = some b) l bs

items.name: List.exists_mapM_eq_some_iff
items.statement:
theorem exists_mapM_eq_some_iff {f : α → Option β} {l : List α} :
    (∃ bs, l.mapM f = some bs) ↔ ∀ a ∈ l, ∃ b, f a = some b

items.name: List.isSome_mapM
items.statement:
theorem isSome_mapM {f : α → Option β} {l : List α} :
    (l.mapM f).isSome ↔ ∀ a ∈ l, (f a).isSome

items.name: List.mapM_eq_none_iff
items.statement:
theorem mapM_eq_none_iff {f : α → Option β} {l : List α} :
    l.mapM f = none ↔ ∃ a ∈ l, f a = none

items.name: List.allSome_eq_some_iff_forall₂
items.statement:
theorem allSome_eq_some_iff_forall₂ {l : List (Option α)} {as : List α} :
    l.allSome = some as ↔ Forall₂ (fun o a => o = some a) l as

items.name: List.exists_allSome_eq_some_iff
items.statement:
theorem exists_allSome_eq_some_iff {l : List (Option α)} :
    (∃ as, l.allSome = some as) ↔ ∀ o ∈ l, ∃ a, o = some a

items.name: List.allSome_eq_none_iff
items.statement: theorem allSome_eq_none_iff {l : List (Option α)} : l.allSome = none ↔ none ∈ l

items.name: List.diff_cons
items.statement: theorem diff_cons (l₁ l₂ : List α) (a : α) : l₁.diff (a :: l₂) = (l₁.erase a).diff l₂

items.name: List.diff_cons_right
items.statement: theorem diff_cons_right (l₁ l₂ : List α) (a : α) : l₁.diff (a :: l₂) = (l₁.diff l₂).erase a

items.name: List.diff_erase
items.statement: theorem diff_erase (l₁ l₂ : List α) (a : α) : (l₁.diff l₂).erase a = (l₁.erase a).diff l₂

items.name: List.nil_diff
items.statement: theorem nil_diff (l : List α) : [].diff l = []

items.name: List.cons_diff
items.statement:
theorem cons_diff (a : α) (l₁ l₂ : List α) :
    (a :: l₁).diff l₂ = if a ∈ l₂ then l₁.diff (l₂.erase a) else a :: l₁.diff l₂

items.name: List.cons_diff_of_mem
items.statement:
theorem cons_diff_of_mem {a : α} {l₂ : List α} (h : a ∈ l₂) (l₁ : List α) :
    (a :: l₁).diff l₂ = l₁.diff (l₂.erase a)

items.name: List.cons_diff_of_not_mem
items.statement:
theorem cons_diff_of_not_mem {a : α} {l₂ : List α} (h : a ∉ l₂) (l₁ : List α) :
    (a :: l₁).diff l₂ = a :: l₁.diff l₂

items.name: List.diff_eq_foldl
items.statement: theorem diff_eq_foldl : ∀ l₁ l₂ : List α, l₁.diff l₂ = foldl List.erase l₁ l₂

items.name: List.diff_append
items.statement: theorem diff_append (l₁ l₂ l₃ : List α) : l₁.diff (l₂ ++ l₃) = (l₁.diff l₂).diff l₃

items.name: List.diff_sublist
items.statement:
theorem diff_sublist : ∀ l₁ l₂ : List α, l₁.diff l₂ <+ l₁
  | _, [] => .refl _
  | l₁, a :: l₂ =>
    calc
      l₁.diff (a :: l₂) = (l₁.erase a).diff l₂

items.name: List.diff_subset
items.statement: theorem diff_subset (l₁ l₂ : List α) : l₁.diff l₂ ⊆ l₁

items.name: List.mem_diff_of_mem
items.statement: theorem mem_diff_of_mem {a : α} : ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α}, a ∈ l₁ → a ∉ l₂ → a ∈ l₁.diff l₂

items.name: List.Sublist.diff_right
items.statement: theorem Sublist.diff_right : ∀ {l₁ l₂ l₃ : List α}, l₁ <+ l₂ → l₁.diff l₃ <+ l₂.diff l₃

items.name: List.Sublist.erase_diff_erase_sublist

theorem Sublist.erase_diff_erase_sublist {a : α} :
    ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α}, l₁ <+ l₂ → (l₂.erase a).diff (l₁.erase a) <+ l₂.diff l₁

theorem dropInfix?_go_eq_some_iff [BEq α] {i l acc p s : List α} :
    dropInfix?.go i l acc = some (p, s) ↔ ∃ p',
      p = acc.reverse ++ p' ∧
      -- `i` is an infix up to `==`
      (∃ i', l = p' ++ i' ++ s ∧ i' == i) ∧
        -- and there is no shorter prefix for which that is the case
        (∀ p'' i'' s'', l = p'' ++ i'' ++ s'' → i'' == i → p''.length ≥ p'.length)

      (∃ i', l = p ++ i' ++ s ∧ i' == i) ∧
        -- and there is no shorter prefix for which that is the case
        (∀ p' i' s', l = p' ++ i' ++ s' → i' == i → p'.length ≥ p.length)

modules.title: Pairwise relations on a list
modules.doc:
This file provides basic results about `List.Pairwise` and `List.pwFilter` (definitions are in
`Batteries.Data.List.Basic`).
`Pairwise r [a 0, ..., a (n - 1)]` means `∀ i j, i < j → r (a i) (a j)`. For example,
`Pairwise (≠) l` means that all elements of `l` are distinct, and `Pairwise (<) l` means that `l`
is strictly increasing.
`pwFilter r l` is the list obtained by iteratively adding each element of `l` that doesn't break
the pairwiseness of the list we have so far. It thus yields `l'` a maximal sublist of `l` such that
`Pairwise r l'`.

## Tags

sorted, nodup

This file introduces the `List.Perm` relation, which is true if two lists are permutations of one

The notation `~` is used for permutation equivalence.

which exists when we have `xs.Perm ys`: conceptually it represents a permuting of

    L.flatten.length ∈ (L.map length).partialSums

items.name: List.getElem_flatten_aux₁
items.statement:
theorem getElem_flatten_aux₁ (L : List (List α)) (i : Nat) (h : i < L.flatten.length) :
    (L.map length).partialSums.findIdx (· > i) - 1 < L.length

items.name: List.getElem_flatten_aux₂
items.statement:
theorem getElem_flatten_aux₂ (L : List (List α)) (i : Nat) (h : i < L.flatten.length) :
    let j := (L.map length).partialSums.findIdx (· > i) - 1
    have hj : j < L.length := getElem_flatten_aux₁ L i h
    let k := i - (L.take j).flatten.length
    k < L[j].length

items.name: List.getElem_flatten
items.doc:
Indexing into a flattened list: `L.flatten[i]` equals `L[j][k]` where
`j` is the sublist index and `k` is the offset within that sublist.

The indices are computed as:
- `j` is one less than where the cumulative sum first exceeds `i`
- `k` is `i` minus the total length of the first `j` sublists

This theorem states that these indices are in range and the equality holds.
items.statement:
theorem getElem_flatten (L : List (List α)) (i : Nat) (h : i < L.flatten.length) :
    L.flatten[i] =
      let j := (L.map length).partialSums.findIdx (· > i) - 1
      have hj : j < L.length := getElem_flatten_aux₁ L i h
      let k := i - (L.take j).flatten.length
      have hk : k < L[j].length := getElem_flatten_aux₂ L i h
      L[j][k]

and then a public `opaque` wrapper of this implementation, satisfying the specification.

modules.title: Truncate a `MLList` when running out of available heartbeats.

items.name: MLList.whileAtLeastHeartbeatsPercent
items.doc:
Take an initial segment of a monadic lazy list,
stopping when there is less than `percent` of the remaining allowed heartbeats.

If `getMaxHeartbeats` returns `0`, then this passes through the original list unmodified.

The `initial` heartbeat counter is recorded when the first element of the list is requested.
Then each time an element is requested from the wrapped list the heartbeat counter is checked, and
if `current * 100 / initial < percent` then that element is returned,
but no further elements.
items.statement:
def MLList.whileAtLeastHeartbeatsPercent [Monad m] [MonadLiftT CoreM m]
    (L : MLList m α) (percent : Nat := 10) : MLList m α

items.name: Nat.bisect
items.doc:
Given natural numbers `a < b` such that `p a = true` and `p b = false`, `bisect` finds a natural
number `a ≤ c < b` such that `p c = true` and `p (c+1) = false`.
items.statement: def bisect {p : Nat → Bool} (h : start < stop) (hstart : p start = true) (hstop : p stop = false)

items.name: Nat.bisect_lt_stop
items.statement:
theorem bisect_lt_stop {p : Nat → Bool} (h : start < stop) (hstart : p start = true)
    (hstop : p stop = false) : bisect h hstart hstop < stop

items.name: Nat.start_le_bisect
items.statement:
theorem start_le_bisect {p : Nat → Bool} (h : start < stop) (hstart : p start = true)
    (hstop : p stop = false) : start ≤ bisect h hstart hstop

items.name: Nat.bisect_true
items.statement:
theorem bisect_true {p : Nat → Bool} (h : start < stop) (hstart : p start = true)
    (hstop : p stop = false) : p (bisect h hstart hstop) = true

items.name: Nat.bisect_add_one_false
items.statement:
theorem bisect_add_one_false {p : Nat → Bool} (h : start < stop) (hstart : p start = true)
    (hstop : p stop = false) : p (bisect h hstart hstop + 1) = false

modules.title: Bitwise Lemmas
modules.doc:
This module defines properties of the bitwise operations on natural numbers.

This file is complements `Init.Data.Nat.Bitwise.Lemmas` with properties that
are not necessary for the bitvector library.

items.name: Nat.and_self_left
items.statement: theorem and_self_left (a b : Nat) : a &&& (a &&& b) = a &&& b

items.name: Nat.and_self_right
items.statement: theorem and_self_right (a b : Nat) : ((a &&& b) &&& b) = (a &&& b)

items.name: Nat.and_left_comm
items.statement: theorem and_left_comm (x y z : Nat) : x &&& (y &&& z) = y &&& (x &&& z)

items.name: Nat.and_right_comm
items.statement: theorem and_right_comm (x y z : Nat) : (x &&& y) &&& z = (x &&& z) &&& y

items.name: Nat.or_self_left
items.statement: theorem or_self_left (a b : Nat) : a ||| (a ||| b) = a ||| b

items.name: Nat.or_self_right
items.statement: theorem or_self_right (a b : Nat) : (a ||| b) ||| b = a ||| b

items.name: Nat.or_left_comm
items.statement: theorem or_left_comm (x y z : Nat) : x ||| (y ||| z) = y ||| (x ||| z)

items.name: Nat.or_right_comm
items.statement: theorem or_right_comm (x y z : Nat) : (x ||| y) ||| z = (x ||| z) ||| y

items.name: Nat.xor_left_comm
items.statement: theorem xor_left_comm (x y z : Nat) : x ^^^ (y ^^^ z) = y ^^^ (x ^^^ z)

items.name: Nat.xor_right_comm
items.statement: theorem xor_right_comm (x y z : Nat) : (x ^^^ y) ^^^ z = (x ^^^ z) ^^^ y

items.name: Nat.xor_xor_cancel_left
items.statement: theorem xor_xor_cancel_left (x y : Nat) : x ^^^ (x ^^^ y) = y

items.name: Nat.xor_xor_cancel_right
items.statement: theorem xor_xor_cancel_right (x y : Nat) : (x ^^^ y) ^^^ y = x

items.name: Nat.eq_of_xor_eq_zero
items.statement: theorem eq_of_xor_eq_zero {x y : Nat} : x ^^^ y = 0 → x = y

items.name: Nat.xor_eq_zero_iff
items.statement: theorem xor_eq_zero_iff {x y : Nat} : x ^^^ y = 0 ↔ x = y

items.name: Nat.xor_ne_zero_iff
items.statement: theorem xor_ne_zero_iff {x y : Nat} : x ^^^ y ≠ 0 ↔ x ≠ y

items.name: Nat.xor_right_injective
items.statement: theorem xor_right_injective {x : Nat} : Function.Injective (x ^^^ ·)

items.name: Nat.xor_left_injective
items.statement: theorem xor_left_injective {x : Nat} : Function.Injective (· ^^^ x)

items.name: Nat.xor_right_inj
items.statement: theorem xor_right_inj {x y z : Nat} : x ^^^ y = x ^^^ z ↔ y = z

items.name: Nat.xor_left_inj
items.statement: theorem xor_left_inj {x y z : Nat} : x ^^^ z = y ^^^ z ↔ x = y

modules.title: Digits
modules.doc:
Conversions between natural numbers and big-endian or little-endian lists of digits in a given
base. The digits are represented as elements of `Fin base`.

The definitions are simple specifications. They are replaced at runtime, using `csimp`, by
divide-and-conquer implementations, which are subquadratic when combined with the subquadratic
multiplication and division of `Nat`.

items.name: Nat.ofFinDigits
items.doc:
Construct a natural number from a big-endian list of digits in the given base:
```
ofFinDigits (base := 10) [2,3,4] = 234 -- 2*10^2 + 3*10^1 + 4*10^0
ofFinDigits (base := 2) [0,1,0,0] = 4 -- 0*2^3 + 1*2^2 + 0*2^1 + 0*2^0
ofFinDigits (base := b) [] = 0 -- any base, including "base 0" and "base 1"
```
There are no valid inputs other than `[]` in "base 0". In "base 1", the only valid digit is `0`
and therefore `ofFinDigits (base := 1) l = 0`.
items.statement: public def ofFinDigits (l : List (Fin base)) : Nat

items.name: Nat.ofFinDigitsRev
items.doc:
Construct a natural number from a little-endian list of digits in the given base:
```
ofFinDigitsRev (base := 10) [4,3,2] = 234 -- 2*10^2 + 3*10^1 + 4*10^0
ofFinDigitsRev (base := 2) [0,0,1,0] = 4 -- 0*2^3 + 1*2^2 + 0*2^1 + 0*2^0
ofFinDigitsRev (base := b) [] = 0 -- any base, including "base 0" and "base 1"
```
There are no valid inputs other than `[]` in "base 0". In "base 1", the only valid digit is `0`
and therefore `ofFinDigitsRev (base := 1) l = 0`.
items.statement: public def ofFinDigitsRev (l : List (Fin base)) : Nat

items.name: Nat.toFinDigitsFixed
items.doc:
The `prec` least significant digits of `n` in the given `base`, listed in big-endian order.

Only "base 0" is invalid, this is ensured by a `NeZero base` instance. In "base 1" the result is
always a list of `0`s with length `prec`.
```
toFinDigitsFixed 123 10 3 = ([1,2,3] : List (Fin 10))
toFinDigitsFixed 123 10 2 = ([2,3] : List (Fin 10))
toFinDigitsFixed 4 2 4 = ([0,1,0,0] : List (Fin 2))
toFinDigitsFixed 12345 1 5 = ([0,0,0,0,0] : List (Fin 1))
```
items.statement: public def toFinDigitsFixed (n base prec : Nat) [NeZero base] : List (Fin base)

items.name: Nat.toFinDigitsFixedRev
items.doc:
The `prec` least significant digits of `n` in the given `base`, listed in little-endian order.

Only "base 0" is invalid, this is ensured by a `NeZero base` instance. In "base 1" the result is
always a list of `0`s with length `prec`.
```
toFinDigitsFixedRev 123 10 3 = ([3,2,1] : List (Fin 10))
toFinDigitsFixedRev 123 10 2 = ([3,2] : List (Fin 10))
toFinDigitsFixedRev 4 2 4 = ([0,0,1,0] : List (Fin 2))
toFinDigitsFixedRev 12345 1 5 = ([0,0,0,0,0] : List (Fin 1))
```
items.statement: public def toFinDigitsFixedRev (n base prec : Nat) [NeZero base] : List (Fin base)

items.name: Nat.toFinDigits
items.doc:
Big-endian list of digits of a natural number `n` in a given `base`.

When `n` is zero, the result is the empty list. Otherwise, the most significant digit is nonzero.
The base should be at least 2, the result is always the empty list in "base 0" and "base 1".
```
toFinDigits 123 10 = ([1,2,3] : List (Fin 10))
toFinDigits 4 2 = ([1,0,0] : List (Fin 2))
toFinDigits 0 12345 = ([] : List (Fin 12345))
```
items.statement: public def toFinDigits (n base : Nat) : List (Fin base)

items.name: Nat.toFinDigitsRev
items.doc:
Little-endian list of digits of a natural number `n` in a given `base`.

When `n` is zero, the result is the empty list. Otherwise, the most significant digit is nonzero.
The base should be at least 2, the result is always the empty list in "base 0" and "base 1".
```
toFinDigitsRev 123 10 = ([3,2,1] : List (Fin 10))
toFinDigitsRev 4 2 = ([0,0,1] : List (Fin 2))
toFinDigitsRev 0 12345 = ([] : List (Fin 12345))
```
items.statement: public def toFinDigitsRev (n base : Nat) : List (Fin base)

items.name: Nat.toFinDigitsRev_eq_reverse_toFinDigits
items.statement:
public theorem toFinDigitsRev_eq_reverse_toFinDigits (n : Nat) :
    n.toFinDigitsRev base = (n.toFinDigits base).reverse

items.name: Nat.toFinDigitsFixedRev_eq_reverse_toFinDigitsFixed
items.statement:
public theorem toFinDigitsFixedRev_eq_reverse_toFinDigitsFixed [NeZero base] (n : Nat) :
    n.toFinDigitsFixedRev base prec = (n.toFinDigitsFixed base prec).reverse

items.name: Nat.ofFinDigitsRev_eq_ofFinDigits_reverse
items.statement:
public theorem ofFinDigitsRev_eq_ofFinDigits_reverse (l : List (Fin base)) :
    ofFinDigitsRev l = ofFinDigits l.reverse

items.name: Nat.ofFinDigits_nil
items.statement: public theorem ofFinDigits_nil : ofFinDigits (base := base) [] = 0

items.name: Nat.ofFinDigits_append
items.statement:
public theorem ofFinDigits_append {l₁ l₂ : List (Fin base)} :
    ofFinDigits (l₁ ++ l₂) = ofFinDigits l₁ * base ^ l₂.length + ofFinDigits l₂

items.name: Nat.ofFinDigits_cons
items.statement:
public theorem ofFinDigits_cons {l : List (Fin base)} :
    ofFinDigits (d :: l) = d * base ^ l.length + ofFinDigits l

items.name: Nat.toFinDigitsFixed_zero
items.statement:
public theorem toFinDigitsFixed_zero [NeZero base] :
    toFinDigitsFixed n base 0 = []

items.name: Nat.toFinDigitsFixed_succ
Nat.length_toFinDigitsFixed
items.statement:
public theorem length_toFinDigitsFixed [NeZero base] :
    (toFinDigitsFixed n base prec).length = prec

items.name: Nat.ofFinDigits_toFinDigitsFixed
items.statement:
public theorem ofFinDigits_toFinDigitsFixed [NeZero base] :
    ofFinDigits (toFinDigitsFixed n base prec) = n % base ^ prec

items.name: Nat.toFinDigitsFixed_add
items.statement:
public theorem toFinDigitsFixed_add [NeZero base] : toFinDigitsFixed n base (prec + k) =
    toFinDigitsFixed (n / base ^ k) base prec ++ toFinDigitsFixed (n % base ^ k) base k

items.name: Nat.toFinDigits_zero
items.statement: public theorem toFinDigits_zero : toFinDigits 0 base = []

items.name: Nat.toFinDigits_of_ne_zero
items.statement:
public theorem toFinDigits_of_ne_zero (h : 2 ≤ base) [NeZero base] (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    toFinDigits n base = toFinDigits (n / base) base ++ [Fin.ofNat base n]

items.name: Nat.ofFinDigits_toFinDigits
items.statement:
public theorem ofFinDigits_toFinDigits (h : 2 ≤ base) :
    ofFinDigits (toFinDigits n base) = n

items.name: Nat.toFinDigits_eq_append
Nat.ofFinDigits_of_le_one
items.doc: In "base 0" and "base 1", the only valid digits are zeros and `ofFinDigits` is always `0`.
items.statement:
public theorem ofFinDigits_of_le_one (h : base ≤ 1) {l : List (Fin base)} :
    ofFinDigits l = 0

items.name: Nat.toFinDigitsFixed_one
items.doc: In "base 1", `toFinDigitsFixed` is a list of zeros.
items.statement: public theorem toFinDigitsFixed_one : toFinDigitsFixed n 1 prec = List.replicate prec 0

items.name: Nat.ofFinDigits_lt_pow
items.statement: public theorem ofFinDigits_lt_pow {l : List (Fin base)} : ofFinDigits l < base ^ l.length

items.name: Nat.toFinDigitsFixed_ofFinDigits
items.statement:
public theorem toFinDigitsFixed_ofFinDigits [NeZero base] {l : List (Fin base)} :
    toFinDigitsFixed (ofFinDigits l) base l.length = l

items.name: Nat.toFinDigits_of_lt_two
items.doc: In "base 0" and "base 1", `toFinDigits` is always the empty list.
items.statement: public theorem toFinDigits_of_lt_two (h : base < 2) : toFinDigits n base = []

items.name: Nat.toFinDigits_eq_nil_iff
items.statement: public theorem toFinDigits_eq_nil_iff : toFinDigits n base = [] ↔ n = 0 ∨ base < 2

items.name: Nat.toFinDigits_head?_ne_zero
items.doc: The most significant digit of `toFinDigits n base` is nonzero.
items.statement: public theorem toFinDigits_head?_ne_zero : ∀ d ∈ (toFinDigits n base).head?, d.val ≠ 0

items.name: Nat.toFinDigits_ofFinDigits
items.statement:
public theorem toFinDigits_ofFinDigits (h : 2 ≤ base) {l : List (Fin base)}
    (hl : ∀ d ∈ l.head?, d.val ≠ 0) : toFinDigits (ofFinDigits l) base = l

items.note:
### Subquadratic implementations

The definitions and theorems in the `Nat.Internal` namespace implement the functions above at
runtime via `csimp`. They are public only because `csimp` requires it. They are not intended as part
of the public API and they may change without warning.

Each implementation splits its input roughly in half and falls back to a simple loop on small
inputs, where computing `base ^ k` and splitting would cost more than it saves. The cutoffs are
16 digits for `ofFinDigits` and `toFinDigitsFixed`, and a split size of at least 8 digits for
`toFinDigits`. They were picked by judgment rather than tuned by benchmarks. Correctness does not
depend on them.

items.name: Nat.Internal.ofFinDigits
items.doc: Divide-and-conquer implementation of `Nat.ofFinDigits`.
items.statement: public def ofFinDigits (l : List (Fin base)) : Nat

items.name: Nat.Internal.ofFinDigits_eq
items.statement: public theorem ofFinDigits_eq : @Nat.ofFinDigits = @ofFinDigits

items.name: Nat.Internal.toFinDigitsFixed
items.doc: Divide-and-conquer implementation of `Nat.toFinDigitsFixed`.
items.statement: public def toFinDigitsFixed (n base prec : Nat) [NeZero base] : List (Fin base)

items.name: Nat.Internal.toFinDigitsFixed_eq
items.statement: public theorem toFinDigitsFixed_eq : @Nat.toFinDigitsFixed = @toFinDigitsFixed

items.name: Nat.Internal.toFinDigits
items.doc: Divide-and-conquer implementation of `Nat.toFinDigits`.
items.statement: public def toFinDigits (n base : Nat) : List (Fin base)

items.name: Nat.Internal.toFinDigits_eq
items.statement: public theorem toFinDigits_eq : @Nat.toFinDigits = @toFinDigits

modules.authors: Leonardo de Moura, Jeremy Avigad, Mario Carneiro
modules.title: Basic lemmas about natural numbers
modules.doc:
The primary purpose of the lemmas in this file is to assist with reasoning
about sizes of objects, array indices and such. For a more thorough development
of the theory of natural numbers, we recommend using Mathlib.

items.name: Nat.recAux_zero
items.statement:
theorem recAux_zero {motive : Nat → Sort _} (zero : motive 0)
    (succ : ∀ n, motive n → motive (n+1)) :
    Nat.recAux zero succ 0 = zero

items.name: Nat.recAux_succ
items.statement:
theorem recAux_succ {motive : Nat → Sort _} (zero : motive 0)
    (succ : ∀ n, motive n → motive (n+1)) (n) :
    Nat.recAux zero succ (n+1) = succ n (Nat.recAux zero succ n)

items.name: Nat.recAuxOn_zero
items.statement:
theorem recAuxOn_zero {motive : Nat → Sort _} (zero : motive 0)
    (succ : ∀ n, motive n → motive (n+1)) :
    Nat.recAuxOn 0 zero succ = zero

items.name: Nat.recAuxOn_succ
items.statement:
theorem recAuxOn_succ {motive : Nat → Sort _} (zero : motive 0)
    (succ : ∀ n, motive n → motive (n+1)) (n) :
    Nat.recAuxOn (n+1) zero succ = succ n (Nat.recAuxOn n zero succ)

items.name: Nat.casesAuxOn_zero
items.statement:
theorem casesAuxOn_zero {motive : Nat → Sort _} (zero : motive 0)
    (succ : ∀ n, motive (n+1)) :
    Nat.casesAuxOn 0 zero succ = zero

items.name: Nat.casesAuxOn_succ
items.statement:
theorem casesAuxOn_succ {motive : Nat → Sort _} (zero : motive 0)
    (succ : ∀ n, motive (n+1)) (n) :
    Nat.casesAuxOn (n+1) zero succ = succ n

items.name: Nat.strongRec_eq
items.statement:
theorem strongRec_eq {motive : Nat → Sort _} (ind : ∀ n, (∀ m, m < n → motive m) → motive n)
    (t : Nat) : Nat.strongRec ind t = ind t fun m _ => Nat.strongRec ind m

items.name: Nat.strongRecOn_eq
items.statement:
theorem strongRecOn_eq {motive : Nat → Sort _} (ind : ∀ n, (∀ m, m < n → motive m) → motive n)
    (t : Nat) : Nat.strongRecOn t ind = ind t fun m _ => Nat.strongRecOn m ind

items.name: Nat.recDiagAux_zero_left
items.statement:
theorem recDiagAux_zero_left {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _}
    (zero_left : ∀ n, motive 0 n) (zero_right : ∀ m, motive m 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) (n) :
    Nat.recDiagAux zero_left zero_right succ_succ 0 n = zero_left n

items.name: Nat.recDiagAux_zero_right
items.statement:
theorem recDiagAux_zero_right {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _}
    (zero_left : ∀ n, motive 0 n) (zero_right : ∀ m, motive m 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) (m)
    (h : zero_left 0 = zero_right 0 := by first | assumption | trivial) :
    Nat.recDiagAux zero_left zero_right succ_succ m 0 = zero_right m

items.name: Nat.recDiagAux_succ_succ
items.statement:
theorem recDiagAux_succ_succ {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _}
    (zero_left : ∀ n, motive 0 n) (zero_right : ∀ m, motive m 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) (m n) :
    Nat.recDiagAux zero_left zero_right succ_succ (m+1) (n+1)
      = succ_succ m n (Nat.recDiagAux zero_left zero_right succ_succ m n)

items.name: Nat.recDiag_zero_zero
items.statement:
theorem recDiag_zero_zero {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 n → motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive m 0 → motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) :
    Nat.recDiag (motive:=motive) zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ 0 0 = zero_zero

items.name: Nat.recDiag_zero_succ
items.statement:
theorem recDiag_zero_succ {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 n → motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive m 0 → motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) (n) :
    Nat.recDiag zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ 0 (n+1)
      = zero_succ n (Nat.recDiag zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ 0 n)

items.name: Nat.recDiag_succ_zero
items.statement:
theorem recDiag_succ_zero {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 n → motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive m 0 → motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) (m) :
    Nat.recDiag zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ (m+1) 0
      = succ_zero m (Nat.recDiag zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ m 0)

items.name: Nat.recDiag_succ_succ
items.statement:
theorem recDiag_succ_succ {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 n → motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive m 0 → motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) (m n) :
    Nat.recDiag zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ (m+1) (n+1)
      = succ_succ m n (Nat.recDiag zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ m n)

items.name: Nat.recDiagOn_zero_zero
items.statement:
theorem recDiagOn_zero_zero {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 n → motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive m 0 → motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) :
    Nat.recDiagOn (motive:=motive) 0 0 zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ = zero_zero

items.name: Nat.recDiagOn_zero_succ
items.statement:
theorem recDiagOn_zero_succ {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 n → motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive m 0 → motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) (n) :
    Nat.recDiagOn 0 (n+1) zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ
      = zero_succ n (Nat.recDiagOn 0 n zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ)

items.name: Nat.recDiagOn_succ_zero
items.statement:
theorem recDiagOn_succ_zero {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 n → motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive m 0 → motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) (m) :
    Nat.recDiagOn (m+1) 0 zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ
      = succ_zero m (Nat.recDiagOn m 0 zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ)

items.name: Nat.recDiagOn_succ_succ
items.statement:
theorem recDiagOn_succ_succ {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 n → motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive m 0 → motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive m n → motive (m+1) (n+1)) (m n) :
    Nat.recDiagOn (m+1) (n+1) zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ
      = succ_succ m n (Nat.recDiagOn m n zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ)

items.name: Nat.casesDiagOn_zero_zero
items.statement:
theorem casesDiagOn_zero_zero {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive (m+1) (n+1)) :
    Nat.casesDiagOn 0 0 (motive:=motive) zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ = zero_zero

items.name: Nat.casesDiagOn_zero_succ
items.statement:
theorem casesDiagOn_zero_succ {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive (m+1) (n+1)) (n) :
    Nat.casesDiagOn 0 (n+1) zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ = zero_succ n

items.name: Nat.casesDiagOn_succ_zero
items.statement:
theorem casesDiagOn_succ_zero {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive (m+1) (n+1)) (m) :
    Nat.casesDiagOn (m+1) 0 zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ = succ_zero m

items.name: Nat.casesDiagOn_succ_succ
items.statement:
theorem casesDiagOn_succ_succ {motive : Nat → Nat → Sort _} (zero_zero : motive 0 0)
    (zero_succ : ∀ n, motive 0 (n+1)) (succ_zero : ∀ m, motive (m+1) 0)
    (succ_succ : ∀ m n, motive (m+1) (n+1)) (m n) :
    Nat.casesDiagOn (m+1) (n+1) zero_zero zero_succ succ_zero succ_succ = succ_succ m n

items.name: Nat.lt_sum_ge
items.doc: Strong case analysis on `a < b ∨ b ≤ a`
items.statement: protected def lt_sum_ge (a b : Nat) : a < b ⊕' b ≤ a

items.name: Nat.sum_trichotomy
items.doc: Strong case analysis on `a < b ∨ a = b ∨ b < a`
items.statement: protected def sum_trichotomy (a b : Nat) : a < b ⊕' a = b ⊕' b < a

items.name: Nat.div_le_div_of_lt
items.statement: theorem div_le_div_of_lt {a b : Nat} (n : Nat) (h : a < b) : a / n ≤ b / n

items.name: Nat.le_of_div_lt_div
items.statement: theorem le_of_div_lt_div {n a b : Nat} (h : a / n < b / n) : a ≤ b

items.name: Nat.mod_lt_mod_of_lt_of_div_eq
items.statement:
theorem mod_lt_mod_of_lt_of_div_eq {n a b : Nat} (h : a < b) (h0 : a / n = b / n) :
    a % n < b % n

items.name: Nat.mod_le_mod_of_le_of_div_eq
items.statement:
theorem mod_le_mod_of_le_of_div_eq {n a b : Nat} (h : a ≤ b) (h0 : a / n = b / n) :
    a % n ≤ b % n

items.name: Nat.lt_of_div_eq_of_mod_lt
items.statement: theorem lt_of_div_eq_of_mod_lt {n a b : Nat} (h0 : a / n = b / n) (h1 : a % n < b % n) : a < b

items.name: Nat.le_of_div_eq_of_mod_le
items.statement: theorem le_of_div_eq_of_mod_le {n a b : Nat} (h0 : a / n = b / n) (h1 : a % n ≤ b % n) : a ≤ b

items.name: Nat.lt_div_mod_iff
items.statement:
theorem lt_div_mod_iff (n a b : Nat) :
    a < b ↔ a / n < b / n ∨ a / n = b / n ∧ a % n < b % n

items.name: Nat.le_div_mod_iff
items.statement:
theorem le_div_mod_iff (n a b : Nat) :
    a ≤ b ↔ a / n < b / n ∨ a / n = b / n ∧ a % n ≤ b % n

items.name: Nat.mkDivMod_def
items.statement: theorem mkDivMod_def (i : Nat) {n} (j : Fin n) : mkDivMod i j = n * i + j

items.name: Nat.div_mkDivMod
items.statement:
theorem div_mkDivMod (i : Nat) {n} (j : Fin n) :
    mkDivMod i j / n = i

items.name: Nat.mod_mkDivMod
items.statement:
theorem mod_mkDivMod (i : Nat) {n} (j : Fin n) :
    mkDivMod i j % n = j

items.name: Nat.cast_mkDivMod
items.statement:
theorem cast_mkDivMod (i : Nat) {n : Nat} (j : Fin n) :
    haveI : NeZero n := ⟨Nat.ne_zero_of_lt j.isLt⟩
    (mkDivMod i j : Fin n) = j

items.name: Nat.mkDivMod_div_add_mod
items.statement:
theorem mkDivMod_div_add_mod (k : Nat) {n} (j : Fin n) :
    mkDivMod (k / n) j + k % n = k + j

items.name: Nat.mkDivMod_div
items.statement: theorem mkDivMod_div (k : Nat) {n} (j : Fin n) : mkDivMod (k / n) j = k + j - k % n

items.name: Nat.mkDivMod_div_cast
items.statement:
theorem mkDivMod_div_cast (k : Nat) {n : Nat} [NeZero n] :
    mkDivMod (k / n) (k : Fin n) = k

items.name: Nat.mul_le_mkDivMod
items.statement: theorem mul_le_mkDivMod (i : Nat) {n} (j : Fin n) : n * i ≤ mkDivMod i j

items.name: Nat.mkDivMod_lt_mul_succ
items.statement: theorem mkDivMod_lt_mul_succ (i : Nat) {n} (j : Fin n) : mkDivMod i j < n * (i + 1)

items.name: Nat.mkDivMod_lt_mul_of_lt
items.statement: theorem mkDivMod_lt_mul_of_lt {i m : Nat} {n} (h : i < m) (j : Fin n) : mkDivMod i j < m * n

items.name: Nat.mkDivMod_inj
items.statement:
theorem mkDivMod_inj {i₁ i₂ : Nat} {n} {j₁ j₂ : Fin n} :
    mkDivMod i₁ j₁ = mkDivMod i₂ j₂ ↔ i₁ = i₂ ∧ j₁ = j₂

items.name: Nat.mkDivMod_lt_mkDivMod_iff
items.statement:
theorem mkDivMod_lt_mkDivMod_iff {i₁ i₂ : Nat} {n} {j₁ j₂ : Fin n} :
    mkDivMod i₁ j₁ < mkDivMod i₂ j₂ ↔ i₁ < i₂ ∨ i₁ = i₂ ∧ j₁ < j₂

items.name: Nat.mkDivMod_le_mkDivMod_iff
items.statement:
theorem mkDivMod_le_mkDivMod_iff {i₁ i₂ : Nat} {n} {j₁ j₂ : Fin n} :
    mkDivMod i₁ j₁ ≤ mkDivMod i₂ j₂ ↔ i₁ < i₂ ∨ i₁ = i₂ ∧ j₁ ≤ j₂

items.name: Nat.ofBits_zero
items.statement: theorem ofBits_zero (f : Fin 0 → Bool) : ofBits f = 0

items.name: Nat.ofBits_succ
items.statement: theorem ofBits_succ (f : Fin (n+1) → Bool) : ofBits f = 2 * ofBits (f ∘ Fin.succ) + (f 0).toNat

items.name: Nat.ofBits_lt_two_pow
items.statement: theorem ofBits_lt_two_pow (f : Fin n → Bool) : ofBits f < 2 ^ n

items.name: Nat.testBit_ofBits_lt

items.name: Nat.testBit_ofBits_ge
items.statement:
theorem testBit_ofBits_ge (f : Fin n → Bool) (i : Nat) (h : n ≤ i) :
    (ofBits f).testBit i = false

items.name: Nat.testBit_ofBits
items.statement:
theorem testBit_ofBits (f : Fin n → Bool) :
    (ofBits f).testBit i = if h : i < n then f ⟨i, h⟩ else false

items.name: Nat.ofBits_testBit
items.statement: theorem ofBits_testBit (x n) : ofBits (fun i : Fin n => x.testBit i) = x % 2 ^ n

items.name: Nat.toString_append_toString

theorem toString_append_toString (a b : Nat) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    toString a ++ toString b = toString (a * 10 ^ (toString b).length + b)

theorem mul_add_lt_mul_of_lt_of_lt {m n x y : Nat} (hx : x < m) (hy : y < n) :
