    x + m * y < m * n

modules.title: Ordered association lists
modules.doc:
`OrderedAssocList` is a wrapper around `AssocList`,
with the additional invariant that the keys are in strictly increasing order.

As a consequence, an `OrderedAssocList` is determined by the lookup function `l[x]?`, that is
`(∀ a, l₁[a]? = l₂[a]?) → l₁ = l₂`
and this makes proving identities between operations much easier than with `AssocList`.

As the operations on `OrderedAssocList` are defined in terms of `AssocList`,
they evaluate in the kernel, but inherit the `O(n)` time complexity
(i.e. are not suitable for large data). Their advantage relative to an ordered map is the
simple extensionality property above.

We will later add another wrapper requiring that a "default" value does not appear,
so e.g. finitely supported functions can be uniquely represented.

The main operations defined are:
* `l[x]?`, which linearly searches the list, stopping if the keys get too large.
* `insert`, which inserts a new key-value pair, maintaining the order invariant.
* `filterMapVal f`, for `f : α → β → Option γ`, which applies a function to values,
  dropping some values.
* `merge f` for `f : α → Option β → Option γ → Option δ` which merges two lists,
  dropping some values. It runs in time `O(l₁.length + l₂.length)`.

items.note:
We first define some predicates and operations in the `AssocList` namespace.

* `KeysOrdered cmp l` asserts that the keys of an `l : AssocList` are strictly increasing
  with respect to a comparator `cmp`.
* `LTHeadKey cmp a l` asserts that `a` is less than (according to `cmp`) the first key of `l`,
  or that `l` is empty.

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.headKey?
items.doc: The head key of an `AssocList`, or `none` if the list is empty.
items.statement: def headKey? (l : AssocList α β) : Option α

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.headKey?_nil
items.statement: theorem headKey?_nil : headKey? (.nil : AssocList α β) = none

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.headKey?_cons
items.statement: theorem headKey?_cons : headKey? (.cons a b t) = some a

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.headKey?_eq_head?
items.statement: theorem headKey?_eq_head? (l : AssocList α β) : l.headKey? = l.toList.head?.map Prod.fst

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.LTHeadKey
items.doc: The condition that an element is less than the first key of an `AssocList`, or that list is empty.
items.statement: abbrev LTHeadKey (cmp : α → α → Ordering) (a : α) (t : AssocList α β) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.ltHeadKey_nil
items.statement:
theorem ltHeadKey_nil {cmp : α → α → Ordering} :
    LTHeadKey cmp a (.nil : AssocList α β) = True

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.ltHeadKey_cons
items.statement: theorem ltHeadKey_cons : LTHeadKey cmp a (.cons x y t) = (cmp a x = .lt)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.ltHeadKey_iff
items.statement:
theorem ltHeadKey_iff {l : AssocList α β} :
    LTHeadKey cmp a l ↔ ∀ p ∈ l.toList.head?, cmp a p.1 = .lt

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.KeysOrdered
items.doc:
The predicate that the keys of an `AssocList` are
in strictly increasing order according to the comparator `cmp`.
items.statement: def KeysOrdered (cmp : α → α → Ordering) : AssocList α β → Prop

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.keysOrdered_cons_nil
items.statement: theorem keysOrdered_cons_nil : KeysOrdered cmp (.cons a b nil)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.keysOrdered_iff_pairwise
Batteries.AssocList.KeysOrdered.tail
items.statement: theorem KeysOrdered.tail (h : KeysOrdered cmp (.cons a b t)) : KeysOrdered cmp t

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.KeysOrdered.lt_of_mem
items.statement:
theorem KeysOrdered.lt_of_mem {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [TransCmp cmp]
    {x : α} {y : β} {t : AssocList α β} (h : KeysOrdered cmp (cons x y t))
    {p : α × β} (hp : p ∈ t.toList) : cmp x p.1 = .lt

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.KeysOrdered.ltHeadKey
items.statement: theorem KeysOrdered.ltHeadKey (w : KeysOrdered cmp (cons a b t)) : LTHeadKey cmp a t

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.ltHeadKey_of_cons
items.statement:
theorem ltHeadKey_of_cons [TransCmp cmp] (w : LTHeadKey cmp a (cons x y t))
    (h : KeysOrdered cmp (cons x y t)) :
    LTHeadKey cmp a t

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.ltHeadKey_of_le
items.statement:
theorem ltHeadKey_of_le [TransCmp cmp] (h : cmp x a ≠ .gt) (w : LTHeadKey cmp a t) :
    LTHeadKey cmp x t

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.LEHeadKey
items.doc:
A relation on two `AssocList`s, asserting that the head key of the first list is at most
the head key of the second list, or that the second list is empty.
items.statement:
abbrev LEHeadKey
    (cmp : α → α → Ordering) (s : AssocList α β) (t : AssocList α γ) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.leHeadKey_cons_cons
items.statement:
theorem leHeadKey_cons_cons :
    LEHeadKey cmp (cons a b t) (cons x y s) = (cmp a x ≠ .gt)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.leHeadKey_iff
items.statement:
theorem leHeadKey_iff {s : AssocList α β} {t : AssocList α γ} :
    LEHeadKey cmp s t ↔ ∀ q ∈ t.toList.head?, ∃ p ∈ s.toList.head?, cmp p.1 q.1 ≠ .gt

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.ltHeadKey_of_leHeadKey
items.statement:
theorem ltHeadKey_of_leHeadKey [TransCmp cmp]
    (w : LTHeadKey cmp a s) (h : LEHeadKey cmp s t) :
    LTHeadKey cmp a t

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.leHeadKey_cons
items.statement:
theorem leHeadKey_cons [TransCmp cmp]
    (h : KeysOrdered cmp (cons x y t)) (w : LEHeadKey cmp t s) :
    LEHeadKey cmp (cons x y t) s

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.KeysOrdered.cons
Batteries.AssocList.find?_eq_none_of_ltHeadKey
items.statement:
theorem find?_eq_none_of_ltHeadKey {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [TransCmp cmp] [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
    (w : LTHeadKey cmp a l) (h : KeysOrdered cmp l) :
    l.find? a = none

items.note:
# Ordered-respecting operations on `AssocList`

We now define `orderedInsert`, and `orderedMerge`,
which will later be wrapped as `OrderedAssocList.insert` and `OrderedAssocList.merge`.

We prove that with `KeysOrdered` input these functions produce `KeysOrdered` outputs.
We prove the same about `AssocList.filterMapVal`.

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedInsert
items.doc:
Insert a key-value pair into an `AssocList`,
in such a way that if the original list has keys in increasing order,
so does the result.
(Otherwise, it is inserted before the first key the new key is smaller than,
or replaces the first key the new key is equal to.)

We later wrap this as `OrderedAssocList.insert`.
items.statement: def orderedInsert (cmp : α → α → Ordering) (l : AssocList α β) (a : α) (b : β) : AssocList α β

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedInsert_nil
items.statement: theorem orderedInsert_nil : (nil : AssocList α β).orderedInsert cmp a b = .cons a b nil

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedInsert_cons
items.statement:
theorem orderedInsert_cons :
    orderedInsert cmp (.cons x y t) a b = match _w : cmp a x with
    | .lt => .cons a b (.cons x y t)
    | .eq => .cons a b t
    | .gt => .cons x y (orderedInsert cmp t a b)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.headKey?_orderedInsert
items.statement:
theorem headKey?_orderedInsert {l : AssocList α β} :
    headKey? (orderedInsert cmp l a b) =
      match headKey? l with
        | none => some a
        | some x => match cmp a x with | .lt | .eq => some a | .gt => some x

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.headKey?_orderedInsert_or
items.statement:
theorem headKey?_orderedInsert_or (cmp) (l : AssocList α β) (a) (b) :
    headKey? (orderedInsert cmp l a b) = some a ∨
      headKey? (orderedInsert cmp l a b) = headKey? l

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.KeysOrdered.orderedInsert_aux
Batteries.AssocList.KeysOrdered.orderedInsert
items.statement:
theorem KeysOrdered.orderedInsert [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [OrientedCmp cmp] (h : KeysOrdered cmp l) :
    KeysOrdered cmp (AssocList.orderedInsert cmp l a b)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.toList_orderedInsert
items.statement:
theorem toList_orderedInsert {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {cmp : α → α → Ordering}
    [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [TransCmp cmp] {l : AssocList α β} (h : KeysOrdered cmp l) (a : α) (b : β) :
    (orderedInsert cmp l a b).toList =
      l.toList.filter (fun p => cmp a p.1 == .gt) ++
        (a, b) :: l.toList.filter (fun p => cmp a p.1 == .lt)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.leHeadKey_filterMapVal
items.statement:
theorem leHeadKey_filterMapVal [TransCmp cmp] (h : KeysOrdered cmp l) :
    LEHeadKey cmp l (l.filterMapVal f)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.KeysOrdered.filterMapVal
items.statement:
theorem KeysOrdered.filterMapVal [TransCmp cmp] (h : KeysOrdered cmp l) :
    KeysOrdered cmp (l.filterMapVal f)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedMerge
items.doc:
Merge two `AssocList`s,
at each stage taking the first key-value pair from whichever list has a smaller first key.
If both inputs have keys in strictly increasing order, so does the result.
(We later wrap this as `OrderedAssocList.merge`.)

We combine values using a function `f : α → Option β → Option γ → Option δ` which we call as
`f a (some b) none` when encountering a key present only in the first list (with value `b`),
`f a none (some g)` when encountering a key present only in the second list (with value `g`), and
`f a (some b) (some g)` when encountering a key present in both lists.
(Note the value of `f a none none` is never used.)
items.statement:
def orderedMerge (cmp : α → α → Ordering) (f : α → Option β → Option γ → Option δ) :
    AssocList α β → AssocList α γ → AssocList α δ

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.ltHeadKey_orderedMerge
items.statement:
theorem ltHeadKey_orderedMerge [TransCmp cmp]
    (h₁ : LTHeadKey cmp a l₁) (h₂ : LTHeadKey cmp a l₂)
    (w₁ : KeysOrdered cmp l₁) (w₂ : KeysOrdered cmp l₂) :
    LTHeadKey cmp a (orderedMerge cmp f l₁ l₂)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.KeysOrdered.orderedMerge
items.statement:
theorem KeysOrdered.orderedMerge [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [TransCmp cmp]
    (h₁ : KeysOrdered cmp l₁) (h₂ : KeysOrdered cmp l₂) :
    KeysOrdered cmp (AssocList.orderedMerge cmp f l₁ l₂)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedFind?
items.doc:
Find the value associated to a key by traversing left to right,
short-circuiting once we are considering larger keys.
items.statement: def orderedFind? (cmp : α → α → Ordering) (l : AssocList α β) (x : α) : Option β

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedFind?_nil
items.statement:
theorem orderedFind?_nil {cmp : α → α → Ordering} :
    orderedFind? cmp (nil : AssocList α β) x = none

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedFind?_eq_find?
items.statement:
theorem orderedFind?_eq_find?
    {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [TransCmp cmp] [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
    (l : AssocList α β) (h : l.KeysOrdered cmp) (x : α) : l.orderedFind? cmp x = l.find? x

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedFind?_eq
items.statement:
theorem orderedFind?_eq
    {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [TransCmp cmp] [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α]
    (l : AssocList α β) (h : l.KeysOrdered cmp) (x : α) :
    l.orderedFind? cmp x = (l.toList.find? (·.1 == x)).map (·.2)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedFind?_eq_none_of_ltHeadKey
items.statement:
theorem orderedFind?_eq_none_of_ltHeadKey (l : AssocList α β) (w : LTHeadKey cmp x l) :
    orderedFind? cmp l x = none

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedFind?_cons
items.statement:
theorem orderedFind?_cons [TransCmp cmp]
    (h : (AssocList.cons a b t).KeysOrdered cmp) :
    orderedFind? cmp (.cons a b t) x = if cmp x a = .eq then some b else orderedFind? cmp t x

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedFind?_cons_self
items.statement:
theorem orderedFind?_cons_self [OrientedCmp cmp] :
    orderedFind? cmp (.cons a b t) a = some b

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedFind?_orderedInsert
items.statement:
theorem orderedFind?_orderedInsert {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [TransCmp cmp]
    (l : AssocList α β) (h : KeysOrdered cmp l) (a : α) (b : β) :
    (orderedInsert cmp l a b).orderedFind? cmp x =
      if cmp x a = .eq then some b else l.orderedFind? cmp x

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedFind?_orderedInsert_self
items.statement:
theorem orderedFind?_orderedInsert_self {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [TransCmp cmp]
    (l : AssocList α β) (h : KeysOrdered cmp l)  (a : α) (b : β) :
    (orderedInsert cmp l a b).orderedFind? cmp a = some b

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.ext_orderedFind?
items.doc:
If two `AssocList`s have ordered keys
we can check whether they are equal by checking if their `orderedFind?` functions are equal.
items.statement:
theorem ext_orderedFind?
    (cmp : α → α → Ordering) [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [TransCmp cmp]
    {l₁ l₂ : AssocList α β} (h₁ : l₁.KeysOrdered cmp) (h₂ : l₂.KeysOrdered cmp)
    (w : ∀ a, l₁.orderedFind? cmp a = l₂.orderedFind? cmp a) : l₁ = l₂

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.orderedFind?_filterMapVal
items.statement:
theorem orderedFind?_filterMapVal {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [TransCmp cmp]
    {l : AssocList α β} (h : KeysOrdered cmp l) :
    (filterMapVal f l).orderedFind? cmp a = (l.orderedFind? cmp a).bind (fun b => f a b)

items.name: Batteries.AssocList.filterMapVal_filterMapVal
items.statement:
theorem filterMapVal_filterMapVal {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [TransCmp cmp]
    {f : α → γ → Option δ} {g : α → β → Option γ}
    {l : AssocList α β} (h : KeysOrdered cmp l) :
    filterMapVal f (filterMapVal g l) =
      filterMapVal (fun a b => (g a b).bind (fun c => f a c)) l

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList
items.doc:
An `OrderedAssocList` is an `AssocList` with the additional invariant that
the keys are in strictly increasing order according to some specified comparator function.
items.statement:
structure OrderedAssocList {α : Type u} (cmp : α → α → Ordering) (β : Type v) where
  /-- The underlying `AssocList` of an `OrderedAssocList`. -/
  toAssocList : AssocList α β
  /-- The invariant that the keys are in strictly increasing order according to `cmp`. -/
  keysOrdered : toAssocList.KeysOrdered cmp

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.nil
items.doc: The empty `OrderedAssocList`.
items.statement: def nil : OrderedAssocList cmp β

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.toAssocList_nil
items.statement: theorem toAssocList_nil : (nil : OrderedAssocList cmp β).toAssocList = .nil

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.length
items.doc: The length of an `OrderedAssocList`.
items.statement: def length (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) : Nat

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.length_nil
items.statement: theorem length_nil : length (nil : OrderedAssocList cmp β) = 0

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.length_mk_cons
items.statement: theorem length_mk_cons : length ⟨.cons a b t, h⟩ = length ⟨t, h.tail⟩ + 1

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.head?
items.doc: The first key-value pair in an `OrderedAssocList`.
items.statement: def head? (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) : Option (α × β)

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.head?_eq_head?
items.statement: theorem head?_eq_head? (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) : l.head? = l.toAssocList.toList.head?

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.tail
items.doc: The tail of an `OrderedAssocList`.
items.statement: def tail (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) : OrderedAssocList cmp β

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.toAssocList_tail_mk_nil
items.statement:
theorem toAssocList_tail_mk_nil {h} :
    (tail (⟨.nil, h⟩ : OrderedAssocList cmp β)).toAssocList = .nil

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.toAssocList_tail_mk_cons
items.statement:
theorem toAssocList_tail_mk_cons {h} :
    (tail (⟨.cons a b t, h⟩ : OrderedAssocList cmp β)).toAssocList = t

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.length_tail
items.statement: theorem length_tail : length (tail l) = length l - 1

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.find?
items.doc:
Find the value associated to a key by traversing left to right,
short-circuiting once we are considering larger keys.

This is the internal implementation of  `l[x]?`, which should be preferred.
items.statement: def find? (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (x : α) : Option β

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.contains
items.doc: Check if an `OrderedAssocList` contains a specific key.
items.statement: def contains (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (x : α) : Bool

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_nil
items.statement: theorem getElem?_nil {x : α} : (nil : OrderedAssocList cmp β)[x]? = none

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_mk_nil
items.statement: theorem getElem?_mk_nil {x : α} : (⟨.nil, h⟩ : OrderedAssocList cmp β)[x]? = none

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.contains_eq_isSome_getElem?
items.statement:
theorem contains_eq_isSome_getElem? {l : OrderedAssocList cmp β} :
    l.contains a = l[a]?.isSome

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.headKey?
items.doc: The first key in an `OrderedAssocList`, or `none` if the list is empty.
items.statement: def headKey? (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) : Option α

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.headKey?_nil
items.statement: theorem headKey?_nil : headKey? (nil : OrderedAssocList cmp β) = none

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.headKey?_mk_cons
items.statement: theorem headKey?_mk_cons : headKey? ⟨.cons a b t, h⟩ = some a

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.LTHeadKey
items.doc: Either `a` is less than the first key of `l`, or `l` is empty.
items.statement: def LTHeadKey (a : α) (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) : Prop

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.ltHeadKey_tail
items.doc: The head key of a tail is either `none`, or greater than the original head key.
items.statement:
theorem ltHeadKey_tail (h : AssocList.KeysOrdered cmp (.cons a b t)) :
    LTHeadKey a ⟨t, h.tail⟩

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_eq_none_of_ltHeadKey
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_eq_none_of_ltHeadKey (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (w : LTHeadKey x l) :
    l[x]? = none

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_mk_cons
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_mk_cons [TransCmp cmp]
    {h : (AssocList.cons a b t).KeysOrdered cmp} :
    (⟨.cons a b t, h⟩ : OrderedAssocList _ _)[x]? =
      if cmp x a = .eq then some b else (⟨t, h.tail⟩ : OrderedAssocList _ _)[x]?

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_mk_cons_self
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_mk_cons_self [OrientedCmp cmp]
    {h : (AssocList.cons a b t).KeysOrdered cmp} :
    (⟨.cons a b t, h⟩ : OrderedAssocList _ _)[a]? = some b

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.ext_toAssocList
items.statement:
theorem ext_toAssocList {l₁ l₂ : OrderedAssocList cmp β}
    (w : l₁.toAssocList = l₂.toAssocList) : l₁ = l₂

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.ext
items.statement:
theorem ext [LawfulEqCmp cmp] [TransCmp cmp] {l₁ l₂ : OrderedAssocList cmp β}
    (w : ∀ a : α, l₁[a]? = l₂[a]?) : l₁ = l₂

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.contains_nil
items.statement: theorem contains_nil : contains (nil : OrderedAssocList cmp β) x = false

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.contains_mk_cons_self
items.statement:
theorem contains_mk_cons_self [OrientedCmp cmp]
    {h : (AssocList.cons a b t).KeysOrdered cmp} :
    contains ⟨.cons a b t, h⟩ a = true

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.cons
items.doc:
Prepend a key-value pair,
requiring a proof that the key is smaller than the existing smallest key.
items.statement:
def cons (a : α) (b : β) (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (w : LTHeadKey a l) :
    OrderedAssocList cmp β

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.toAssocList_cons
items.statement: theorem toAssocList_cons : (cons a b l w).toAssocList = .cons a b l.toAssocList

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_cons
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_cons [TransCmp cmp] {l : OrderedAssocList cmp β} {w} :
    (cons a b l w)[x]? = if cmp x a = .eq then some b else l[x]?

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.headKey?_cons
items.statement: theorem headKey?_cons : headKey? (cons a b l w) = some a

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.insert
items.doc:
Insert a key-value pair into an `OrderedAssocList`.
This replaces the current value if the key is already present,
and otherwise inserts it before the first key which is greater than the inserted key.
items.statement: def insert (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (a : α) (b : β) : OrderedAssocList cmp β

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.toAssocList_insert
items.statement:
theorem toAssocList_insert (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (a : α) (b : β) :
    (insert l a b).toAssocList = l.toAssocList.orderedInsert cmp a b

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.insert_mk_nil
items.statement:
theorem insert_mk_nil :
    insert (⟨.nil, h⟩ : OrderedAssocList cmp β) a b =
      ⟨.cons a b .nil, AssocList.keysOrdered_cons_nil⟩

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.insert_mk_cons
items.statement:
theorem insert_mk_cons :
    insert (⟨.cons x y t, h⟩ : OrderedAssocList cmp β) a b = match w : cmp a x with
    | .lt => ⟨.cons a b (.cons x y t), ⟨w, h⟩⟩
    | .eq => ⟨.cons a b t, by
        cases (LawfulEqCmp.eq_of_compare w); exact h⟩
    | .gt => ⟨.cons x y (t.orderedInsert cmp a b),
        h.orderedInsert_aux w⟩

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.length_insert_ne_zero
items.statement: theorem length_insert_ne_zero {l : OrderedAssocList cmp β} : (insert l a b).length ≠ 0

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_insert
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_insert (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (a : α) (b : β) :
    (insert l a b)[x]? = if cmp x a = .eq then some b else l[x]?

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_insert_self
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_insert_self (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (a : α) (b : β) :
    (insert l a b)[a]? = some b

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.contains_insert
items.statement:
theorem contains_insert (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (a : α) (b : β) :
    (l.insert a b).contains x = ((cmp x a = .eq) || l.contains x)

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.contains_insert_self
items.statement:
theorem contains_insert_self (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (a : α) (b : β) :
    (l.insert a b).contains a = true

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.filterMapVal
items.doc:
Apply a function to each key-value pair,
either replacing the value or dropping it if the function returns `none`.
items.statement:
def filterMapVal (f : α → β → Option δ) (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) :
    OrderedAssocList cmp δ

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.toAssocList_filterMapVal
items.statement:
theorem toAssocList_filterMapVal (f : α → β → Option δ) (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) :
    (filterMapVal f l).toAssocList = l.toAssocList.filterMapVal f

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_filterMapVal
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_filterMapVal [LawfulEqCmp cmp] (l : OrderedAssocList cmp β) :
    (filterMapVal f l)[a]? = l[a]?.bind (fun b => f a b)

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.filterMapVal_filterMapVal
items.statement:
theorem filterMapVal_filterMapVal [LawfulEqCmp cmp]
    {f : α → γ → Option δ} {g : α → β → Option γ}
    {l : OrderedAssocList cmp β} :
    filterMapVal f (filterMapVal g l) =
      filterMapVal (fun a b => (g a b).bind (fun c => f a c)) l

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.merge
items.doc:
Merge two `OrderedAssocList`s using a function `α → Option β → Option γ → Option δ`,
dropping values where the function returns `none`.
items.statement:
def merge (f : α → Option β → Option γ → Option δ)
    (l₁ : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (l₂ : OrderedAssocList cmp γ) : OrderedAssocList cmp δ

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.toAssocList_merge
items.statement:
theorem toAssocList_merge {l₁ : OrderedAssocList cmp β} :
    (merge f l₁ l₂).toAssocList = AssocList.orderedMerge cmp f l₁.toAssocList l₂.toAssocList

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.merge_nil_nil
items.statement:
theorem merge_nil_nil {f : α → Option β → Option γ → Option δ} :
    merge f (nil : OrderedAssocList cmp β) nil = nil

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.merge_mk_nil_mk_cons
items.statement:
theorem merge_mk_nil_mk_cons {f : α → Option β → Option γ → Option δ} :
    merge f (⟨.nil, h⟩ : OrderedAssocList cmp β) ⟨.cons x' y' t', h'⟩ =
      filterMapVal (fun a g => f a none (some g)) ⟨.cons x' y' t', h'⟩

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.merge_mk_cons_mk_nil
items.statement:
theorem merge_mk_cons_mk_nil {f : α → Option β → Option γ → Option δ} :
    merge f ⟨.cons x y t, h⟩ (⟨.nil, h'⟩ : OrderedAssocList cmp γ) =
      filterMapVal (fun a b => f a (some b) none) ⟨.cons x y t, h⟩

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_merge
Batteries.OrderedAssocList.merge_comm
items.statement:
theorem merge_comm
    (f : α → Option β → Option γ → Option δ) (g : α → Option γ → Option β → Option δ)
    (hg : ∀ a, g a none none = none)
    (w : ∀ a x y, f a x y = g a y x)
    (l₁ : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (l₂) : merge f l₁ l₂ = merge g l₂ l₁

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.merge_assoc
items.statement:
theorem merge_assoc
    (f₁ : α → Option β₁ → Option β₂ → Option γ₁) (f₂ : α → Option γ₁ → Option β₃ → Option ε)
    (g₁ : α → Option β₂ → Option β₃ → Option γ₂) (g₂ : α → Option β₁ → Option γ₂ → Option ε)
    (hf₁ : ∀ a, f₁ a none none = none) (hf₂ : ∀ a, f₂ a none none = none)
    (hg₁ : ∀ a, g₁ a none none = none) (hg₂ : ∀ a, g₂ a none none = none)
    (w : ∀ a x y z, f₂ a (f₁ a x y) z = g₂ a x (g₁ a y z))
    (l₁ : OrderedAssocList cmp β₁) (l₂) (l₃) :
    merge f₂ (merge f₁ l₁ l₂) l₃ = merge g₂ l₁ (merge g₁ l₂ l₃)

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.add
items.doc:
Add two `OrderedAssocList`s, taking the value from one list if the other value is missing.
(That is, treating missing values as `0`.)
items.statement:
def add [Add β] (l₁ : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (l₂ : OrderedAssocList cmp β) :
    OrderedAssocList cmp β

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_add
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_add [Add β] {l₁ : OrderedAssocList cmp β} {a : α} :
    (add l₁ l₂)[a]? =
      match l₁[a]?, l₂[a]? with
      | some x, some y => some (x + y)
      | some x, none => some x
      | none, some y => some y
      | none, none => none

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.mul
items.doc:
Multiply two `OrderedAssocList`s,
dropping any values where the corresponding value in the other list is missing.
(That is, treating missing values as `0`.)
items.statement:
def mul [Mul β] (l₁ : OrderedAssocList cmp β) (l₂ : OrderedAssocList cmp β) :
    OrderedAssocList cmp β

items.name: Batteries.OrderedAssocList.getElem?_mul
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_mul [Mul β] {l₁ : OrderedAssocList cmp β} {a : α} :
    (mul l₁ l₂)[a]? =
      match l₁[a]?, l₂[a]? with
      | some x, some y => some (x * y)
      | some _, none => none
      | none, some _ => none
      | none, none => none

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap
items.doc:
A `Heap` is the nodes of the pairing heap.
Each node have two pointers: `child` going to the first child of this node,
and `sibling` goes to the next sibling of this tree.
So it actually encodes a forest where each node has children
`node.child`, `node.child.sibling`, `node.child.sibling.sibling`, etc.

Each edge in this forest denotes a `le a b` relation that has been checked, so
the root is smaller than everything else under it.
items.statement:
inductive Heap (α : Type u) where
  /-- An empty forest, which has depth `0`. -/
  | nil : Heap α
  /-- A forest consists of a root `a`, a forest `child` elements greater than `a`,
  and another forest `sibling`. -/
  | node (a : α) (child sibling : Heap α) : Heap α
  deriving Repr

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.size
items.doc: `O(n)`. The number of elements in the heap.
items.statement: def Heap.size : Heap α → Nat

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.singleton
items.doc: A node containing a single element `a`.
items.statement: def Heap.singleton (a : α) : Heap α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.isEmpty
items.doc: `O(1)`. Is the heap empty?
items.statement: def Heap.isEmpty : Heap α → Bool

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.merge
items.doc: `O(1)`. Merge two heaps. Ignore siblings.
items.statement: def Heap.merge (le : α → α → Bool) : Heap α → Heap α → Heap α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.combine
items.doc: Auxiliary for `Heap.deleteMin`: merge the forest in pairs.
items.statement: def Heap.combine (le : α → α → Bool) : Heap α → Heap α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.headD
items.doc: `O(1)`. Get the smallest element in the heap, including the passed in value `a`.
items.statement: def Heap.headD (a : α) : Heap α → α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.head?
items.doc: `O(1)`. Get the smallest element in the heap, if it has an element.
items.statement: def Heap.head? : Heap α → Option α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.deleteMin
items.doc: Amortized `O(log n)`. Find and remove the the minimum element from the heap.
items.statement: def Heap.deleteMin (le : α → α → Bool) : Heap α → Option (α × Heap α)

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.tail?
items.doc: Amortized `O(log n)`. Get the tail of the pairing heap after removing the minimum element.
items.statement: def Heap.tail? (le : α → α → Bool) (h : Heap α) : Option (Heap α)

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.tail
items.doc: Amortized `O(log n)`. Remove the minimum element of the heap.
items.statement: def Heap.tail (le : α → α → Bool) (h : Heap α) : Heap α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.NoSibling
items.doc: A predicate says there is no more than one tree.
items.statement:
inductive Heap.NoSibling : Heap α → Prop
  /-- An empty heap is no more than one tree. -/
  | nil : NoSibling .nil
  /-- Or there is exactly one tree. -/
  | node (a c) : NoSibling (.node a c .nil)

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.noSibling_merge
items.statement:
theorem Heap.noSibling_merge (le) (s₁ s₂ : Heap α) :
    (s₁.merge le s₂).NoSibling

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.noSibling_combine
items.statement:
theorem Heap.noSibling_combine (le) (s : Heap α) :
    (s.combine le).NoSibling

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.noSibling_deleteMin
items.statement:
theorem Heap.noSibling_deleteMin {s : Heap α} (eq : s.deleteMin le = some (a, s')) :
    s'.NoSibling

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.noSibling_tail?
items.statement:
theorem Heap.noSibling_tail? {s : Heap α} : s.tail? le = some s' →
    s'.NoSibling

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.noSibling_tail
items.statement: theorem Heap.noSibling_tail (le) (s : Heap α) : (s.tail le).NoSibling

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.size_merge_node
items.statement:
theorem Heap.size_merge_node (le) (a₁ : α) (c₁ s₁ : Heap α) (a₂ : α) (c₂ s₂ : Heap α) :
    (merge le (.node a₁ c₁ s₁) (.node a₂ c₂ s₂)).size = c₁.size + c₂.size + 2

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.size_merge
items.statement:
theorem Heap.size_merge (le) {s₁ s₂ : Heap α} (h₁ : s₁.NoSibling) (h₂ : s₂.NoSibling) :
    (merge le s₁ s₂).size = s₁.size + s₂.size

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.size_combine
items.statement:
theorem Heap.size_combine (le) (s : Heap α) :
    (s.combine le).size = s.size

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.size_deleteMin
items.statement:
theorem Heap.size_deleteMin {s : Heap α} (h : s.NoSibling) (eq : s.deleteMin le = some (a, s')) :
    s.size = s'.size + 1

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.size_tail?
items.statement:
theorem Heap.size_tail? {s : Heap α} (h : s.NoSibling) : s.tail? le = some s' →
    s.size = s'.size + 1

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.size_tail
items.statement: theorem Heap.size_tail (le) {s : Heap α} (h : s.NoSibling) : (s.tail le).size = s.size - 1

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.size_deleteMin_lt
items.statement:
theorem Heap.size_deleteMin_lt {s : Heap α} (eq : s.deleteMin le = some (a, s')) :
    s'.size < s.size

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.size_tail?_lt
items.statement:
theorem Heap.size_tail?_lt {s : Heap α} : s.tail? le = some s' →
    s'.size < s.size

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.foldM
items.doc:
`O(n log n)`. Monadic fold over the elements of a heap in increasing order,
by repeatedly pulling the minimum element out of the heap.
items.statement:
def Heap.foldM [Monad m] (le : α → α → Bool) (s : Heap α)
    (init : β) (f : β → α → m β) : m β

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.fold
items.doc:
`O(n log n)`. Fold over the elements of a heap in increasing order,
by repeatedly pulling the minimum element out of the heap.
items.statement: def Heap.fold (le : α → α → Bool) (s : Heap α) (init : β) (f : β → α → β) : β

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.toArray
items.doc: `O(n log n)`. Convert the heap to an array in increasing order.
items.statement: def Heap.toArray (le : α → α → Bool) (s : Heap α) : Array α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.toList
items.doc: `O(n log n)`. Convert the heap to a list in increasing order.
items.statement: def Heap.toList (le : α → α → Bool) (s : Heap α) : List α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.foldTreeM
items.doc: `O(n)`. Fold a monadic function over the tree structure to accumulate a value.
items.statement: def Heap.foldTreeM [Monad m] (nil : β) (join : α → β → β → m β) : Heap α → m β

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.foldTree
items.doc: `O(n)`. Fold a function over the tree structure to accumulate a value.
items.statement: def Heap.foldTree (nil : β) (join : α → β → β → β) (s : Heap α) : β

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.toListUnordered
items.doc: `O(n)`. Convert the heap to a list in arbitrary order.
items.statement: def Heap.toListUnordered (s : Heap α) : List α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.toArrayUnordered
items.doc: `O(n)`. Convert the heap to an array in arbitrary order.
items.statement: def Heap.toArrayUnordered (s : Heap α) : Array α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.NodeWF
items.doc:
The well formedness predicate for a heap node.
It asserts that:
* If `a` is added at the top to make the forest into a tree, the resulting tree
  is a `le`-min-heap (if `le` is well-behaved)
items.statement: def Heap.NodeWF (le : α → α → Bool) (a : α) : Heap α → Prop

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.WF
items.doc:
The well formedness predicate for a pairing heap.
It asserts that:
* There is no more than one tree.
* It is a `le`-min-heap (if `le` is well-behaved)
items.statement:
inductive Heap.WF (le : α → α → Bool) : Heap α → Prop
  /-- It is an empty heap. -/
  | nil : WF le .nil
  /-- There is exactly one tree and it is a `le`-min-heap. -/
  | node (h : c.NodeWF le a) : WF le (.node a c .nil)

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.WF.singleton
items.statement: theorem Heap.WF.singleton : (Heap.singleton a).WF le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.WF.merge_node
items.statement:
theorem Heap.WF.merge_node (h₁ : NodeWF le a₁ c₁) (h₂ : NodeWF le a₂ c₂) :
    (merge le (.node a₁ c₁ s₁) (.node a₂ c₂ s₂)).WF le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.WF.merge
items.statement:
theorem Heap.WF.merge (h₁ : s₁.WF le) (h₂ : s₂.WF le) :
    (merge le s₁ s₂).WF le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.WF.combine
items.statement: theorem Heap.WF.combine (h : s.NodeWF le a) : (combine le s).WF le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.WF.deleteMin
items.statement:
theorem Heap.WF.deleteMin {s : Heap α} (h : s.WF le)
    (eq : s.deleteMin le = some (a, s')) : s'.WF le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.WF.tail?
items.statement:
theorem Heap.WF.tail? (hwf : (s : Heap α).WF le) : s.tail? le = some tl →
  tl.WF le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.WF.tail
items.statement: theorem Heap.WF.tail (hwf : (s : Heap α).WF le) : (s.tail le).WF le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeapImp.Heap.deleteMin_fst
items.statement: theorem Heap.deleteMin_fst : ((s : Heap α).deleteMin le).map (·.1) = s.head?

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap
items.doc:
A [pairing heap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pairing_heap) is a data structure which supports
the following primary operations:

* `insert : α → PairingHeap α → PairingHeap α`: add an element to the heap
* `deleteMin : PairingHeap α → Option (α × PairingHeap α)`:
  remove the minimum element from the heap
* `merge : PairingHeap α → PairingHeap α → PairingHeap α`: combine two heaps

The first two operations are known as a "priority queue", so this could be called
a "mergeable priority queue". The standard choice for a priority queue is a binary heap,
which supports `insert` and `deleteMin` in `O(log n)`, but `merge` is `O(n)`.
With a `PairingHeap`, `insert` and `merge` are `O(1)`, `deleteMin` is amortized `O(log n)`.

Note that `deleteMin` may be `O(n)` in a single operation. So if you need an efficient
persistent priority queue, you should use other data structures with better worst-case time.
items.statement: def PairingHeap (α : Type u) (le : α → α → Bool)

items.name: Batteries.mkPairingHeap
items.doc: `O(1)`. Make a new empty pairing heap.
items.statement: def mkPairingHeap (α : Type u) (le : α → α → Bool) : PairingHeap α le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.empty
items.doc: `O(1)`. Make a new empty pairing heap.
items.statement: def empty : PairingHeap α le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.isEmpty
items.doc: `O(1)`. Is the heap empty?
items.statement: def isEmpty (b : PairingHeap α le) : Bool

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.size
items.doc: `O(n)`. The number of elements in the heap.
items.statement: def size (b : PairingHeap α le) : Nat

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.singleton
items.doc: `O(1)`. Make a new heap containing `a`.
items.statement: def singleton (a : α) : PairingHeap α le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.merge
items.doc: `O(1)`. Merge the contents of two heaps.
items.statement: def merge : PairingHeap α le → PairingHeap α le → PairingHeap α le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.insert
items.doc: `O(1)`. Add element `a` to the given heap `h`.
items.statement: def insert (a : α) (h : PairingHeap α le) : PairingHeap α le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.ofList
items.doc: `O(n log n)`. Construct a heap from a list by inserting all the elements.
items.statement: def ofList (le : α → α → Bool) (as : List α) : PairingHeap α le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.ofArray
items.doc: `O(n log n)`. Construct a heap from a list by inserting all the elements.
items.statement: def ofArray (le : α → α → Bool) (as : Array α) : PairingHeap α le

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.deleteMin
items.doc: Amortized `O(log n)`. Remove and return the minimum element from the heap.
items.statement: def deleteMin (b : PairingHeap α le) : Option (α × PairingHeap α le)

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.head?
items.doc: `O(1)`. Returns the smallest element in the heap, or `none` if the heap is empty.
items.statement: def head? (b : PairingHeap α le) : Option α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.head!
items.doc: `O(1)`. Returns the smallest element in the heap, or panics if the heap is empty.
items.statement: def head! [Inhabited α] (b : PairingHeap α le) : α

items.name: Batteries.PairingHeap.headI
items.doc: `O(1)`. Returns the smallest element in the heap, or `default` if the heap is empty.
items.statement: def headI [Inhabited α] (b : PairingHeap α le) : α

modules.title: Mersenne Twister
modules.doc:
Generic implementation for the Mersenne Twister pseudorandom number generator.

All choices of parameters from Matsumoto and Nishimura (1998) are supported, along with later
refinements. Parameters for the standard 32-bit MT19937 and 64-bit MT19937-64 algorithms are
provided. Both `RandomGen` and `Stream` interfaces are provided.

Use `mt19937.init seed` to create a MT19937 PRNG with a 32 bit seed value; use
`mt19937_64.init seed` to create a MT19937-64 PRNG with a 64 bit seed value. If omitted, default
seed choices will be used.

Sample usage:
```
import Batteries.Data.Random.MersenneTwister

open Batteries.Random.MersenneTwister

def mtgen := mt19937.init -- default seed 4357

#eval (Stream.take mtgen 5).fst -- [874448474, 2424656266, 2174085406, 1265871120, 3155244894]
```

### References:

- Matsumoto, Makoto and Nishimura, Takuji (1998),
  [**Mersenne twister: A 623-dimensionally equidistributed uniform pseudo-random number generator**](https://doi.org/10.1145/272991.272995),
  ACM Trans. Model. Comput. Simul. 8, No. 1, 3-30.
  [ZBL0917.65005](https://zbmath.org/?q=an:0917.65005).

- Nishimura, Takuji (2000),
  [**Tables of 64-bit Mersenne twisters**](https://doi.org/10.1145/369534.369540),
  ACM Trans. Model. Comput. Simul. 10, No. 4, 348-357.
  [ZBL1390.65014](https://zbmath.org/?q=an:1390.65014).

  /-- Tempering mask parameters (`d`, `b`, `c`). -/
  temperingMasks : BitVec wordSize × BitVec wordSize × BitVec wordSize
  /-- Initialization multiplier (`f`). -/
  initMult : BitVec wordSize
  /-- Default initialization seed value. -/

modules.title: Running Statistics
modules.doc:
This module implements Welford's one-pass algorithm for calculating the mean and
standard deviation of a sample or a population. The advantage of this algorithm is
This module implements Welford's one-pass algorithm for calculating the mean,
variance and standard deviation of a sample or a population. The advantage of
this algorithm is that it is not necessary to store the data.

The algorithm uses the recurrence formulas for the mean `μ`, variance `σ²`
and the sample variance `s²`:
```
  μₖ = μₖ₋₁ + (xₖ − μₖ₋₁)/k
  σ²ₖ = σ²ₖ₋₁*(k-1)/k + (xₖ − μₖ₋₁)*(xₖ − μₖ)/k
  s²ₖ = s²ₖ₋₁*(k-2)/(k-1) + (xₖ - μₖ₋₁)²/k
```
To improve performance, Welford's algorithm keeps track of the two running
quantities:
```
  Mₖ = Mₖ₋₁ + (xₖ - Mₖ₋₁)/k
  Sₖ = Sₖ₋₁ + (xₖ - Mₖ₋₁)*(xₖ - Mₖ)
```
Then: `μₖ = Mₖ`, `σ²ₖ = Sₖ/k`, `s²ₖ = Sₖ/(k-1)`.

items.name: Batteries.RunningStats
items.doc: Compute running statistics of a data stream using Welford's algorithm.

  /-- Initialize running statistics. -/
  init ::
  /-- Number of data points, -/
  count : Nat := 0
  /-- Mean of data points. -/
  mean : Float := 0.0
  /-- Variance of data points times the number of data points. -/

theorem fst_take_zero [Stream σ α] (s : σ) :

items.name: Std.Stream.fst_take_succ
items.statement:
theorem fst_take_succ [Stream σ α] (s : σ) :
    (take s (n+1)).fst = match next? s with
      | none => []

theorem fst_takeTR_loop [Stream σ α] (s : σ) (acc : List α) (n : Nat) :

modules.title: Legacy implementations of `String` operations
modules.doc:
This file includes old definitions of `String` functions that were downstreamed from core to prevent
`Batteries.Data.String.Lemmas` from breaking.

items.name: String.Legacy.map
items.doc:
Applies the function `f` to every character in a string, returning a string that contains the
resulting characters.

This is an old implementation, preserved here for users of the lemmas in
`Batteries.Data.String.Lemmas`. Its runtime behavior is equivalent to that of `String.map`.

Examples:
 * `"abc123".map Char.toUpper = "ABC123"`
 * `"".map Char.toUpper = ""`
items.statement: def Legacy.map (f : Char → Char) (s : String) : String

items.name: String.Legacy.drop
items.doc:
Removes the specified number of characters (Unicode code points) from the start of the string.

If `n` is greater than `s.length`, returns `""`.

This is an old implementation, preserved here for users of the lemmas in
`Batteries.Data.String.Lemmas`. Its runtime behavior is equivalent to that of `String.drop`.

Examples:
 * `"red green blue".drop 4 = "green blue"`
 * `"red green blue".drop 10 = "blue"`
 * `"red green blue".drop 50 = ""`
items.statement: def Legacy.drop (s : String) (n : Nat) : String

items.name: String.Legacy.take
items.doc:
Creates a new string that contains the first `n` characters (Unicode code points) of `s`.

If `n` is greater than `s.length`, returns `s`.

This is an old implementation, preserved here for users of the lemmas in
`Batteries.Data.String.Lemmas`. Its runtime behavior is equivalent to that of `String.take`.

Examples:
* `"red green blue".take 3 = "red"`
* `"red green blue".take 1 = "r"`
* `"red green blue".take 0 = ""`
* `"red green blue".take 100 = "red green blue"`
items.statement: def Legacy.take (s : String) (n : Nat) : String

items.name: String.Legacy.takeWhile
items.doc:
Creates a new string that contains the longest prefix of `s` in which `p` returns `true` for all
characters.

This is an old implementation, preserved here for users of the lemmas in
`Batteries.Data.String.Lemmas`. Its runtime behavior is equivalent to that of `String.takeWhile`.

Examples:
* `"red green blue".takeWhile (·.isLetter) = "red"`
* `"red green blue".takeWhile (· == 'r') = "r"`
* `"red green blue".takeWhile (· != 'n') = "red gree"`
* `"red green blue".takeWhile (fun _ => true) = "red green blue"`
items.statement: def Legacy.takeWhile (s : String) (p : Char → Bool) : String

items.name: String.Legacy.dropWhile
items.doc:
Creates a new string by removing the longest prefix from `s` in which `p` returns `true` for all
characters.

This is an old implementation, preserved here for users of the lemmas in
`Batteries.Data.String.Lemmas`. Its runtime behavior is equivalent to that of `String.dropWhile`.

Examples:
* `"red green blue".dropWhile (·.isLetter) = " green blue"`
* `"red green blue".dropWhile (· == 'r') = "ed green blue"`
* `"red green blue".dropWhile (· != 'n') = "n blue"`
* `"red green blue".dropWhile (fun _ => true) = ""`
items.statement: def Legacy.dropWhile (s : String) (p : Char → Bool) : String

Folds a function over a string from the left, accumulating a value starting with `init`. The
accumulated value is combined with each character in order, using `f`.

This is an old implementation, preserved here for users of the lemmas in
`Batteries.Data.String.Lemmas`. Its runtime behavior is equivalent to that of `String.foldl`.

Examples:
 * `"coffee tea water".foldl (fun n c => if c.isWhitespace then n + 1 else n) 0 = 2`
 * `"coffee tea and water".foldl (fun n c => if c.isWhitespace then n + 1 else n) 0 = 3`
 * `"coffee tea water".foldl (·.push ·) "" = "coffee tea water"`

items.doc:
Induction along the valid positions in a list of characters.
(This definition is intended only for specification purposes.)
items.statement:
def utf8InductionOn {motive : List Char → Pos.Raw → Sort u}
    (s : List Char) (i p : Pos.Raw)
    (nil : ∀ i, motive [] i)
    (eq  : ∀ c cs, motive (c :: cs) p)
    (ind : ∀ (c : Char) cs i, i ≠ p → motive cs (i + c) → motive (c :: cs) i) :
    motive s i

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind
items.doc:
### Union-find data structure

The `UnionFind` structure is an implementation of disjoint-set data structure
that uses path compression to make the primary operations run in amortized
nearly linear time. The nodes of a `UnionFind` structure `s` are natural
numbers smaller than `s.size`. The structure associates with a canonical
representative from its equivalence class. The structure can be extended
using the `push` operation and equivalence classes can be updated using the
`union` operation.

The main operations for `UnionFind` are:

* `empty`/`mkEmpty` are used to create a new empty structure.
* `size` returns the size of the data structure.
* `push` adds a new node to a structure, unlinked to any other node.
* `union` links two nodes of the data structure, joining their equivalence
  classes, and performs path compression.
* `find` returns the canonical representative of a node and updates the data
  structure using path compression.
* `root` returns the canonical representative of a node without altering the
  data structure.
* `checkEquiv` checks whether two nodes have the same canonical representative
  and updates the structure using path compression.

Most use cases should prefer `find` over `root` to benefit from the speedup from path-compression.

The main operations use `Fin s.size` to represent nodes of the union-find structure.
Some alternatives are provided:

* `unionN`, `findN`, `rootN`, `checkEquivN` use `Fin n` with a proof that `n = s.size`.
* `union!`, `find!`, `root!`, `checkEquiv!` use `Nat` and panic when the indices are out of bounds.
* `findD`, `rootD`, `checkEquivD` use `Nat` and treat out of bound indices as isolated nodes.

The noncomputable relation `UnionFind.Equiv` is provided to use the equivalence relation from a
`UnionFind` structure in the context of proofs.
items.statement:
structure UnionFind where
  /-- Array of union-find nodes -/
  arr : Array UFNode
  /-- Validity for parent nodes -/
  parentD_lt : ∀ {i}, i < arr.size → parentD arr i < arr.size
  /-- Validity for rank -/
  rankD_lt : ∀ {i}, parentD arr i ≠ i → rankD arr i < rankD arr (parentD arr i)

items.statement:
structure FindAux (n : Nat) where
  /-- Array of nodes -/
  s : Array UFNode
  /-- Index of root node -/
  root : Fin n
  /-- Size requirement -/
  size_eq : s.size = n

items.doc: Auxiliary function for find operation

items.statement:
theorem findAux_root {self : UnionFind} {x : Fin self.size} :
    (findAux self x).root = self.root x

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.findAux_s
items.statement:
theorem findAux_s {self : UnionFind} {x : Fin self.size} :
    (findAux self x).s = if self.arr[x.1].parent = x then self.arr else
      (self.findAux ⟨_, self.parent'_lt x x.2⟩).s.modify x fun s =>
        { s with parent := self.rootD x }

items.statement:
theorem rankD_findAux {self : UnionFind} {x : Fin self.size} :
    rankD (findAux self x).s i = self.rank i

items.statement:
theorem parentD_findAux {self : UnionFind} {x : Fin self.size} :
    parentD (findAux self x).s i =
    if i = x then self.rootD x else parentD (self.findAux ⟨_, self.parent'_lt _ x.2⟩).s i

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.parentD_findAux_or
items.statement:
theorem parentD_findAux_or (self : UnionFind) (x : Fin self.size) (i) :
    parentD (findAux self x).s i = self.rootD i ∧ self.rootD i = self.rootD x ∨
    parentD (findAux self x).s i = self.parent i

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.lt_rankD_findAux
items.statement:
theorem lt_rankD_findAux {self : UnionFind} {x : Fin self.size} :
    parentD (findAux self x).s i ≠ i →
    self.rank i < self.rank (parentD (findAux self x).s i)

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.parentD_linkAux
items.statement:
theorem parentD_linkAux {self} {x y : Fin self.size} :
    parentD (linkAux self x y) i =
    if x.1 = y then
      parentD self i
    else
      if self[y.1].rank < self[x.1].rank then
        if y = i then x else parentD self i
      else
        if x = i then y else parentD self i

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.parent_link
items.statement:
theorem parent_link {self} {x y : Fin self.size} (yroot) {i} :
    (link self x y yroot).parent i =
    if x.1 = y then
      self.parent i
    else
      if self.rank y < self.rank x then
        if y = i then x else self.parent i
      else
        if x = i then y else self.parent i

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.root_link
items.statement:
theorem root_link {self : UnionFind} {x y : Fin self.size}
    (xroot : self.parent x = x) (yroot : self.parent y = y) :
    ∃ r, (r = x ∨ r = y) ∧ ∀ i,
      (link self x y yroot).rootD i =
      if self.rootD i = x ∨ self.rootD i = y then r.1 else self.rootD i

items.statement: nonrec theorem Equiv.rfl : Equiv self a a

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.Equiv.symm
items.statement: nonrec theorem Equiv.symm : Equiv self a b → Equiv self b a

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.Equiv.trans
items.statement: nonrec theorem Equiv.trans : Equiv self a b → Equiv self b c → Equiv self a c

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.equiv_empty
items.statement: theorem equiv_empty : Equiv empty a b ↔ a = b

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.equiv_push
items.statement: theorem equiv_push : Equiv self.push a b ↔ Equiv self a b

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.equiv_rootD
items.statement: theorem equiv_rootD : Equiv self (self.rootD a) a

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.equiv_rootD_l
items.statement: theorem equiv_rootD_l : Equiv self (self.rootD a) b ↔ Equiv self a b

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.equiv_rootD_r
items.statement: theorem equiv_rootD_r : Equiv self a (self.rootD b) ↔ Equiv self a b

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.equiv_find
items.statement: theorem equiv_find : Equiv (self.find x).1 a b ↔ Equiv self a b

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.equiv_link
items.statement:
theorem equiv_link {self : UnionFind} {x y : Fin self.size}
    (xroot : self.parent x = x) (yroot : self.parent y = y) :
    Equiv (link self x y yroot) a b ↔
    Equiv self a b ∨ Equiv self a x ∧ Equiv self y b ∨ Equiv self a y ∧ Equiv self x b

items.name: Batteries.UnionFind.equiv_union
items.statement:
theorem equiv_union {self : UnionFind} {x y : Fin self.size} :
    Equiv (union self x y) a b ↔
    Equiv self a b ∨ Equiv self a x ∧ Equiv self y b ∨ Equiv self a y ∧ Equiv self x b

modules.authors: Shreyas Srinivas, François G. Dorais, Chad Sharp
modules.title: Vectors
modules.doc: `Vector α n` is a thin wrapper around `Array α` for arrays of fixed size `n`.

items.name: Vector.isSome_finIdxOf?

items.name: Vector.isNone_finIdxOf?

theorem isNone_finIdxOf? [BEq α] [PartialEquivBEq α] {v : Vector α n} {a : α} :
    (v.finIdxOf? a).isNone = !v.contains a

items.name: Vector.toList_scanlM
items.statement:
theorem toList_scanlM [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → m β} {as : Vector α n} :

items.name: Vector.toList_scanrM
items.statement:
theorem toList_scanrM [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α → β → m β} {as : Vector α n} :
    Vector.toList <$> as.scanrM f init = as.toList.scanrM f init

items.name: Vector.scanlM_empty
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_empty [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → m β} :
    (#v[] : Vector α 0).scanlM f init = pure #v[init]

items.name: Vector.scanrM_empty
items.statement:
theorem scanrM_empty [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α → β → m β} :
    (#v[] : Vector α 0).scanrM f init = pure #v[init]

items.name: Vector.scanlM_reverse
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_reverse [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → m β} {as : Vector α n} :
    as.reverse.scanlM f init = Vector.reverse <$> (as.scanrM (flip f) init)

items.name: Vector.scanlM_pure
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_pure [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    as.scanlM (m := m) (pure <| f · ·) init = pure (as.scanl f init)

items.name: Vector.scanrM_pure
items.statement:
theorem scanrM_pure [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    as.scanrM (m := m) (pure <| f · ·) init = pure (as.scanr f init)

items.name: Vector.idRun_scanlM
items.statement:
theorem idRun_scanlM {f : β → α → Id β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanlM f init).run = as.scanl (f · · |>.run) init

items.name: Vector.idRun_scanrM
items.statement:
theorem idRun_scanrM {f : α → β → Id β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanrM f init).run = as.scanr (f · · |>.run) init

items.name: Vector.scanlM_map
items.statement:
theorem scanlM_map [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α₁ → α₂} {g : β → α₂ → m β} {as : Vector α₁ n} :
    (as.map f).scanlM g init = as.scanlM (g · <| f ·) init

items.name: Vector.scanrM_map
items.statement:
theorem scanrM_map [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m] {f : α₁ → α₂} {g : α₂ → β → m β} {as : Vector α₁ n} :
    (as.map f).scanrM g init = as.scanrM (fun a b => g (f a) b) init

items.name: Vector.scanl_eq_scanlM
items.statement:
theorem scanl_eq_scanlM {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    as.scanl f init = (as.scanlM (m := Id) (pure <| f · ·) init).run

items.name: Vector.scanr_eq_scanrM
items.statement:
theorem scanr_eq_scanrM {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    as.scanr f init = (as.scanrM (m := Id) (pure <| f · ·) init).run

items.name: Vector.toArray_scanl
items.statement:
theorem toArray_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanl f init).toArray = as.toArray.scanl f init

items.name: Vector.toArray_scanr
items.statement:
theorem toArray_scanr {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanr f init).toArray = as.toArray.scanr f init

items.name: Vector.toList_scanl
items.statement:
theorem toList_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanl f init).toList = as.toList.scanl f init

items.name: Vector.toList_scanr
items.statement:
theorem toList_scanr {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} :

items.name: Vector.scanl_empty
items.statement:
theorem scanl_empty {f : β → α → β} :

items.name: Vector.scanr_empty

    #v[].scanr f init = #v[init]

items.name: Vector.scanl_singleton
items.statement:
theorem scanl_singleton {f : β → α → β} {a : α} :
    #v[a].scanl f init = #v[init, f init a]

items.name: Vector.getElem_scanl
items.statement:
theorem getElem_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} (h : i < n + 1) :
    (as.scanl f init)[i] = (as.take i).foldl f init

items.name: Vector.getElem_scanr
items.statement:
theorem getElem_scanr {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} (h : i < n + 1) :
    (as.scanr f init)[i] = (as.drop i).foldr f init

items.name: Vector.getElem?_scanl
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanl f init)[i]? = if i ≤ n then some ((as.take i).foldl f init) else none

items.name: Vector.getElem?_scanr
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_scanr {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanr f init)[i]? = if i < n + 1 then some ((as.drop i).foldr f init)
      else none

items.name: Vector.getElem_scanl_zero
items.statement:
theorem getElem_scanl_zero {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanl f init)[0] = init

items.name: Vector.getElem_scanr_zero
items.statement:
theorem getElem_scanr_zero {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanr f init)[0] = as.foldr f init

items.name: Vector.getElem?_scanl_zero
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_scanl_zero {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanl f init)[0]? = some init

items.name: Vector.getElem?_scanr_zero
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_scanr_zero {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanr f init)[0]? = some (as.foldr f init)

items.name: Vector.getElem?_succ_scanl
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_succ_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanl f init)[i + 1]? = (as.scanl f init)[i]?.bind fun x => as[i]?.map fun y => f x y

items.name: Vector.getElem_succ_scanl
items.statement:
theorem getElem_succ_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} (h : i + 1 < n + 1) :
    (as.scanl f init)[i + 1] = f (as.scanl f init)[i] as[i]

items.name: Vector.scanl_push
items.statement:
theorem scanl_push {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} {a : α} :
    (as.push a).scanl f init = (as.scanl f init).push (f (as.foldl f init) a)

items.name: Vector.scanr_push
items.statement:
theorem scanr_push {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} {a : α} :
    (as.push a).scanr f init = (as.scanr f (f a init)).push init

items.name: Vector.scanl_map
items.statement:
theorem scanl_map {f : γ → β → γ} {g : α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.map g).scanl f init = as.scanl (f · <| g ·) init

items.name: Vector.scanr_map
items.statement:
theorem scanr_map {f : β → γ → γ} {g : α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.map g).scanr f init = as.scanr (fun x acc => f (g x) acc) init

items.name: Vector.scanl_reverse
items.statement:
theorem scanl_reverse {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.reverse).scanl f init = (as.scanr (flip f) init).reverse

items.name: Vector.scanr_reverse
items.statement:
theorem scanr_reverse {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.reverse).scanr f init = (as.scanl (flip f) init).reverse

items.name: Vector.back_scanl
items.statement:
theorem back_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanl f init).back = as.foldl f init

items.name: Vector.back_scanr
items.statement:
theorem back_scanr {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanr f init).back = init

items.name: Vector.back?_scanl
items.statement:
theorem back?_scanl {f : β → α → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanl f init).back? = some (as.foldl f init)

items.name: Vector.back?_scanr
items.statement:
theorem back?_scanr {f : α → β → β} {as : Vector α n} :
    (as.scanr f init).back? = some init

items.name: Lean.TagAttributeExtra
items.doc:
`TagAttributeExtra` works around a limitation of `TagAttribute`, which is that definitions
must be tagged in the same file that declares the definition.
This works well for definitions in lean core, but for attributes declared outside the core
this is problematic because we may want to tag declarations created before the attribute
was defined.

To resolve this, we allow a one-time exception to the rule that attributes must be applied
in the same file as the declaration: During the declaration of the attribute itself,
we can tag arbitrary other definitions, but once the attribute is declared we must tag things
in the same file as normal.
items.statement:
structure TagAttributeExtra where
  /-- The environment extension for the attribute. -/
  ext : PersistentEnvExtension Name Name NameSet
  /-- A list of "base" declarations which have been pre-tagged. -/
  base : NameHashSet
  deriving Inhabited

items.name: Lean.registerTagAttributeExtra
items.doc:
Registers a new tag attribute. The `extra` field is a list of definitions from other modules
which will be "pre-tagged" and are not subject to the usual restriction on tagging in the same
file as the declaration.

Note: The `extra` fields bypass the `validate` function -
we assume the builtins are also pre-validated.

items.name: Lean.TagAttributeExtra.hasTag
items.doc: Does declaration `decl` have the tag `attr`?
items.statement: def hasTag (attr : TagAttributeExtra) (env : Environment) (decl : Name) : Bool

items.name: Lean.TagAttributeExtra.getDecls
items.doc: Get the list of declarations tagged with the tag attribute `attr`.
items.statement: def getDecls (attr : TagAttributeExtra) (env : Environment) : Array Name

items.name: Lean.ParametricAttributeExtra
items.doc:
`ParametricAttributeExtra` works around a limitation of `ParametricAttribute`, which is that
definitions must be tagged in the same file that declares the definition.
This works well for definitions in lean core, but for attributes declared outside the core
this is problematic because we may want to tag declarations created before the attribute
was defined.

To resolve this, we allow a one-time exception to the rule that attributes must be applied
in the same file as the declaration: During the declaration of the attribute itself,
we can tag arbitrary other definitions, but once the attribute is declared we must tag things
in the same file as normal.
items.statement:
structure ParametricAttributeExtra (α : Type) where
  /-- The underlying `ParametricAttribute`. -/
  attr : ParametricAttribute α
  /-- A list of pre-tagged declarations with their values. -/
  base : Std.HashMap Name α
  deriving Inhabited

items.name: Lean.registerParametricAttributeExtra
items.doc:
Registers a new parametric attribute. The `extra` field is a list of definitions from other modules
which will be "pre-tagged" and are not subject to the usual restriction on tagging in the same
file as the declaration.
items.statement:
def registerParametricAttributeExtra (impl : ParametricAttributeImpl α)
    (extra : List (Name × α)) : IO (ParametricAttributeExtra α)

items.name: Lean.ParametricAttributeExtra.getParam?
items.doc:
Gets the parameter of attribute `attr` associated to declaration `decl`,
or `none` if `decl` is not tagged.
items.statement:
def getParam? [Inhabited α] (attr : ParametricAttributeExtra α)
    (env : Environment) (decl : Name) : Option α

items.name: Lean.ParametricAttributeExtra.setParam
items.doc: Applies attribute `attr` to declaration `decl`, given a value for the parameter.
items.statement:
def setParam (attr : ParametricAttributeExtra α)
    (env : Environment) (decl : Name) (param : α) : Except String Environment

items.name: EStateM.Result.map
items.doc: Map a function over an `EStateM.Result`, preserving states and errors.
items.statement: def map {ε σ α β} (f : α → β) (x : Result ε σ α) : Result ε σ β

items.name: EStateM.Result.map_ok
items.statement:
theorem map_ok {ε σ α β} (f : α → β) (a : α) (s : σ) :
    (Result.ok a s : Result ε σ α).map f = .ok (f a) s

items.name: EStateM.Result.map_error
items.statement:
theorem map_error {ε σ α β} (f : α → β) (e : ε) (s : σ) :
    (Result.error e s : Result ε σ α).map f = .error e s

items.name: EStateM.Result.map_eq_ok
items.statement:
theorem map_eq_ok {ε σ α β} {f : α → β} {x : Result ε σ α} {b : β} {s : σ} :
    x.map f = .ok b s ↔ ∃ a, x = .ok a s ∧ b = f a

items.name: EStateM.Result.map_eq_error
items.statement:
theorem map_eq_error {ε σ α β} (f : α → β) {x : Result ε σ α} {e : ε} {s : σ} :
    x.map f = .error e s ↔ x = .error e s

items.name: EStateM.dummySave_apply
items.statement: theorem dummySave_apply (s : σ) : EStateM.dummySave s = PUnit.unit

items.name: EStateM.dummyRestore_apply
items.statement: theorem dummyRestore_apply (s : σ) : EStateM.dummyRestore s = Function.const _ s

items.name: EStateM.run'_pure
items.statement:
theorem run'_pure (x : α) (s : σ) :
    (pure x : EStateM ε σ α).run' s = some x

items.name: EStateM.run'_bind
items.statement:
theorem run'_bind (x : EStateM ε σ α) (f : α → EStateM ε σ β) (s : σ) :
    (x >>= f).run' s = match x.run s with
    | .ok a s => (f a).run' s
    | .error _ _ => none

items.name: EStateM.run_map
items.statement:
theorem run_map (f : α → β) (x : EStateM ε σ α) (s : σ) :
    (f <$> x).run s = (x.run s).map f

items.name: EStateM.run'_map
items.statement:
theorem run'_map (f : α → β) (x : EStateM ε σ α) (s : σ) :
    (f <$> x).run' s = Option.map f (x.run' s)

items.name: EStateM.run_seq
items.statement:
theorem run_seq (f : EStateM ε σ (α → β)) (x : EStateM ε σ α) (s : σ) :
    (f <*> x).run s = match f.run s with
    | .ok g s => Result.map g (x.run s)
    | .error e s => .error e s

items.name: EStateM.run'_seq
items.statement:
theorem run'_seq (f : EStateM ε σ (α → β)) (x : EStateM ε σ α) (s : σ) :
    (f <*> x).run' s = match f.run s with
    | .ok g s => Option.map g (x.run' s)
    | .error _ _ => none

items.name: EStateM.run_seqLeft
items.statement:
theorem run_seqLeft (x : EStateM ε σ α) (y : EStateM ε σ β) (s : σ) :
    (x <* y).run s = match x.run s with
    | .ok v s => Result.map (fun _ => v) (y.run s)
    | .error e s => .error e s

items.name: EStateM.run'_seqLeft
items.statement:
theorem run'_seqLeft (x : EStateM ε σ α) (y : EStateM ε σ β) (s : σ) :
    (x <* y).run' s = match x.run s with
    | .ok v s => Option.map (fun _ => v) (y.run' s)
    | .error _ _ => none

items.name: EStateM.run_seqRight
items.statement:
theorem run_seqRight (x : EStateM ε σ α) (y : EStateM ε σ β) (s : σ) :
    (x *> y).run s = match x.run s with
    | .ok _ s => y.run s
    | .error e s => .error e s

items.name: EStateM.run'_seqRight
items.statement:
theorem run'_seqRight (x : EStateM ε σ α) (y : EStateM ε σ β) (s : σ) :
    (x *> y).run' s = match x.run s with
    | .ok _ s => y.run' s
    | .error _ _ => none

items.name: EStateM.run'_get
items.statement:
theorem run'_get (s : σ) :
    (get : EStateM ε σ σ).run' s = some s

items.name: EStateM.run'_set
items.statement:
theorem run'_set (v s : σ) :
    (set v : EStateM ε σ PUnit).run' s = some PUnit.unit

items.name: EStateM.run'_modify
items.statement:
theorem run'_modify (f : σ → σ) (s : σ) :
    (modify f : EStateM ε σ PUnit).run' s = some PUnit.unit

items.name: EStateM.run'_modifyGet
items.statement:
theorem run'_modifyGet (f : σ → α × σ) (s : σ) :
    (modifyGet f : EStateM ε σ α).run' s = some (f s).1

items.name: EStateM.run_getModify
items.statement:
theorem run_getModify (f : σ → σ) :
    (getModify f : EStateM ε σ σ).run s = Result.ok s (f s)

items.name: EStateM.run'_getModify
items.statement:
theorem run'_getModify (f : σ → σ) (s : σ) :
    (getModify f : EStateM ε σ σ).run' s = some s

items.name: EStateM.run'_throw
items.statement:
theorem run'_throw (e : ε) (s : σ) :
    (throw e : EStateM ε σ α).run' s = none

items.name: EStateM.run_orElse
items.statement:
theorem run_orElse {δ} [h : Backtrackable δ σ] (x₁ x₂ : EStateM ε σ α) (s : σ) :
    (x₁ <|> x₂).run s = match x₁.run s with
    | .ok x s => .ok x s
    | .error _ s' => x₂.run (restore s' (save s))

items.name: EStateM.run'_orElse
items.statement:
theorem run'_orElse {δ} [h : Backtrackable δ σ] (x₁ x₂ : EStateM ε σ α) (s : σ) :
    (x₁ <|> x₂).run' s = match x₁.run s with
    | .ok x _ => some x
    | .error _ s' => x₂.run' (restore s' (save s))

items.name: EStateM.run_tryCatch
items.statement:
theorem run_tryCatch {δ} [h : Backtrackable δ σ]
    (body : EStateM ε σ α) (handler : ε → EStateM ε σ α) (s : σ) :
    (tryCatch body handler).run s = match body.run s with
    | .ok x s => .ok x s
    | .error e s' => (handler e).run (restore s' (save s))

items.name: EStateM.run'_tryCatch
items.statement:
theorem run'_tryCatch {δ} [h : Backtrackable δ σ]
    (body : EStateM ε σ α) (handler : ε → EStateM ε σ α) (s : σ) :
    (tryCatch body handler).run' s = match body.run s with
    | .ok x _ => some x
    | .error e s' => (handler e).run' (restore s' (save s))

items.name: EStateM.run'_adaptExcept
items.statement:
theorem run'_adaptExcept (f : ε → ε) (x : EStateM ε σ α) (s : σ) :
    (adaptExcept f x).run' s = x.run' s

items.name: EStateM.run_tryFinally'
items.statement:
theorem run_tryFinally' (x : EStateM ε σ α)
    (h : Option α → EStateM ε σ β) (s : σ) : (tryFinally' x h).run s = match x.run s with
    | .ok a s => match (h (some a)).run s with
      | .ok b s => Result.ok (a, b) s
      | .error e s => Result.error e s
    | .error e₁ s => match (h none).run s with
      | .ok _ s => Result.error e₁ s
      | .error e₂ s => Result.error e₂ s

items.name: EStateM.run'_tryFinally'
items.statement:
theorem run'_tryFinally' (x : EStateM ε σ α)
    (h : Option α → EStateM ε σ β) (s : σ) :
    (tryFinally' x h).run' s = match x.run s with
    | .ok a s => Option.map (a, ·) ((h (some a)).run' s)
    | .error _ _ => none

items.name: EStateM.run_fromStateM
items.statement:
theorem run_fromStateM (x : StateM σ α) (s : σ) :
    (fromStateM x : EStateM ε σ α).run s =
    Result.ok (x.run s).1 (x.run s).2

items.name: EStateM.run'_fromStateM
items.statement:
theorem run'_fromStateM (x : StateM σ α) (s : σ) :
    (fromStateM x : EStateM ε σ α).run' s = some (x.run' s)

items.name: EStateM.ext
items.statement: theorem ext {ε σ α} {x y : EStateM ε σ α} (h : ∀ s, x.run s = y.run s) : x = y

items.name: Lean.Meta.saturate1
items.doc:
`saturate1 goal tac` runs `tac` on `goal`, then on the resulting goals, etc.,
until `tac` does not apply to any goal any more (i.e. it returns `none`). The
order of applications is depth-first, so if `tac` generates goals `[g₁, g₂, ⋯]`,
we apply `tac` to `g₁` and recursively to all its subgoals before visiting `g₂`.
If `tac` does not apply to `goal`, `saturate1` returns `none`. Otherwise it
returns the generated subgoals to which `tac` did not apply. `saturate1`
respects the `MonadRecDepth` recursion limit.
items.statement:
partial def saturate1 [Monad m] [MonadError m] [MonadRecDepth m] [MonadLiftT (ST IO.RealWorld) m]
    (goal : MVarId) (tac : MVarId → m (Option (Array MVarId))) : m (Option (Array MVarId))

items.name: Lean.Position.getDeclsAfter
items.doc:
If `pos` is a `Lean.Position`, then `pos.getDeclsAfter` returns the array of names of declarations
whose selection range begins in position at least `pos`. By using the `selectionRange`, which is
usually smaller than the `range`, we err on the side of including declarations when possible.

By default, this only inspects the local branch of the environment. This is compatible with being
used to find declarations from the current command in a linter, where we have already waited for
async tasks/parallel branches to complete. Further, since the environment exposed to linters does
not include constants added after the elaboration of the current command, it is safe to use this on
the command's start position without picking up later declarations.
items.statement:
protected def Position.getDeclsAfter (env : Environment) (pos : Position)
    (asyncMode := EnvExtension.AsyncMode.local) : Array Name

items.name: String.Pos.Raw.getDeclsAfter
items.doc:
If `pos` is a `String.Pos.Raw`, then `pos.getDeclsAfter` returns the array of names of declarations
whose selection range begins in position at least `pos`. By using the `selectionRange`, which is
usually smaller than the `range`, we err on the side of including declarations when possible.

By default, this is intended for use in linters, where only the current environment branch needs to
be checked. See the docstring for `Lean.Position.getDeclsAfter` for details.
items.statement:
protected def _root_.String.Pos.Raw.getDeclsAfter (env : Environment) (map : FileMap)
    (pos : String.Pos.Raw) (asyncMode := EnvExtension.AsyncMode.local) : Array Name

items.name: Lean.findDeclarationSyntaxRange?
items.doc:
Yields the `Syntax.Range` for the declaration `decl` in the current file. If `decl` is not in
the current file, yields `none`.

By default, this provides the "selection range", which is usually the declaration's identifier or
e.g. the `instance` token for an unnamed instance. If `fullRange` is instead set to `true`, this
returns the full declaration range (which includes modifiers, such as the docstring).
items.statement:
def findDeclarationSyntaxRange? {m : Type → Type} [Monad m] [MonadEnv m] [MonadLiftT BaseIO m]
    [MonadFileMap m] (decl : Name) (fullRange := false) : m (Option Syntax.Range)

items.name: Lean.withDeclRef?
items.doc:
Runs `x` with a synthetic ref that has position info locating the given `decl` if it is defined
in the current file, or else runs `x` without modifying the ref. This is useful for logging on a
declaration's name from within linters.

By default, this uses the "selection range" of the declaration, which is usually the declaration's
identifier or e.g. the `instance` token for an unnamed instance. (This is also the place that
receives hovers for the declaration.)

If `fullRange` is instead set to `true`, this uses the full declaration range, which includes the
modifiers (such as the docstring, if there is one) and the body of the declaration.

`canonical` applies to the synthetic syntax generated for the ref; see `Syntax.ofRange`.
items.statement:
def withDeclRef? {α} {m : Type → Type} [Monad m] [MonadEnv m] [MonadLiftT BaseIO m]
    [MonadFileMap m] [MonadRef m] (decl : Name) (x : m α)
    (fullRange := false) (canonical := true) : m α

modules.title: The `alias` command
modules.doc:
The `alias` command is used to create synonyms. The plain command can create a synonym of any
declaration. There is also a version to create synonyms for the forward and reverse implications of
an iff theorem.

inductive AliasInfo where
  /-- Plain alias -/
  | plain (n : Name)
  /-- Forward direction of an iff alias -/
  | forward (n : Name)
  /-- Reverse direction of an iff alias -/

Also adds `case'` extensions.

The `patt` term is elaborated in the context where the inaccessibles have been renamed.

Returns the found goal, goals caused by elaborating `patt`, and the remaining goals.

modules.title: The `#do` command
modules.doc:
The `#do` command is like `run_cmd` but allows using variables from previous uses of `#do`.
Furthermore, `#do_meta` is like `#do` and shares its variable state while operating in `MetaM`.
Finally, `#clear_do` can be used to remove all variables from the current do state.

items.name: Batteries.Tactic.DoCommand.MonadStateStack
items.doc: The part of the `DoCommandExtensionState` used for monad state
items.statement:
structure MonadStateStack where
  /-- The meta state used for `#do_meta` -/
  metaState : Meta.State := {}
deriving Inhabited

items.name: Batteries.Tactic.DoCommand.DoCommandExtensionState
items.doc: The state for `#do`
items.statement:
structure DoCommandExtensionState where
  /--
  The current local context for `#do`.

  Invariant: `lctx` does not contain metavariables or level parameters or non-dependent `ldecl`s.
  -/
  lctx : LocalContext := {}
  /-- The local instances for `lctx` -/
  localInstances : LocalInstances := #[]
  /--
  The values associated to free variables in `lctx`.

  Invariant: every free variable in `lctx` has a corresponding value in `values`
  -/
  values : FVarIdMap NonScalar := {}
  /-- See `Lean.Elab.Do.Context.mutVars` -/
  mutVars : Array MutVar := #[]
  /-- See `Lean.Elab.Do.Context.mutVarDefs` -/
  mutVarDefs : Std.HashMap Name MutVar := {}
  /-- Monad state for use in e.g. `#do_meta` -/
  monadState : MonadStateStack := {}
deriving Inhabited

modules.title: The `generalize_proofs` tactic
modules.doc:
Generalize any proofs occurring in the goal or in chosen hypotheses,
replacing them by local hypotheses.
When these hypotheses are named, this makes it easy to refer to these proofs later in a proof,
commonly useful when dealing with functions like `Classical.choose` that produce data from proofs.
It is also useful to eliminate proof terms to handle issues with dependent types.

For example:
```lean
def List.nthLe {α} (l : List α) (n : ℕ) (_h : n < l.length) : α := sorry
example : List.nthLe [1, 2] 1 (by simp) = 2 := by
  -- ⊢ [1, 2].nthLe 1 ⋯ = 2
  generalize_proofs h
  -- h : 1 < [1, 2].length
  -- ⊢ [1, 2].nthLe 1 h = 2
```

The tactic is similar in spirit to `Lean.Meta.AbstractNestedProofs` in core.
One difference is that it the tactic tries to propagate expected types so that
we get `1 < [1, 2].length` in the above example rather than `1 < Nat.succ 1`.

items.name: Batteries.Tactic.GeneralizeProofs.Config
items.doc: Configuration for the `generalize_proofs` tactic.
items.statement:
structure Config where
  /-- The maximum recursion depth when generalizing proofs.
  When `maxDepth > 0`, then proofs are generalized from the types of the generalized proofs too. -/
  maxDepth : Nat := 8
  /-- When `abstract` is `true`, then the tactic will create universally quantified proofs
  to account for bound variables.
  When it is `false` then such proofs are left alone. -/
  abstract : Bool := true
  /-- (Debugging) When `true`, enables consistency checks. -/
  debug : Bool := false

items.name: Batteries.Tactic.GeneralizeProofs.GState
items.doc: State for the `MGen` monad.
items.statement:
structure GState where
  /-- Mapping from propositions to an fvar in the local context with that type. -/
  propToFVar : ExprMap Expr

items.name: Batteries.Tactic.GeneralizeProofs.MGen
items.doc:
Monad used to generalize proofs.
Carries `Mathlib.Tactic.GeneralizeProofs.Config` and `Mathlib.Tactic.GeneralizeProofs.State`.
items.statement: abbrev MGen

items.name: Batteries.Tactic.GeneralizeProofs.MGen.insertFVar
items.doc: Inserts a prop/fvar pair into the `propToFVar` map.
items.statement: def MGen.insertFVar (prop fvar : Expr) : MGen Unit

items.name: Batteries.Tactic.GeneralizeProofs.AContext
items.doc: Context for the `MAbs` monad.
items.statement:
structure AContext where
  /-- The local fvars corresponding to bound variables.
  Abstraction needs to be sure that these variables do not appear in abstracted terms. -/
  fvars : Array Expr := #[]
  /-- A copy of `propToFVar` from `GState`. -/
  propToFVar : ExprMap Expr
  /-- The recursion depth, for how many times `visit` is called from within `visitProof. -/
  depth : Nat := 0
  /-- The initial local context, for resetting when recursing. -/
  initLCtx : LocalContext
  /-- The tactic configuration. -/
  config : Config

items.name: Batteries.Tactic.GeneralizeProofs.AState
items.doc: State for the `MAbs` monad.
items.statement:
structure AState where
  /-- The prop/proof triples to add to the local context.
  The proofs must not refer to fvars in `fvars`. -/
  generalizations : Array (Expr × Expr) := #[]
  /-- Map version of `generalizations`. Use `MAbs.findProof?` and `MAbs.insertProof`. -/
  propToProof : ExprMap Expr := {}

items.name: Batteries.Tactic.GeneralizeProofs.MAbs
items.doc:
Monad used to abstract proofs, to prepare for generalization.
Has a cache (of expr/type? pairs),
and it also has a reader context `Mathlib/Tactic/GeneralizeProofs/AContext.lean`
and a state `Mathlib/Tactic/GeneralizeProofs/AState.lean`.
items.statement: abbrev MAbs

items.doc:
Does `mkLambdaFVars fvars e` but

2. only includes used fvars
